bugs.title: A seller can accept an introduction the buyer already withdrew, which charges the buyer 1T and opens the introduction against her will.
bugs.scenario: Buyer requests an intro (1T held), then withdraws it (status 'withdrawn', hold released). The seller - from a stale screen or a direct PUT /intros/{id}/accept - accepts it: 'withdrawn' is not in the settled list, the UPDATE flips it to accepted, the legacy branch inserts intro_deduct -1, and the relay or webhook then hands the two parties to each other. Correct result: 409, no charge, no reveal.
bugs.evidence:
_settled = (_row["status"] or "").strip().lower() in ("accepted", "declined", "expired")
"AND COALESCE(LOWER(status), 'pending') NOT IN ('accepted', 'declined', 'expired')"
bugs.fix: In accept_intro treat every non-pending status as settled: add 'withdrawn' to the tuple at line 9480 and change the UPDATE at 9555-9557 to "AND COALESCE(LOWER(status),'pending') = 'pending'". Make the same change in decline_intro (line 9772), which today rewrites a 'withdrawn' or 'expired' request to 'declined' and fires the decline webhook to the buyer.
bugs.lead: Lead read accept_intro: the settled list and the UPDATE both omit "withdrawn".
bugs.plain_title: A seller can still accept an introduction the buyer has withdrawn — the buyer is charged 1T and the two are introduced against her wish.
bugs.one_line_fix: Treat every status except 'pending' as closed in both accept and decline (add 'withdrawn' to the two checks).

bugs.title: One Paystack payment can be credited any number of times, because the once-only claim is keyed on the caller's reference text and not on the reference Paystack returns.
bugs.scenario: Pay once for 1T (ref ms_tuppence_abc), then call GET /payment/verify?reference=ms_tuppence_abc%23a, ...%23b, ...%3Fx%3D1 or ../verify/ms_tuppence_abc. payments.verify_payment pastes the text into the URL unencoded, so Paystack answers with the same successful transaction each time, while the LIKE check and _claim_payment_ref see a new string and credit again. The same hole is on /payment/seller-subscription/verify (re-applies a plan and collects a new monthly Tuppence grant each month) and on the wishlist verify at line 12950 (adds 30 days per call).
bugs.fix: In all three verify handlers refuse any reference that does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.=-]{1,100}$ before calling Paystack, url-quote it in payments.verify_payment (urllib.parse.quote(reference, safe='')), and use result['data']['reference'] - Paystack's own value - for the LIKE check, the _claim_payment_ref key and the ledger description.
bugs.lead: Lead read payments.py 96 and bea_main.py 9899-9925: the reference is pasted into the Paystack URL unencoded and the once-only key is the typed text.
bugs.plain_title: One Paystack payment can be credited again and again by re-sending its reference with '#a' or '?x=1' added.
bugs.one_line_fix: Accept only plain reference characters, URL-encode the reference, and key the once-only claim on the reference Paystack itself returns.

bugs.title: Pick labels are written into innerHTML unescaped (step trail, draft facts, draft title/body), and picks can be injected from the URL via ?resume=, giving DOM XSS on the trustsquare.co origin.
bugs.scenario:
Attacker sends https://trustsquare.co/quick/?resume="}]}>. Line 4666 stores it and sets _qResumeNow, the drawDoor wrapper auto-calls restore() 60 ms later, and the base drawStep builds the trail with ''+p.label+'' (a step >= flow length lands in drawDraft, which does the same for facts, the

title and the description), so the attacker's script runs on the main app's origin with the victim's session cookie and can call every same-origin API as them.
bugs.evidence:
return p.photo?'':''+p.label+''; }).join(''); (677; same at 1479 facts, 1556 '

'+title+'

'+c.draftBody(picks)+'

', and the CITY-OTHER-1 copy at src 4554) | var _w=JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(escape(atob(_b)))); if(_w && _w.picks){ ... window._qResumeNow=true; } (src 4666)
bugs.fix: Add one escape helper beside $() (function qEsc(t){return String(t==null?'':t).replace(/[&<>"']/g,function(c){return '&#'+c.charCodeAt(0)+';';});}) and wrap p.label at 677, 1479, the CITY-OTHER-1 trail copy, and title / c.draftBody(picks) at 1556 (and the 3571 innerHTML re-render). Also validate in the ?resume= reader: keep only picks whose label is a string of <=80 chars and whose photo is a key present in PH, and clamp step to the flow length.
bugs.lead: Lead probed it on the live site, 4 Oct: a crafted /quick/?resume= link put the lead's harmless test element into the page with no tap.
bugs.plain_title: A crafted Quick link (/quick/?resume=…) runs someone else's script in the visitor's browser on trustsquare.co, which can take over her account.
bugs.one_line_fix: Escape every label where it is painted, rebuild resumed answers from an allow-list, and never restore a ?resume= link without a tap.

bugs.title: Photo uploads are open to anyone holding the public app key and all unattached uploads share one AI budget ('photo-upload'), so a stranger - or a normal busy day - stops photo uploads for every seller
bugs.scenario: POST /listings/photo without listing_id needs only X-Api-Key (shipped in ms.js). Each call runs a paid vision scan billed to the literal user 'photo-upload', which has the same per-user daily ceiling as one person (default $0.50). The main sell flow uploads this way before the listing exists, so once that shared bucket is spent every seller gets 429 'You've reached today's AI usage limit' on new photos; a script reaches it in minutes and can go on to the platform ceiling. With a draft token the scan is billed to the draft's typed seller_email, so a stranger can also burn a named victim's daily AI allowance.
bugs.evidence:
_anon_who = "photo-upload"
...
if _r0 and _r0["seller_email"]:
    _anon_who = _r0["seller_email"]
...
img, _anon_note = _seller_photo_anon_gate(img, _gate_cat, _anon_who, is_primary=_gate_primary)
bugs.fix: Require a proven session (or a valid draft token / admin key) for every upload, bill the scan to _session_email(ts_user), add a per-IP hourly cap for token-only uploads (the _QP_IP_LOG pattern), and never meter anonymous uploads under one shared pseudo-user (give that lane its own, larger, separately-configured cap).
bugs.plain_title: Photo uploads are open to anyone with the public app key and share one AI budget, so one stranger — or one busy day — stops photo uploads for every seller.
bugs.one_line_fix: Require a signed-in session for uploads and count the AI budget per account, not in one shared pot.

bugs.title: A signed-in user can drain the whole daily platform AI budget through price-check web searches that are never charged and never counted against their own daily limit
bugs.scenario: A user holding 1T calls POST /listings/{id}/price-check?tier=1T on a Local Market or Collectors listing whose title finds fewer than 3 web comparables (their own oddly-titled listing works). Each call runs up to two OpenAI web-search calls (reason model, up to 120 s each), answers cannot_verify and charges nothing; the spend is logged under email '' so the $0.50 per-user ceiling never trips. Repeating it eats the $100 platform ceiling, after which every AI feature answers 429 for all users until 00:00 UTC.
bugs.evidence:
_check_cost_ceiling("")   # platform daily rail, like every AI lane
_log_ai_spend("", "/listings/price-check#web-comps", "reason", _it, _ot, provider="openai", model=model)
bugs.fix: Pass the caller's email through _fair_price_resolve into _web_comps_band and use it in _check_cost_ceiling(email) and _log_ai_spend(email, ...). Add a per-user daily cap on uncharged checks (for example 5) and cache a no-result outcome per listing for a few hours so the same listing cannot trigger the search again.
bugs.plain_title: A signed-in user can use up the platform's whole daily AI budget through price-check web searches that are never charged or counted.
bugs.one_line_fix: Bill and count the web search against the caller, with a small daily cap on unpaid checks.

bugs.title: publish_listing turns ANY non-live status into live, so a seller whose adverts were blocked (EULA 14.5) or withdrawn re-publishes them herself
bugs.scenario: Staff or the B3 sweep set a seller's adverts to listing_status='blocked' (reinstatement is meant to be a staff act after a 60-day cooling-off). The seller calls PUT /listings/{id}/publish on her own blocked (or archived/paused/faded/resting) advert: the only status test is 'already live', blocked rows are not counted by the slot guard, and the UPDATE sets listing_status='live'. The block is undone with one request.
bugs.evidence:
current_status = existing["listing_status"] or "draft"
if current_status == "live":
...
"""UPDATE listings
   SET listing_status = 'live',
bugs.fix: In publish_listing, after the ownership check, allow the transition only from 'draft' (and whichever seller-owned states are meant to be re-openable, e.g. 'resting'/'faded'); answer 403/409 for 'blocked' and 'archived', and refuse to publish ANY draft while the seller has a blocked advert (SELECT 1 FROM listings WHERE LOWER(seller_email)=? AND listing_status='blocked').
bugs.lead: Lead read publish_listing: the only status test is "already live".
bugs.plain_title: A seller whose advert was blocked or withdrawn can put it back live herself with one publish request.
bugs.one_line_fix: Let publish act only on drafts and the seller's own paused adverts; refuse blocked, withdrawn and archived ones.

bugs.title: _LEGAL_SIGNALS holds two ids that do not exist and omits three go-live gate signals, so those legal credentials are auto-earned by any upload
bugs.scenario: The catalogue ids are category.travel.asata_member and category.service.trade_licence, but the set lists 'category.travel.asata' and 'category.services.trade_licence'. An agent uploads any file naming category.service.trade_licence: it is 'earned' at once (+12) and estate_agents._go_live_gaps treats the gate credential as verified, so the profile can go live unchecked. category.collector.shg_registered, category.institution.clearances and category.placement.del_registered (also gate_signals) are missing altogether.
bugs.evidence:
"category.travel.asata",
    "category.services.trade_licence",
bugs.fix: Correct the two ids and add every VERTICALS[*]['gate_signal'] from estate_agents.py; best, build the set from that table plus the stranger-gate signal tuples so it cannot drift again.
bugs.plain_title: The list of legal credentials has two misspelt ids and misses three go-live signals, so those credentials are earned by uploading any file.
bugs.one_line_fix: Correct the two ids, add the three missing signals, and build the list from the go-live gate's own list so they cannot drift apart.

bugs.title: The bank-name, payment-name and certificate-name checks can never run for a seller, because nothing a seller can reach writes users.id_name.
bugs.scenario: A seller verifies her ID in the app (POST /users/{email}/verify-identity-npr, which writes only id_npr_verified_at) and taps 'Check the name'. verify_bank_name reads users.id_name, which is written only by the admin-only /users/{email}/verify-identity (line 16741), so she is told 'Verify your ID first' every time; _payment_name_check (16877) and the certificate name check (16143) return early the same way. The three credentials shipped on 27 Sep (7 points) are unreachable.
bugs.fix: Store the confirmed name on the seller-reachable path: in verify_identity_npr, when res.verified, also SET id_name = payload.full_name.strip() (the name the register confirmed) in the UPDATE at line 9255.
bugs.plain_title: The bank-name, payment-name and certificate-name checks can never run, because nothing a seller can do stores her ID name.
bugs.one_line_fix: Store the confirmed name when the Home Affairs ID check passes.

bugs.title: Emailed sign-in links are refused after 72 hours although they are minted and advertised for 7 days, and outreach console links minted for 14-30 days die on day 3.
bugs.scenario: A user opens the 'Sign in' button from a sign-in email on day 4 (the email says 'the button works for 7 days', SIGNIN-LINK-7D of 3 Oct), or an agency prospect opens the wave-prep console link (link_days default 14) after 3 days. /auth/verify decodes the token fine but the hard-coded 72-hour iat check answers 401 'This sign-in link is too old'. The 3 Oct ruling changed the token expiry and the email text but not this check.
bugs.fix: Delete the separate 72-hour check and let the token's own exp decide (or replace 72*3600 with the minting lifetime carried in the token). At the same time keep used_signin_links rows for at least the longest link life (30 days, not 8) so a used 14-30 day link cannot become usable again after the purge at 20356.
bugs.lead: Lead read bea_main.py 20344: a hard-coded 72-hour test, against the 7-day promise of 3 Oct.
bugs.plain_title: Emailed sign-in links stop working after 72 hours although the email promises 7 days, and agency console links made for 14–30 days die on day 3.
bugs.one_line_fix: Remove the hard-coded 72-hour test and rely on the link's own expiry date.

bugs.title: Every internal-comps query filters on a column the listings table does not have, so the 1T 'Verified comps' tier never appears and the error is swallowed
bugs.scenario: _comp_count and _comp_amounts test COALESCE(status,'active'), but the listings lifecycle column is listing_status and no code creates a 'status' column. SQLite raises 'no such column: status', the except blocks return 0 / [], so comp_count is always 0: Cars listings get no fair-price chip at all, Property never offers the 1T comps tier, and yield never offers 'Verified yield'. Nothing is logged, so the feature has looked merely 'not enough comps yet'.
bugs.fix: In _comp_count (line 24611) and both queries of _comp_amounts (24857, 24862) replace the status test with COALESCE(listing_status,'live')='live', and log the exception instead of returning 0/[] silently. Ship it together with the comparables filter in the next finding.
bugs.plain_title: The 1T 'Verified comps' price tier never appears, because its query asks for a column the listings table does not have and the error is hidden.
bugs.one_line_fix: Test listing_status (empty counts as live) in the three comps queries and log the error instead of hiding it.

bugs.title: The agent go-live gate is checked only at publish time: a live profile can switch vertical (car dealer becomes a live 'Tutor' with no child-safety clearance) and stays live
bugs.scenario: An agent earns the MIRA gate, publishes under 'cars', then POSTs /agents/profile with vertical='institution': _upsert_profile changes vertical and leaves profile_status='live', so /agents/nearby?vertical=institution lists them as a live Tutor (reproduced). The same hole keeps a profile live after ops later rejects or the annual FFC lapses.
bugs.evidence: agency_id=COALESCE(?, agency_id), vertical=COALESCE(NULLIF(?,''), vertical), updated_at=?
bugs.fix: In _upsert_profile set profile_status='draft' whenever vertical changes on an existing profile; in _rank_agents and request_agent_intro skip any profile whose _go_live_gaps() is non-empty.
bugs.plain_title: A live agent can change vertical after going live — a car dealer becomes a live 'Tutor' with no child-safety clearance.
bugs.one_line_fix: Re-run the go-live gate whenever the vertical changes and take the profile off live until it passes.

bugs.title: A document uploaded from any non-Local-Market listing is filed under a Local Market signal and then filtered out of that listing's own document list.
bugs.scenario: A tutor opens Edit Listing, picks 'Certificate / Diploma', leaves the credential selector on 'general' and uploads. With no signal_id the server takes category.lm.formal_cert from _DOC_TYPE_SIGNAL_CHAINS (Local Market only), and the refreshed GET /users/{email}/documents?category=Tutors keeps only category.tutors.*, universal.*, track_record.* or NULL. The upload succeeds but the list still says 'No documents uploaded yet', and the earned credential counts for Local Market, not Tutors; the same happens for Services, Adventures, Collectors, Cars and Property and for the default 'ID / Passport' type.
bugs.evidence:
effective_signal = signal_id or _next_signal_for_doc(doc_type, conn_pre, email)
...
                   signal_id IS NULL
                   OR signal_id LIKE ?
bugs.fix: In list_seller_documents add "OR signal_id LIKE 'category.lm.%'" to the filtered query so generic doc-type uploads always show; and in upload_seller_document only use _next_signal_for_doc when the seller's listing category is Local Market (send the category with the upload), otherwise store signal_id NULL.
bugs.plain_title: A document uploaded from any advert that is not Local Market is filed under a Local Market signal and disappears from that advert's own document list.
bugs.one_line_fix: Use the Local Market signal chain only for Local Market adverts and always list generic uploads.

bugs.title: Inviting an address into an agency immediately rewrites that existing user's slot limit and tier, and treats them as a member before they ever accept.
bugs.scenario: An agency admin invites the email of any existing account (a paying Pro seller with 30 slots, a member of another verified agency, a superuser with 500). Line 20657 overwrites users.slot_limit with 1..20 unconditionally, and _sync_agency_member_tiers (20663) moves a free/starter/agency user to this agency's tier (a verified agency's agent invited by an unverified one drops to 'starter'). Status 'invited' already counts as membership, so the agency can then import drafts into that person's account and re-tier them via the PUT route. The bulk lane was hardened against exactly this on 24 Sep (estate_agents.py 792-800); the single-invite lane was not. The route also sends an invite email per call with no rate limit.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email) VALUES (?)", (email,))
...
        conn.execute("UPDATE users SET slot_limit=? WHERE LOWER(email)=?", (cap, email))   # 20657
        _sync_agency_member_tiers(conn, agency_id)   # 20663
bugs.fix: Mirror the bulk lane: only provision slot_limit when the user row was created by this invite or is already an active member of THIS agency, and only when the current tier is free/starter. Apply caps, tier sync, rollups and import matching to status='active' members only (the invitee's own sign-in is the consent). Add a per-agency/per-IP invite budget before _mint_agent_invite.
bugs.plain_title: Inviting someone into an agency changes that person's plan and slot limit at once, before they accept.
bugs.one_line_fix: Apply the plan and slot change only when the invited person accepts.

bugs.title: The gate blanks photo_urls to '' in every JSON answer (suspicion b CONFIRMED - it is the CONTENT-GATE url filter, not the private-field stripping)
bugs.scenario: listings.photo_urls is stored and returned as a JSON-array STRING ('["https://...","https://..."]', bea_main.py:7317, 11489). 'photo_urls' is in _URL_KEYS, and _url_field() treats any string that is not one single https link as bad and returns ''. So every listing answer (admins included) carries photo_urls:'' - Coach-published and Local Market adverts, which keep their gallery ONLY in photo_urls, show one cover photo (ms.js:423, 17662). Worse: the edit screen then loads one photo (ms.js:12753-12773) and Save writes photo_urls=[cover] back (ms.js:13791) - the other photos are permanently dropped. Run against the module: _encode({'id':1,'photo_urls':'["https://a/1.jpg","https://a/2.jpg"]'}) -> photo_urls ''. Same for 'photos'/'images' sent as a string, and for any http:// or relative 'media/x.jpg' value.
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:598-599  _URL_KEYS = frozenset({... "photos", "photo_urls", "images"})  ||  security_gate.py:633-634  if isinstance(v, str):\n        return v if (not v or _URL_OK.match(v)) else ""
bugs.fix: In _url_field(): when v is a str starting with '[', json.loads it, keep the items that pass _URL_OK, and return json.dumps(kept) (same string shape the app expects); only a plain single-link string is tested against _URL_OK directly. Add a regression test with a real listing row.
bugs.lead: Lead read security_gate.py 598-637: a photo_urls value that is a JSON-array STRING fails the URL test and is returned as an empty string; a real list passes.
bugs.plain_title: The security gate empties any photo list that a handler returns as text instead of a list, so the gallery collapses to one photo (Local Market detail does this).
bugs.one_line_fix: Decode a JSON-text photo list in the gate before testing each link, and return photo_urls as a real list everywhere.

bugs.title: restore_on_return() can credit the same retained balance several times when called concurrently (read-then-write with no claim)
bugs.scenario: A member closes his account with N Tuppence retained, signs in again, and fires several POST /users at once, each with a different upper/lower-case spelling of his own address (the gate does not rewrite a same-address spelling and users.email is case-sensitive UNIQUE, so each insert is 'new' and reaches restore_on_return). Every thread reads the same unrestored account_closures row before any commits, then each inserts its own +N 'closure_restore' row. He can close again with the multiplied balance and repeat.
bugs.evidence: account_closure.py:167  row, match = find_restorable(conn, email, id_number_hash)  ||  account_closure.py:173-176  conn.execute("INSERT INTO transactions ... (email, \"closure_restore\", amount, ...))  ||  account_closure.py:177-179  "UPDATE account_closures SET restored_at=?, ... WHERE id=?"
bugs.fix: Claim before crediting: run UPDATE account_closures SET restored_at=?, restored_to_email=?, restore_match=? WHERE id=? AND restored_at IS NULL first, and return None unless cursor.rowcount == 1; only then insert the closure_restore row and commit (or wrap the function in BEGIN IMMEDIATE).
bugs.plain_title: Tuppence kept back at account closure can be credited several times if two requests arrive together.
bugs.one_line_fix: Claim the restore with a single marker row inside the same transaction before crediting.

bugs.title: A paid seller plan never ends when its 30-day period runs out: the only expiry worker acts on explicitly requested downgrades
bugs.scenario: A seller pays R90 (Starter) or R360 (Pro) once; verify sets seller_tier and billing_period_end = paid_at + 30 days. The Paystack charge is one-off (no plan, no renewal webhook) and nothing lowers seller_tier when billing_period_end passes, so she keeps 10/30 slots, global reach and Squire for good unless she cancels herself. _buyer_reach_tier (line 3908) even selects billing_period_end and never reads it.
bugs.evidence:
"SELECT email, pending_downgrade_tier FROM users "
"WHERE pending_downgrade_tier IS NOT NULL "
"AND billing_period_end <= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP"
bugs.fix: In _apply_pending_downgrades also select users whose seller_tier is starter/pro, pending_downgrade_tier IS NULL and billing_period_end has passed (plus a grace period if wanted) and lower them to free through the same UPDATE + _plan_changed(conn, email, 'free', lowered=True); leave agency-seat and superuser accounts out.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: A paid seller plan never ends: nothing takes Starter or Pro back when the paid 30 days are over.
bugs.one_line_fix: Add a daily job that returns a plan to Free when its paid period ends without renewal.

bugs.title: Deleting a listing orphans its pending introduction requests, so the buyer's held Tuppence is never released
bugs.scenario: A buyer asks for an introduction (1T held, intro_requests.tuppence_held=1). The seller deletes the advert through DELETE /listings/{id}/seller (or staff through DELETE /listings/{id}). The intro row stays 'pending', and the expiry sweep that releases holds reads `intro_requests ir JOIN listings l ON l.id = ir.listing_id`, so an intro whose listing is gone is never expired and _release_intro_hold never runs. The buyer loses 1T unless she finds and withdraws the request herself.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("DELETE FROM listings WHERE id = ?", (listing_id,))
conn.execute("DELETE FROM listing_cities WHERE listing_id = ?", (listing_id,))
conn.execute("DELETE FROM wishlist_matches WHERE listing_id = ?", (listing_id,))
bugs.fix: In both delete handlers, before the DELETE and in the same transaction: for every intro_requests row of this listing with status='pending', set status='expired' (or 'cancelled') and call _release_intro_hold(conn, id, 'listing removed by seller'); tell the buyer. Alternatively archive instead of deleting when intros exist.
bugs.plain_title: Deleting an advert leaves its pending introduction requests behind, so the buyer's held Tuppence is never released.
bugs.one_line_fix: Release each pending request's held Tuppence in the same transaction that deletes the advert.

bugs.title: POST /users only acts when its INSERT creates the row, but sign-in (and account closure) always leave a row first - so retained Tuppence is never restored to a returning member, and the name and free AI sessions are dropped
bugs.scenario: The route now needs a session (USERS-BIND-1), and _establish_user_session already ran `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email)`; close_account() also keeps the row (closed_at). So for every real caller `is_new` is False: account_closure.restore_on_return (its only caller) never runs and a member who closed with a balance and comes back never gets her Tuppence (EULA 14.1/14.3); the name sent by the sell flow is ignored by INSERT OR IGNORE; the +3 AI sessions and the Brevo sign-up suppression never happen.
bugs.evidence:
result = conn.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?,?)", (user.email, user.name))
is_new = result.rowcount > 0
...
if is_new:
    ... restored = account_closure.restore_on_return(conn, user.email, _idh)
bugs.fix: Stop keying on rowcount. Always run restore_on_return (it is idempotent via restored_at) - best placed in _establish_user_session so every sign-in of a returning address restores and clears closed_at; set the name with `UPDATE users SET name=? WHERE email=? AND (name IS NULL OR TRIM(name)='')`; grant the free sessions on a dedicated once-only flag (e.g. welcome_credit_at IS NULL) instead of 'row was just created'.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: Tuppence kept back at account closure is never given back to a returning member, because the restore only runs for a brand-new account row.
bugs.one_line_fix: Run the restore whenever a returning person signs in, not only when a new row is created.

bugs.title: An introduction request from a buyer whose typed email has a capital letter is refused with 402 although she has Tuppence, because the wallet is read by the typed spelling.
bugs.scenario: A signed-in buyer's intro form holds 'Thandi@Gmail.com' (ms.js 7165 sends the box value un-lowercased). The gate rewrites buyer_email only when it differs from the session after lower-casing, so the handler keeps the typed spelling; the balance query is an exact match, finds 0, and she gets 402 and a top-up prompt - again after topping up. The canonical email that _bind_charged_email returns at line 8848 is thrown away.
bugs.evidence:
_bind_charged_email(intro.buyer_email, ts_user, "create-intro")   # ACCOUNT-BIND-1
"SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) AS bal FROM transactions WHERE user_email = ?",
(intro.buyer_email,)).fetchone()["bal"]
bugs.fix: At the top of create_intro set intro.buyer_email = (_session_email(ts_user) or intro.buyer_email or '').strip().lower() and use that one value for the terms check, duplicate check, balance read, intro row and hold row. Root cause: in security_gate.py lines 396-413 write the session email into a bound parameter whenever the raw value is not already exactly the session email (compare str(v), not _norm(v)).
bugs.plain_title: A buyer who types her email with a capital letter is told she has no Tuppence although she has.
bugs.one_line_fix: Lower-case and trim the email in the gate's rewrite and read every wallet by LOWER(email).

bugs.title: An agency admin can give any member (or themselves) a paid Pro seat and any slot limit without paying, by sending seat_paid / listing_cap to PUT /agencies/{id}/agents/{email}.
bugs.scenario: The route is level 'user' + own-agency, so every agency admin (including unverified outreach agencies created by wave-prep) passes. Sending {"seat_paid": true} sets users.seller_tier='pro' and slot_limit=20 with no payment; {"listing_cap": 100000} or -1 is written unclamped into users.slot_limit (negative blocks the member from publishing). The console itself says a Pro seat is 'earned via the agent's own subscription - the console never grants one' (ms.js 2323), and the old agencySeat() caller still exists.
bugs.evidence:
if req.seat_paid is not None:
            paid = 1 if req.seat_paid else 0
            cap = 20 if paid else 10
        if req.listing_cap is not None:
            cap = int(req.listing_cap)
...
            conn.execute("UPDATE users SET slot_limit=?, seller_tier=? WHERE LOWER(email)=?", (cap, ('pro' if paid else 'starter'), email))
bugs.fix: Accept seat_paid only when the caller presents X-Admin-Key (ops, after a recorded payment); ignore/refuse it for a session caller. Clamp listing_cap exactly as invite_agent does (max(1, min(cap, 20))), require status != 'removed', and never write seller_tier here for a session caller (leave tier to _sync_agency_member_tiers).
bugs.lead: Lead read bea_main.py 20693-20702. This breaks ruling RUL-048 (23 Aug 2026): "A Pro seat is earned through the subscription flow - never a console value flip".
bugs.plain_title: An agency admin can give any member a paid Pro seat and any slot limit without paying — against ruling RUL-048.
bugs.one_line_fix: Remove seat_paid and listing_cap from what the console may send; set them only from the subscription flow.

bugs.title: The monthly 'non-rolling' sweep removes Tuppence the member BOUGHT: it takes min(balance, last grant) without subtracting what she already spent
bugs.scenario: Pro seller: September grant 10T. She spends 12T on introductions and buys 10T (balance 8T, all of it purchased, since the grant is spent first). On her October payment grant_monthly_tuppence() computes sweep = min(8, 10) = 8 and writes a -8T 'grant_expiry' row: 8 purchased Tuppence are deleted. The function's own comment says purchased Tuppence is never touched. Only runs when TUPPENCE_MONTHLY_ENABLED=1.
bugs.evidence: launch_redemption.py:268  _sweep = min(_balance, _prev_grant)  ||  launch_redemption.py:272  (email, "grant_expiry", -_sweep,
bugs.fix: Sweep only the unspent part of the previous grant: spent = -SUM(amount) of that member's negative non-grant_expiry rows created since the previous grant's granted_at; unspent = max(0, prev_grant - spent); sweep = min(balance, unspent).
bugs.plain_title: The monthly sweep of unused free Tuppence can also remove Tuppence the member bought.
bugs.one_line_fix: Sweep only what is left of the free grant: the grant minus what was spent since it was given.

bugs.title: Webhook signatures are checked against PAYSTACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET, a value Paystack does not issue - unless that variable was hand-set to the secret key, every webhook is refused and the 'reliable' credit path is dead
bugs.scenario: Paystack signs each webhook with the account SECRET KEY (HMAC-SHA512); its dashboard has no separate 'Webhook Secret' (the docstring at bea_main.py:9984 tells the operator to copy one). With the variable unset, verify_webhook_signature() returns False, the route answers 400 and nothing is credited. A buyer who pays and closes the tab before the browser returns to /payment/verify has paid and gets no Tuppence. It is also read with a bare os.getenv, which the code's own ENVKEY-1 note (bea_main.py:8566) says is empty on the server for keys kept only in .env.
bugs.evidence: payments.py:133-135  secret = os.getenv("PAYSTACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET", "")\n    if not secret:\n        return False
bugs.fix: Use the secret key: secret = os.getenv('PAYSTACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET') or ai_provider.envkey('PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY'); correct the docstring at bea_main.py:9982-9984; guard compare_digest against a non-ASCII header (encode both sides to bytes). Then send a test event from the Paystack dashboard and confirm a 200.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: Payment webhooks are checked against a secret Paystack does not issue, so unless that setting was hand-filled with the secret key every webhook is refused.
bugs.one_line_fix: Verify webhook signatures with the Paystack secret key and fail loudly at start-up if it is missing.

bugs.title: The public GET /zoom/next hands out the private street address of Property and Services listings as a 'street' chip
bugs.scenario: Zoom's geography goes down to street level for Property and Services and reads the private street_address column (zoom_engine.py line 302). An anonymous call such as /zoom/next?category=Property&city=Pretoria&q=<two words from an advert's title>, or f=geo_suburb:<a suburb with one advert>, narrows to one listing and the answer carries {"facet":"geo_street","v":"Flat 7 Duncan Court, 1090 Prospect St"} in auto/chips beside that listing's id. Only a house number at the very start is dropped; the gate hides the key street_address, not a value under 'v'/'label'. Confirmed by running zoom_engine.next_step on sample rows. The route has no flag check, so it is reachable now even though the app only calls it when baseline_q4 is armed.
bugs.fix: Remove the 'street' level from GEO_LEVELS for Property and Services in zoom_engine.py, and in _zoom_candidates drop street_address from every row before it reaches the engine (r.pop('street_address', None)); apply the same to the two Squire callers (lines 30351 and 30438). While there, run _scrub_vehicle_specs on the rows first so unconfirmed car specs are not offered as facet values either.
bugs.lead: Lead read zoom_engine.py 292-309. Live probe 4 Oct on Property/Pretoria returned no street choices, so no address is leaking there today; it starts the day an advert with a street address enters the funnel. Lead lowered this from Critical to High for that reason. The same public answer does carry listing_lat / listing_lng.
bugs.plain_title: The public search funnel (/zoom/next) can offer an advert's private street as a 'Which street?' choice, and its answers already carry each advert's map coordinates.
bugs.one_line_fix: Remove the street level from the funnel and drop street_address and exact coordinates from the rows before they reach the engine.

bugs.title: The seller's read of a request she has not accepted still carries the buyer's full typed name and her unchecked message.
bugs.scenario: A buyer asks for an introduction as 'Thandi Mokoena' with the message 'call me on 082 555 1234'. GET /intros and GET /intros/{listing_id} blank only buyer_email for the seller; buyer_name and message go out as stored, and ms.js 19043-19052 shows both on the pending card. The seller knows who the buyer is - and can phone her and decline, so no Tuppence is burned - before she accepts.
bugs.evidence:
if v and (d.get("buyer_email") or "").strip().lower() != v and (d.get("status") or "pending") != "accepted":
    d["buyer_email"] = ""
bugs.fix: In _intro_for_viewer, in the same branch, also set d['buyer_name'] to its first word (as ms.js 752 already does) and pass d['message'] through _anon_regex_clean; in create_intro run intro.message through _private_text_scrub before the INSERT at line 8923 so contact details are never stored for a pending request.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: Before she accepts, the seller already receives the buyer's full typed name and unchecked message.
bugs.one_line_fix: Send only a first name or alias and run the message through the contact scrub until both have accepted.

bugs.title: Seller profile tags are saved without the contact scrub and then shown to every buyer.
bugs.scenario: A seller saves a profile tag such as 'WhatsApp 082 555 1234' or 'me@shop.co.za'. Only headline and about are scrubbed; tags are stored as typed and the public route GET /sellers/summary/{listing_id} (line 5688) returns headline, about and tags to any stranger. The seller's contact is public with no introduction.
bugs.evidence:
cur["tags"] = [_plain_text(str(t))[:40] for t in (fields["tags"] or [])][:20]
cur["headline"], cur["about"], _h = _private_text_scrub(cur.get("headline", ""), cur.get("about", ""), me, "profile")
bugs.fix: Pass every tag (and region) through _anon_regex_clean before storing, dropping tags that become empty; apply the same scrub when /sellers/summary reads old rows.
bugs.plain_title: Seller profile tags are saved without the contact scrub and shown to every buyer.
bugs.one_line_fix: Run the tags through the same contact scrub as descriptions before saving.

bugs.title: Squire lets a buyer and a seller swap free text both ways with no contact scrub, before any introduction.
bugs.scenario: A Pro buyer adds 'call me on 082 555 1234' to an approach (ms.js sends the typed extra as text) and the seller reads it in /squire/inbox; the seller's answer (also free text) comes back on the shortlist. Both sides have each other's contact details with no introduction accepted and no Tuppence paid. Dark until baseline_q4 is armed, live the moment it is.
bugs.evidence:
text = (body.text or b["brief_text"] or b["need_text"] or "").strip()
text = _squire_minimise(text, bool(b["is_minor"]))[:1200]
((body.answer or "").strip()[:1200], _squire_now(), approach_id))
bugs.fix: Run _plain_text + _anon_regex_clean (the advert scrub) over the approach text (31055-31061), the brief answers (30984), need_text at brief creation (30430) and the seller's answer (31112) before they are stored; refuse or strip when a hit is found.
bugs.plain_title: Squire lets a buyer and a seller exchange free text both ways with no contact scrub, before any introduction.
bugs.one_line_fix: Run Squire's two free-text fields through the contact scrub in both directions.

bugs.title: The photo migration reads whatever path a listing's thumb_url names, so a listing with thumb_url '/media/../.env' makes it copy the server's secrets file to public storage.
bugs.scenario: POST /listings (public level, app key) stores the caller's thumb_url and medium_url unchecked (line 4210). An attacker creates a listing with thumb_url '/media/../.env' or '/media/../marketsquare.db'. When an admin next runs POST /admin/migrate-photos the handler opens /var/www/marketsquare/media/../.env, uploads it to the public bucket and its /media mirror, and writes the new public URL onto the attacker's own listing.
bugs.evidence:
thumb_local = f"/var/www/marketsquare{thumb_path}"
with open(thumb_local, "rb") as fh:
    thumb_data = fh.read()
bugs.fix: In migrate_photos resolve the path and skip the row unless os.path.realpath(local).startswith('/var/www/marketsquare/media/') and the file opens as an image with PIL; in create_listing (and the listing edit route) refuse a client thumb_url/medium_url that is not an https URL on the storage domain or a plain /media/<name> with no '..'.
bugs.plain_title: The photo migration copies whatever file path an advert's thumbnail names, so a crafted path could copy the server's secrets file to public storage.
bugs.one_line_fix: Resolve the path and refuse anything outside the media folder.

bugs.title: Document upload lets the seller name any category.* signal, so verification-result signals are self-awarded and the stranger gate opens without an ID check
bugs.scenario: A housekeeper posts any JPEG to POST /users/{email}/documents with doc_type=other and signal_id=category.lm.id_ai_verified. The only check is the 'category.' prefix, the signal is neither an ID doc nor in _LEGAL_SIGNALS, so it is written 'earned'; that id is in _GATE_ID_SIGNALS, so her advert becomes visible to strangers with no ID check (RUL-115). id_admin_verified, cert_name_verified, bank/payment_name_verified, claim_only FIDE titles and 'system tracked' tx_* signals can be self-awarded the same way.
bugs.evidence:
if signal_id and not str(signal_id).startswith("category."):
        signal_id = None        (16116: initial_status = "earned")
bugs.fix: Accept a client-named signal only when it exists in _CATEGORY_SIGNALS, is not claim_only, has evidence_required != False and is not a verification-result signal (id_ai_verified, id_admin_verified, cert_name_verified, *_name_verified, tx_*); otherwise ignore it and fall back to the doc_type chain. (The handler starts at 15994 and runs past 16000 - overlaps the next slice.)
bugs.lead: Lead read bea_main.py 16075: the only test on a client-named signal is the "category." prefix.
bugs.plain_title: A seller can award herself identity-verified and other checked credentials by naming them when uploading any document.
bugs.one_line_fix: Accept a client-named signal only from a short allow-list of upload-earnable signals, never a verification result.

bugs.title: AI answers are returned as raw strings and the app paints them as HTML, so a seller's listing text can run script in a buyer's browser
bugs.scenario: A seller writes a description that tells the model to put an tag in its answer. A buyer pays 1T for the price check; the model's sa_context/assessment come back unescaped and ms.js writes them with innerHTML (ms.js 6363 tvsCard body, 6576, 6595), so the script runs signed in as the buyer. The security gate's text cleaning does not cover these keys (the answer has no 'id' and the keys are not in _TEXT_KEYS). Same pattern: market_context (yield-calc), new_title/new_description, actions[].step/reason, and the web-comps site names inside official_context.
bugs.fix: Run every model-derived string through _plain_text() before returning it (price-check: verdict, sa_context, sa_range, assessment, local_vs_global; yield-calc: market_context, sa_yield_benchmark; ai-rewrite: new_title, new_description; ai-audit: step, reason; batch-cards drafts; _web_comps_band: title and site). Whitelist verdict/local_vs_global to their allowed values. In ms.js render these fields with textContent or an escape helper.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: AI answers are painted as HTML, so a seller can word an advert to make the AI write script that runs in a buyer's browser.
bugs.one_line_fix: Escape AI text before painting it, or render it as plain text with line breaks.

bugs.title: The anonymous support form makes TrustSquare Support send an email with an attacker-written subject (and an AI-written body) to any address typed into it
bugs.scenario: A stranger posts /support/message with a victim's address and a first line such as 'Your payout is on hold - confirm at example.co/pay'. The address is never proven, yet _support_followup mails that address from support@mail.trustsquare.co with subject 'Re: [TS-0412] <that line>'; with EMAIL_AUTO_SEND=1 the body is the model's reply to the attacker's own text. The 5-per-hour cap is per exact address (victim+1@, victim+2@ pass) and the IP limit allows 20 per 10 minutes. /app/fault was fixed for exactly this on 24 Sep (ACK only to a proven address); this door was not.
bugs.evidence:
handled = await _triage_message(
    email, "support@trustsquare.co", _support_subject(ref, title), message,
    ref_override=ref, source="support-form")
bugs.fix: For an address that is not the signed-in session's own, send a fixed acknowledgement only: subject 'TrustSquare <ref> - we have your message' with no user text, and never the AI draft (store the draft for the admin queue). Count the hourly cap on the address with the +tag and dots removed, and add a per-IP daily cap on distinct recipient addresses.
bugs.plain_title: The public support form makes TrustSquare Support send an email with a stranger-written subject to any address.
bugs.one_line_fix: For an address that is not the signed-in user's own, send only a fixed acknowledgement with no user-written text.

bugs.title: Agent lead inbox returns the seller's listing fields un-neutralised, giving a seller stored script execution in the agent's session
bugs.scenario: A seller creates a listing whose suburb (or price) is '' (POST /listings cleans only title and description), then requests an agent intro with that listing_id. The inbox nests the listing in a dict with no 'id', so the gate's plain-text pass skips it (verified: message is cleaned, listing.suburb/price are not), and ms.js 22904-22906 writes l.suburb / l.price into innerHTML: the script runs as the agent and can accept leads on the agent's Tuppence.
bugs.fix: Select id as well (SELECT id, title, ...) so security_gate._encode treats the nested listing as a record, or strip markup in the handler; and escape l.title/l.suburb/l.city/l.price/x.message in ms.js _asLeadsLoad.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: The agent lead inbox shows the seller's advert fields without cleaning, so a seller can run script in an agent's session.
bugs.one_line_fix: Clean the nested advert fields in the gate's output filter and escape them where the Agent Hub paints them.

bugs.title: Both photo-upload handlers are `async def` but run Pillow, the blocking vision-AI call and the S3 write inline, freezing the whole event loop for every user during each upload
bugs.scenario: A seller uploads 8 photos. For each one upload_listing_photo decodes and resizes the image, calls _seller_photo_anon_gate -> ai_provider.complete (a synchronous httpx.Client call, repeated when the blur-verify loop runs) and _s3_upload, all on the event-loop thread. While that runs the worker answers nothing else - browsing, sign-in, payments all hang for seconds per photo. Anyone with the public key can keep the API frozen by posting photos (or a 13000x13000 'small' PNG) in a loop.
bugs.evidence:
@app.post("/listings/photo")
async def upload_listing_photo(
...
    img, _anon_note = _seller_photo_anon_gate(img, _gate_cat, _anon_who, is_primary=_gate_primary)
bugs.fix: Make upload_listing_photo and upload_draft_listing_photo plain `def` handlers (FastAPI runs them in the thread pool) and read the body with `file.file.read()`; or keep `async` and move everything after `await file.read()` into `await run_in_threadpool(...)`. Reject images above a pixel budget (e.g. width*height > 50 MP) before convert().
bugs.plain_title: Photo uploads do their image work, AI call and storage write on the server's main loop, freezing it for every user during each upload.
bugs.one_line_fix: Move the three steps to a worker thread (run_in_threadpool) or make the handlers ordinary def functions.

bugs.title: Wishlist push writes on a second connection while run_match_job still holds the write lock, and devices per token are unbounded
bugs.scenario: run_match_job inserts a match (open, uncommitted write transaction) and calls _send_push_for_match, which opens its own connection and runs UPDATE wearable_devices. SQLite has one writer, so that UPDATE waits the 5 s default timeout and fails 'database is locked' for every device: last_ping_at is never saved, dead (410) subscriptions are never deleted, and every other writer in the app is blocked for that time. Because POST /wishlist/wearable/register (level token, no cap) accepts any number of endpoints, one anonymous caller with a slow endpoint can hold the database write lock for about 13 s per device on every pinged match.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute(
    "UPDATE wearable_devices SET last_ping_at = ? WHERE id = ?",        (called from 11890, before conn.commit() at 11894)
bugs.fix: In run_match_job collect (buyer_token, match_id) pairs, commit and close, THEN send the pushes. Cap devices per buyer_token in register_wearable (e.g. 5) and add LIMIT to the device SELECT.
bugs.plain_title: Wishlist alerts write on a second connection while the match job holds the database lock, stalling all writes about 5 seconds per device.
bugs.one_line_fix: Commit the match job first, then send the alerts, and cap devices per token.

bugs.title: Agency bulk import keeps ONE uncommitted transaction open for the whole run, so the database is write-locked for minutes and the import's own AI spend is never logged.
bugs.scenario: An agency imports 2+ adverts (the console sends the whole list in one call). The first INSERT at 21843 opens a write transaction that is only committed after the loop (21851), while every later advert runs AI rewrites, photo downloads and vision scans. For that whole time every other writer in the app (sign-in, publish, payments, _log_ai_spend, the cost-ceiling hold) waits 5 s and fails with "database is locked"; the import's AI spend from advert 2 onward is lost (so the daily ceiling cannot see it), and one bad row or a restart rolls back every advert already processed while their photos and AI cost are already spent.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("INSERT INTO listings (" + ",".join(_imp_cols) + ") VALUES (" + ",".join("?" * len(_imp_cols)) + ")", _imp_vals)   # 21843, inside the for-loop
        conn.commit()   # 21851, only after the loop
database.py: conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH, check_same_thread=False)   # default 5 s busy timeout, implicit BEGIN on INSERT
bugs.fix: Commit per advert: do the AI text pass and the photo pass for a row with no transaction open, then INSERT + conn.commit() for that row (wrap each row in try/except so one bad row is reported in rows[] instead of aborting the batch). Re-read the cap inside the same short transaction.
bugs.plain_title: An agency bulk import holds one open database transaction for the whole run, locking writes for minutes.
bugs.one_line_fix: Commit after each imported advert and do the AI and photo work outside the transaction.

bugs.title: The Seller Hub never removes a request that is no longer pending, so a withdrawn or expired request keeps a live Accept button.
bugs.scenario: A buyer asks, the seller's hub loads the request, the buyer then withdraws (or it expires, or she answers it on another device). Every later loadLiveDash only ADDS requests (and returns early when the server sends none), so the card stays 'pending' until a full page reload. Tapping Accept on it reaches the server fault reported in B3 (bea_main.py 9480: 'withdrawn' is not treated as settled), which charges the buyer 1T and opens the introduction after she withdrew.
bugs.fix: In loadLiveDash step 2, when /intros answers OK, rebuild from the server: build the set of pending ids returned, and for every dashState listing drop (or mark closed) any intro with status 'pending' and a beaId not in that set - before the two early returns at 715/720, which should fall through to updateDashStats() instead of returning.
bugs.plain_title: The Seller Hub keeps a live Accept button on a request that was withdrawn or has expired.
bugs.one_line_fix: Reload requests from the server on open and drop every request that is no longer pending.

bugs.title: formatZAR glues every digit in the price text together, so many real prices are shown wrong on cards and adverts.
bugs.scenario: A seller types 'R450 per day (min 2 days)', 'R850k', 'R1.5 million' or 'R99,99'. Run in Node on the shipped code, the price label comes out as 'R4,502', 'R850', 'R1.50' and 'R9,999' ('R 1 250 000,00' becomes 'R125,000,000', 'R95 each or 3 for R250' becomes 'R953,250'). _msPriceNum in the same file reads the same texts correctly, so the shown price also disagrees with the price filters.
bugs.evidence:
const numStr = s.replace(/[^0-9.]/g, '');
const n = parseFloat(numStr);
bugs.fix: In formatZAR (line 794-800) stop squeezing digits: take the amount from the PRICE-NUM-1 parser (_msPriceNum({price:s}) - first amount, k/m multiplier, decimal comma) and format that; if the text holds a second number that is not part of the first amount, return the seller's text escaped (as the range and compound branches already do).
bugs.lead: Lead ran the shipped function: "R85 000 (2019 model)" came out as R850,002,019 and "R1.5 million" as R1.50.
bugs.plain_title: The price formatter glues together every digit in the price text — 'R85 000 (2019 model)' shows as R850,002,019 and 'R1.5 million' as R1.50.
bugs.one_line_fix: Read only the first amount, understand 'k', 'm' and 'million', and show the rest as the seller wrote it — one shared price parser for app, batch and Quick.

bugs.title: Adventures category chips (Safari, Train, Tours, Lodge, …) filter on a field and vocabulary no advert carries, so they always show 'No Adventures yet'
bugs.scenario: Buyer taps Experiences then the Safari chip. The filter reads l.experience_type||l.activity_type, which neither the server nor _msMapBeaListing provides, so typeVal is '' and every experience is dropped. For Stays the seller form saves 'Guest House', 'Chalet', 'Caravan / Camp site' etc., which only match 2 of the 8 chip keys (bush_camp, self_catering).
bugs.evidence: const typeVal = (isAccom ? (l.accommodation_type||'') : (l.experience_type||l.activity_type||''))…;  if(!typeVal || typeVal !== advCat) return false;
bugs.fix: Carry the seller's 'Activity type' line into the mapped listing (like environment_type via _msDescLine) and map both seller vocabularies onto the chip keys with one lookup table; hide a chip that has zero matches instead of showing an empty grid.
bugs.plain_title: The Adventures chips (Safari, Train, Tours, Lodge …) filter on a field no advert has, so they always show 'No Adventures yet'.
bugs.one_line_fix: Carry the seller's activity type into the advert and map it to the chips with one table; hide a chip that has no matches.

bugs.title: Typed search routes with the server's raw category, so an adventure search crashes the filter bar and pulls the buyer off the Adventures screen
bugs.scenario: /listings rows carry the raw category ('adventures_experiences', 'adventures_accommodation'), never 'Adventures'. On the Adventures screen, Enter on a search that matches adventures finds counts['Adventures']==0, jumps to Browse and calls _msApplyChip('adventures_experiences'); renderFilterBar then throws on Object.entries(filterState[undefined]) and activeFilter is left as an unknown category, so the next redraw empties the grid. From Browse, typing 'lodge' on the Cars chip hits the same throw and the results line stays on 'Searching…'.
bugs.evidence: rows.forEach(r => { const c = r.category || ''; if (c) counts[c] = (counts[c]||0) + 1; });  …  if ((counts['Adventures']||0) > 0) return;  …  _msApplyChip(intent || ((topShare >= 0.7 && top !== 'Adventures') ? top : 'All'));
bugs.fix: In msRouteToMatches count by the chip key: const c = normCat(r.category). Also make renderFilterBar tolerant: const fs = filterState[cat] || {} (line 3071), as renderActiveFilterTags already does.
bugs.plain_title: A typed search for an adventure crashes the filter bar and takes the buyer off the Adventures screen.
bugs.one_line_fix: Normalise the server's category before routing and keep the buyer on the screen she searched from.

bugs.title: The Services 'Service Type' filter reads a field live listings never have, so any choice hides every real service
bugs.scenario: The listing mapper stores the server column as service_type; renderGrid compares l.serviceType. For every live listing l.serviceType is undefined, so picking Plumbing, Electrical, etc. returns 'No listings match your filters' even when matching adverts exist.
bugs.evidence: if(fv.serviceType && fv.serviceType!=='' && l.serviceType !== fv.serviceType) return false;   // mapper (line 508): service_type: l.service_type || null
bugs.fix: Compare against (l.service_type || l.serviceType) and match case-insensitively / by contains, because Quick sends the role's own label as service_type.
bugs.plain_title: The Services 'Service Type' filter reads a field live adverts never have, so any choice hides every real service.
bugs.one_line_fix: Read service_type (both spellings) and match without case, because Quick sends the role label there.

bugs.title: Batch publish treats the server's 409 'saved as a draft - accept the Terms' answer as a failure, tells the seller to check her connection, and every retry creates another set of draft listings.
bugs.scenario: A signed-in seller without a recorded EULA publishes 5 cards: /advert-agent/publish saves each as a draft and answers 409 {need:'eula', detail:...}; the loop counts them as failed, shows 'Publishing failed - check your connection and try again', and each retry inserts 5 more drafts. The EULA step she actually needs is never offered.
bugs.evidence: if (r.ok) { published++; } else if (r.status === 402) { ... } else { console.error('Batch publish failed', r.status, ...); failed++; }
bugs.fix: Handle 409 explicitly: read the JSON, stop the loop, show j.detail and route her to the EULA/publish gate (as aaDoPublish does), and mark those drafts as saved so a retry does not re-post them.
bugs.plain_title: Batch publish treats 'saved as a draft — accept the Terms' as a connection failure, and every retry makes another set of drafts.
bugs.one_line_fix: Handle the 409 answer by opening the Terms and publishing the saved drafts after acceptance.

bugs.title: Edit screen's AI 'Trust Score Action Plan' reads g.guidance, a field /trust-score/guidance never returns, so a paid AI call runs on every Edit open and its answer is always thrown away.
bugs.scenario: Seller taps Edit on any listing -> elLoadSidebarPanels POSTs /trust-score/guidance; the server answers {intro, steps[], closing, ai_available,...} with no 'guidance' key -> `if (g && g.guidance)` is false -> panel hidden. Each open still spends an AI call logged against the seller's daily cost ceiling (_check_cost_ceiling), which can later make the real 'Ask AI coach' button refuse with 429.
bugs.evidence:
const g = await apiPostAuth('/trust-score/guidance', { email, category });
if (g && g.guidance) {
bugs.fix:
Render g.intro + g.steps[].action/why + g.closing (each through _lmEsc) as the other coach screen does (ms.js ~19406), or stop calling the route from openEditListing and offer a button instead; never insert AI text with only \n->
(the current template would also be raw-HTML injection if the key ever existed).
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: The Edit screen pays for an AI 'action plan' every time it opens and then throws the answer away.
bugs.one_line_fix: Paint the fields the server really sends, or call the AI only when the seller taps for it.

bugs.title: Local Market create form never handles the server's '409 need:eula' answer: a seller without the Seller Terms gets an error line, no way to accept, and every further Publish tap creates another hidden draft.
bugs.scenario: First-time Local Market seller (eula_accepted_at NULL) fills the form and taps Publish -> POST /local-market/listings INSERTs a draft and answers 409 {id, need:'eula', detail:'saved as a draft...'} -> the client only opens the Terms sheet on a 403, so it prints 'Error: Your listing is saved as a draft...' and re-enables Publish; each retry inserts one more draft, and the Terms are never offered.
bugs.fix: Treat `resp.status === 409 && j.need === 'eula'` as the Terms case: open _tsSellerTermsGate, then publish the draft already created via PUT /listings/{j.id}/publish (do not POST again); keep the 403 branch for older servers.
bugs.plain_title: The Local Market form ignores the server's 'accept the Terms' answer, so the seller cannot accept and every Publish tap adds a hidden draft.
bugs.one_line_fix: Handle the 409 answer the way the Sell wizard does: show the Terms, then publish the draft already saved.

bugs.title: AI Coach publishes Local Market adverts with category 'LocalMarket', but the server stores it raw and the Local Market page, tile and LM intro route only match 'local_market', so the advert never appears there.
bugs.scenario: Seller picks the LocalMarket chip in the Coach and publishes; /advert-agent/publish inserts category='LocalMarket' (no normalisation, bea_main 11194+). GET /local-market/listings filters l.category = LM_CATEGORY ('local_market'), so the item is missing from the Local Market page and tile, and /local-market/intro answers 404 for it.
bugs.evidence: fd.append('category',      draft.category);   // AA_CATEGORIES key 'LocalMarket'; bea_main.py 13264: LM_CATEGORY = "local_market"
bugs.fix: In aaDoPublish send (draft.category === 'LocalMarket' ? 'local_market' : draft.category); better, normalise category in aa_publish with the existing map (bea_main 14751 _TRUST_CAT_NORM style) before the INSERT.
bugs.plain_title: The AI Coach saves Local Market adverts as 'LocalMarket', so they never appear on the Local Market page.
bugs.one_line_fix: Send 'local_market' and normalise the category at the server door.

bugs.title: The agency console's 'view this agent's drafts' panel shows the signed-in admin's OWN drafts under the agent's name: the gate rewrites the email query to the session.
bugs.scenario: Agency admin taps an agent's amber 'N drafts' chip: agencyDraftsView fetches /listings/mine?email=<agent>; route_policy binds 'email' (in query) to the session, so security_gate replaces it with the admin's email. The panel says 'Drafts — agent@x' but lists the admin's own drafts, or 'No drafts right now' straight after a bulk import.
bugs.evidence:
var r=await fetch(BEA_URL+'/listings/mine?email='+encodeURIComponent(email),{headers:{'X-Api-Key':API_KEY}});
{"key": "GET /listings/mine", "level": "user", "bind": [{"name": "email", "in": "query"}]}
bugs.fix: Add an agency-scoped read route (e.g. GET /agencies/{agency_id}/agents/{email}/drafts, policy user + own agency) that checks membership and returns the agent's drafts, and call it here; do not reuse the self-bound /listings/mine.
bugs.plain_title: The agency console's 'view this agent's drafts' shows the admin's own drafts under the agent's name.
bugs.one_line_fix: Give the console its own agency route for an agent's drafts instead of the 'my listings' route.

bugs.title: Agent Hub crashes for agents in the collector, institution, service_company and placement verticals: AS_VERT only knows property, cars and travel.
bugs.scenario: An agent onboarded from a collector/institution/service/placement agency console (agencyBulkRun sends vertical=agencySkinVertical(); estate_agents stores it on the profile) opens the Agent Hub: _asProfileLoad sets _asState.vertical='collector', _asProfileHtml reads AS_VERT['collector'].certs -> TypeError inside an async render nobody catches, so the pane stays on 'Loading…' for ever and the agent can never upload credentials or go live.
bugs.evidence:
var AS_VERT={property:{...},cars:{...},travel:{...}};
'...'+AS_VERT[_asState.vertical].certs+' Upload each one here…'
bugs.fix: Add AS_VERT entries for collector, institution, service_company and placement (labels/certs from estate_agents.VERTICALS), use (AS_VERT[v]||{label:'Professional agent',certs:''}) at 22735 and 22785, and wrap the render in try/catch that paints an error line instead of leaving 'Loading…'.
bugs.plain_title: The Agent Hub crashes for collector, institution, service-company and placement agents.
bugs.one_line_fix: Add the four verticals to the hub's table and fall back to a generic entry for an unknown one.

bugs.title: Batch card publish keeps only the first run of digits of the price, so 'R1 200' or 'R1,500' is published as R1.
bugs.scenario: The AI suggests 'R1,200-R1,500' for a valuable card (or the seller types 'R1 500' into the PRICE box); the regex /[0-9]+/ takes '1' and the advert goes live at R1, and the server also stores ai_suggested_price=1 as the price-check anchor.
bugs.evidence: price:       (d.price_suggestion.match(/[0-9]+/)||[''])[0],  // take first number from range e.g. 'R25-R45' -> '25'
bugs.fix: Take the first amount including thousands separators and strip them: const m=String(d.price_suggestion).match(/\d[\d\s,]*(?:\.\d+)?/); price: m? m[0].replace(/[\s,]/g,'') : '' - or send the seller's text unchanged and let the server's _price_number parse it.
bugs.plain_title: Batch card publish keeps only the first group of digits — 'R1 200' is published as R1.
bugs.one_line_fix: Strip spaces and thousands separators before reading the number (use the shared price parser).

bugs.title: Edit screen asks /trust-score/breakdown for the bare 'Services'/'Adventures'/'Property' category, so Casuals workers, accommodation hosts and private property sellers are scored against the wrong signal set and that wrong score is written onto their listing cards.
bugs.scenario: A nanny (Services, service_class casual) or a guest-house host (Adventures accommodation) opens Edit -> elCurrentCat='Services'/'Adventures' -> server _norm_cat_key maps them to 'Services-Technical' / 'Adventures-Experiences' (no service_class sent) -> score/tip/declarable docs come from the wrong set (e.g. her earned police clearance does not count), and the breakdown's category branch runs `UPDATE listings SET trust_score=? ... AND category=?` with that wrong score for all her listings in the category. The intended Property_private suffix never happens: it is read from raw.structured_fields._gate, a field the server does not store, so private sellers get the agent (FFC/PPRA) set; the doc list for 'Adventures' likewise hides adv_acc documents.
bugs.evidence:
elCurrentCat = normCat(dl.cat || dl._raw.category || '');
const catParam = category ? '&category=' + encodeURIComponent(category) : '';
bugs.fix: Compute a trust key separate from the form key in openEditListing: Services -> 'Services-Technical'/'Services-Casuals' from raw.service_class; Adventures -> 'Adventures-Accommodation' when /accom/ matches raw.category or raw.service_class, else 'Adventures-Experiences'; Property -> 'Property_private' unless the seller is an agent (from the server's own data, not structured_fields). Pass that key to elLoadSidebarPanels, the doc-list and upload-comment calls; or omit category and let the server's _category_key_for_user decide.
bugs.plain_title: The Edit screen asks for the Trust Score with the wrong category, and the wrong score is written onto the seller's advert cards.
bugs.one_line_fix: Send the full trust category from the Edit screen (for example Services-Casuals, Adventures-Accommodation).

bugs.title: Drafts made by the AI report's 'List as one lot' / 'List separately' publish with NO photos, although the Coach shows them as captured and 'ready to upload'.
bugs.scenario: aiListLot()/aiListEach() store photos as {slot, blob} (no dataUrl). aaRenderPhotosScreen counts those slots as captured, the Publish screen says '3 photos ready to upload', but aaDoPublish only appends photos that have p.dataUrl, so the advert goes live with zero photos and no warning.
bugs.evidence:
for (const p of (draft.photos || [])) {
    if (p.dataUrl) {   // ms.js 16092-16093; drafts from ms.js 20469: photos = AI_PHOTOS.slice(0,3).map((p,i)=>({slot:slots[i], blob:aiDataUrlToBlob(p)}))
bugs.fix: In aaDoPublish append p.blob when present (fd.append('photos', p.blob, p.slot+'.jpg')) before falling back to dataUrl; in aaRenderPhotosScreen build the thumbnail from URL.createObjectURL(p.blob) when there is no dataUrl (or store dataUrl in aiListLot/aiListEach instead of blob).
bugs.plain_title: Drafts made from the AI report publish with no photos although the Coach shows the photos as ready.
bugs.one_line_fix: Send the report's stored photos when the draft is published, and show their thumbnails in the Coach.

bugs.title: aaCurrency() only knows ZA/US/GB/DE/EU, so a Coach seller in Kenya, Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique, Canada, Australia or New Zealand has rates and Adventure prices published in US dollars.
bugs.scenario: activeCountry.iso2='KE': aaCurrency() falls back to {USD,'$'}; aaRateText publishes 'Rate: $30 /hr' and aaDoPublish sends price '$1200 / night' for a stay, while the rest of the app (ADV_COUNTRY_CURRENCY, ms.js 3624/20788) shows KSh. Buyers see a dollar price the seller never meant.
bugs.evidence: return map[(activeCountry && activeCountry.iso2) || 'ZA'] || { code: 'USD', symbol: '$' };
bugs.fix: Derive the symbol from ADV_COUNTRY_CURRENCY (ms.js 3624) and add the ISO code per country (KES, NAD, BWP, MZN, CAD, AUD, NZD); default to the ZA entry, never USD.
bugs.plain_title: The AI Coach only knows five currencies, so sellers in Kenya, Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique, Canada, Australia and New Zealand are priced in US dollars.
bugs.one_line_fix: Take the currency from the same country table the rest of the app uses.

bugs.title: The contact mask on advert descriptions misses the usual phone formats, so a seller's number can show before any introduction
bugs.scenario: A description containing '082 123 4567', '082-123-4567', '+27 82 123 4567', '012 345 6789' or any non-South-African number passes through unmasked; '0821234567' is masked but its last digit is left. The server scrub (24 Sep 2026) reduces exposure for new adverts, but this is the last guard for older text and any door the scrub misses.
bugs.fix: Replace with a format-agnostic pattern (a + or 0 followed by 8–14 digits allowing spaces, dots, dashes and brackets between them, e.g. /(?:\+|\b0)(?:[\s().-]?\d){8,14}/g), run it on text nodes only, and backfill the server scrub over existing adverts so the client mask is not the only guard.
bugs.lead: Lead read the pattern at ms.js 5662: "082 123 4567" and "+27 82 123 4567" do not match it.
bugs.plain_title: The contact mask misses ordinary phone formats ('082 123 4567', '+27 82 123 4567'), so a number can show before an introduction.
bugs.one_line_fix: Use one phone pattern that allows spaces, dashes and country codes, shared with the server scrub.

bugs.title: The agency console paints agent emails and names into HTML and inline onclick handlers without escaping (stored XSS).
bugs.scenario: POST /agencies/{id}/agents accepts any string containing '@' as the email (bea_main.py 20639), and the rollup name falls back to the part before '@'. An agency admin (or anyone holding the agency import key, via agents/bulk) adds '@x.co'; the script then runs for whoever opens that org's console, including a TrustSquare superuser using the Ops org switcher. Agent rows carry no 'id', so the server's content gate does not clean them; an ordinary address with an apostrophe (o'brien@...) also breaks the Remove and Pro-seat buttons.
bugs.evidence:
+'
'+(m.name||m.email)+'
'+m.email+'
' +'
bugs.fix: In _agRowFn (2320-2337) wrap m.name, m.email, c.label, m.status, m.tier in _lmEsc() for HTML, and stop building handlers from the email: put data-email="_lmEsc(m.email)" on the buttons and read it in one delegated click listener. Also escape a.admin_email, a.countries and a.api_key at 2369-2379, and email at 2280/2284. Server: validate the invite email with a strict pattern.
bugs.plain_title: The agency console paints agent names and emails as HTML, so a crafted name can run script in an admin's session.
bugs.one_line_fix: Escape names and emails where they are painted and stop building onclick text from them.

bugs.title: Zoom option buttons put server values inside inline onclick with only HTML-encoded apostrophes, so a value with an apostrophe breaks out of the script string
bugs.scenario: A facet value such as street "St John's Road" or a seller-typed make arrives from /zoom/next. The attribute is HTML-decoded before the handler is compiled, so ' becomes ' again: the tap throws a syntax error (dead button) and a crafted make like ');alert(1);// runs script in every buyer's session. Reachable when the baseline_q4 flag is on (dark for the public today).
bugs.evidence: onclick="zoomPick('${_zoomEsc(q.facet)}','${_zoomEsc(o.v).replace(/'/g,''')}')"   (same pattern in zoomLockedTap line 3328, tail options line 3330, zoomDrop lines 3309/3314)
bugs.fix: Stop building JS from data: render data-facet / data-v attributes (HTML-escaped) and use onclick="zoomPick(this.dataset.facet,this.dataset.v)"; do the same for zoomDrop and zoomLockedTap.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.
bugs.plain_title: Zoom option buttons break when a value contains an apostrophe, which lets advert text run as script (the feature is switched off today).
bugs.one_line_fix: Attach the click with addEventListener and keep the value in a data attribute.

bugs.title: Reflected XSS: the invite link's city/suburb (?magic=1&city=...&suburb=...) reaches the sell flow's agents step and is painted with innerHTML unescaped.
bugs.scenario: Attacker sends https://trustsquare.co/?magic=1&cat=property&city= (no token needed: ms.js 1276 copies sp.get('city') into magicLink.area unvalidated, unlike _msLinkCity at 1343; sfNewState copies it to sfState.city, and suburb reaches sfState.area via sfResetListing). When the seller reaches 'Boost your sale?', line 22619 ('near '+(sfState.area||sfState.city)) and 22647 ('No listed agents near '+city) inject it, running script on trustsquare.co with her session cookie.
bugs.evidence:
'Finding trusted '+sfAgentNoun()+'s near '+(sfState.area||sfState.city)+'…' h+='
No listed '+sfAgentNoun()+'s near '+city+' yet
'
bugs.fix: Wrap every sfState.area / sfState.city / city insertion in esc() (ms.js 3566) at 22619 and 22647; also validate magicLink.area/suburb/name where they are read from the URL (ms.js 1276), with the same pattern _msLinkCity uses, so no other screen can repeat this.
bugs.lead: Lead read ms.js 22647: the city from the link is painted with innerHTML unescaped.
bugs.plain_title: A crafted invite link (?magic=1&city=…) runs script when the seller reaches the agents step in Sell.
bugs.one_line_fix: Escape the city and suburb where they are painted and validate them against the city list when the link is read.

bugs.title: Stored XSS: an agent's own 'Suburbs served' / 'City' text from /agents/nearby is inserted raw into the seller agent card (sell flow) and the buyer agent cards (Adventures panel, Property/Cars browse panel, agent directory).
bugs.scenario: A live agent saves suburbs '' via POST /agents/profile (estate_agents._upsert_profile stores it with only .strip(); later edits never re-trigger verification). /agents/nearby is public and its rows carry anon_ref, not id, so security_gate CONTENT-GATE-1 (_encode only cleans dicts that have an 'id') leaves them untouched; sfAgentCardHtml (22667) and advAgentCard (23249) paint them for every visitor of that city, signed in or not.
bugs.evidence:
'
'+(a.suburbs||a.city)+' · '+a.experience+''+sold+'
' '
'+(a.suburbs||a.city||'')+' · ...
bugs.fix: esc() a.suburbs, a.city, a.experience, a.anon_ref, every badge b and pitch.label/advantages/legal_note in sfAgentCardHtml, sfAgentsLoad, advAgentCard, advAgentsLoad and catAgentsLoad; server side, run _plain_text() over headline/bio/city/suburbs/specialties/languages in _upsert_profile (covers bulk onboarding too).
bugs.plain_title: An agent's own 'Suburbs served' text runs as script in every seller's and buyer's agent card.
bugs.one_line_fix: Escape agent fields in the card builder and add /agents/nearby to the gate's output cleaning.

bugs.title: POST /listings lets anyone file unlimited drafts under any email address - the Quick limits do not apply to it
bugs.scenario: The route is public and its key ships in ms.js; the only flood control (check_listing_velocity) is switched off by default. A script posts thousands of drafts with seller_email=victim@x.com: they fill her My Listings, feed their suburb text into GET /suburbs, grow the database without bound, and after ten of them the victim's own Quick saves are refused for the day ('Too many listings for this email address today') because _QP_ID_MAX counts those rows.
bugs.evidence:
launch_redemption.check_listing_velocity(listing.seller_email)  # per-day flood control (env-gated OFF)
conn = database.get_db()
bugs.fix: Apply the quick-publish limits here too: when there is no session matching seller_email, enforce the per-IP cap (_QP_IP_LOG pattern) and the per-address daily cap before the INSERT, and cap title/description length (e.g. 200 / 8,000 characters).

bugs.title: One buyer can keep any Property advert hidden from all other buyers at no cost by withdrawing and asking again.
bugs.scenario: A request on a Property listing pauses it. The buyer withdraws (hold returned in full, listing live again) and asks again at once; the duplicate check only looks at pending rows and there is no wait after a withdrawal, decline or expiry and no cap on open requests. With a float of N Tuppence a rival can keep N properties paused indefinitely and get every Tuppence back.
bugs.evidence: "SELECT id FROM intro_requests WHERE listing_id = ? AND lower(buyer_email) = lower(?) AND status = 'pending'",
bugs.fix: In create_intro, for commitment listings, refuse a new request from a buyer who withdrew, was declined or expired on the same listing in the last 7 days, and cap open pending requests per buyer (for example 5); say so in the 409 text.

bugs.title: The anonymous AI draft routes put uncapped text from the request into the prompt, so a few calls can use up the platform's daily AI budget and pause AI for everyone.
bugs.scenario: POST /listings/draft-from-photo caps 'intent' at 300 characters but passes 'city' whole; POST /listings/draft-from-photos passes each photo's 'slot' whole. A caller sends a 500 000-character city 30 times (the per-IP budget counts calls, not size). Each call bills well over 100k input tokens, the platform ceiling in _check_cost_ceiling is reached and every AI feature answers 429 until midnight UTC.
bugs.evidence:
city = (req.get("city") or "").strip() or "Pretoria"
f""{intent}"
City: {city}

"
line 10605: slots.append(ph.get("slot") or f"photo_{len(slots)+1}")
bugs.fix: Cap every request string before it reaches a prompt: city[:80]; str(slot)[:40]; in aa_coach_ask req.step[:40] in user_message (line 11137); in aa_coach category[:40], each field value [:2000] and at most 40 fields. Refuse non-string values with 400.

bugs.title: The public wishlist-signal route opens demand tickets on a client-claimed 'zero results' with no rate limit or size limit, and the invite those tickets trigger says 'A verified buyer'
bugs.scenario: Anyone can script POST /wishlist/signal with any 8-character token, a category, three words and result_count=0: score 4 opens a ticket, and varying the text opens as many as wanted (raw_text has no length bound, the route has no per-client budget). Once DEMAND_LOOP is switched on each ticket spends one prospect's 'one email, ever' on an invitation stating 'A verified buyer on TrustSquare is actively looking for...' although nothing about the sender was verified.
bugs.evidence:
if sig.result_count is None or int(sig.result_count) != 0:
            return None        (12035: A verified buyer on TrustSquare is actively looking for)
bugs.fix: Bound raw_text (e.g. 240 chars) and add _sec_ip_budget_ok on the route; open a ticket only for a token linked to a signed-in account (users.buyer_token) or after N distinct tokens ask the same thing, and re-check the miss server-side before an invite is composed.

bugs.title: Local Market intro cooldown and daily cap are keyed on a value the caller chooses
bugs.scenario: A signed-in buyer posts /local-market/intro with buyer_email omitted and a fresh buyer_token each time. The gate only rewrites buyer_email when it is present, so the 7-day cooldown, the 10-a-day cap and the stored row all use the throw-away token: she can re-request straight after a decline and send unlimited requests, each of which notifies the seller.
