bugs.evidence: (req.listing_id, req.buyer_email or req.buyer_token, cooldown_cutoff)        (13782: (req.buyer_email or req.buyer_token, _sql_since(hours=24)))
bugs.fix: Derive one identity at the top - buyer_id = _session_email(ts_user) or req.buyer_email or req.buyer_token - and use it for the cooldown, the cap and the INSERT.

bugs.title: The import photo fetcher downloads the whole response before checking the 12 MB limit, and its private-address check can be bypassed by a host that changes its DNS answer.
bugs.scenario: An advert's photo URL points at a multi-gigabyte file or an endless stream with an image/* header: c.get() buffers the entire body in memory and only then is the size tested (the 12 s timeout is per read, not total). Separately, the host is resolved and checked with getaddrinfo, then httpx resolves it again for the real request, so a rebinding DNS name passes the check and fetches a loopback/private address; the per-photo notes (http-404 / not-an-image / fetch-failed) report what was found there.
bugs.evidence:
infos = socket.getaddrinfo(host, None)
                r = c.get(url, follow_redirects=False)
        raw = r.content
        return (raw, "") if 100 < len(raw) <= 12 * 1024 * 1024 else (None, "bad-size")
bugs.fix: Use c.stream('GET', ...) and stop reading once 12 MB + 1 is exceeded, with an overall deadline (e.g. 20 s). Connect to the IP that was checked (resolve once, pass the IP to httpx with the Host/SNI header set) and refuse unless ip.is_global.

bugs.title: Inbound email is acknowledged every time with no loop guard, no per-sender cap and no duplicate check, so an autoresponder or a forged sender gets unlimited mail
bugs.scenario: Our acknowledgement goes to a customer whose mailbox auto-replies (out-of-office, another helpdesk's 'ticket received'). That reply arrives at support@, is triaged (one AI call), stored and acknowledged again, which triggers the next auto-reply: a ping-pong with no end. The same path lets anyone who forges a From address make us mail that address repeatedly; the support form has a 5-per-hour cap, this door has none, and a re-delivered message (same message_id) is answered twice.
bugs.evidence:
elif category != "spam" and fault_code and os.getenv("MAINT_ACK_SEND", "1") == "1":
    payload["headers"] = {"In-Reply-To": in_reply_to, "References": in_reply_to}
bugs.fix: In _triage_message: skip when a row with the same message_id exists; send at most one acknowledgement per sender per 24 h and at most N auto-answers per sender per hour (count email_triage rows); give the customer lane a 'machine' class that is answered with silence, as the outreach lane has. In _smtp_send_reply add headers Auto-Submitted: auto-replied and X-Auto-Response-Suppress: All, and have the worker pass the inbound Auto-Submitted header so auto-generated mail is never answered.

bugs.title: A phrase the translator returns unchanged is never cached, so it is bought again on every page load.
bugs.scenario: Names the prompt orders the model to keep ('TrustSquare', 'Tuppence', 'Buzz', 'Pro'), prices like 'R1 200' and place names come back equal to the source and are dropped. They are missing again for the next reader and the next page load (ms.js only remembers them for one page session), so each load makes a paid 'reason' call and the 400-calls-a-day cap is used up; after that genuinely new text stays English for everyone that day.
bugs.evidence:
if val and val != src:
    got[src] = val
bugs.fix: Cache the answered line even when it equals the source (store out = src), and return it in 'out', so the phrase is settled once.

bugs.title: A closed account stays fully alive: its adverts remain live, its passkeys and sign-in keep working, and nothing ever reopens or anonymises it
bugs.scenario: A seller closes her account. close_account() only zeroes the wallet, bumps session_version and stamps users.closed_at. Her listings are untouched (no query reads closed_at except the key-link and phone doors, bea_main.py:4885, 5055), so buyers keep seeing them and sending introduction requests nobody will answer. She can sign in again by code, Google/Apple or passkey (_establish_user_session has no closed check) and carries on with closed_at still set; the '30 days' anonymisation job named in the comment does not exist. The old cookie also keeps working for up to 30 s (_SV_CACHE).
bugs.evidence: account_closure.py:126-130  # ... Mark closed now; the anonymisation pass is a separate, dated job  ...  conn.execute("UPDATE users SET closed_at=? WHERE lower(email)=?", (_now(), email))
bugs.fix: In close_account(): set the account's live/resting listings to a withdrawn status, delete its passkey credentials, device/push registrations and pending sign-in codes in the same transaction, and pop the address from _SV_CACHE in the handler. In _establish_user_session(): if closed_at is set, treat the sign-in as a return (clear closed_at + restore_on_return).

bugs.title: The tier matrix is keyed 'UK' but listings store the country as 'GB', so every UK property gets no fair-price or yield service
bugs.scenario: A London listing has country 'GB' (geo tables, Quick pack and ms.js all use GB). _listing_country_iso2 passes 'GB' through, available_tiers('fair_price','property','GB') returns [] and the button is hidden; tier_resolvers.served_tiers and the Land Registry resolver also test for 'UK' and never run.
bugs.evidence:
return str(country).strip().upper()[:2] or "*"
"UK": [
    _t(VERIFIED, "Verified comps", "Exact sold comparables (HM Land Registry).",
bugs.fix: Normalise in one place: in _norm_country map 'GB' -> 'UK' (and do the same at the top of tier_resolvers.served_tiers and in bea_main._listing_country_iso2).

bugs.title: GET /listings adds the online-mode and trip-planning branches without the requested category, so a Services search returns online Tutors (and one travel category returns all of them)
bugs.scenario: GET /listings?category=services adds branch D, which selects every listing whose mode is Online/Both in any category and any city; online tutor adverts come back in the Services result and its facet counts (and online services in a Tutors result). The app's search relies on this call to 'never leak other categories' (ms.js line 5212). Branch C does the same for category=accommodation, returning every trip-planning category.
bugs.fix: When category is given, append 'AND LOWER(l.category) = LOWER(?)' to branch_d and branch_c and add the category to params_d / params_c (params_d is always empty today); on the mixed feed give branch D the same Local Market exclusion branches A and B use.

bugs.title: Post-publish geocoding always sends the street address to Nominatim as South Africa and with the geo-table city only, so non-ZA adverts get wrong or no map coordinates
bugs.scenario: A Kenyan or US property advert with a street address is published. _publish_autolinks calls _geocode_address(address, city_name) with no country, so the query is '<address>, <city>, ZA' (and city is '' when the city is not in geo_cities, e.g. Montana). Nominatim returns nothing or a same-named South African street, and that wrong point is stored as the public listing_lat/lng and drives the nearby-places look-up.
bugs.evidence:
glat, glng = _geocode_address(listing_row["street_address"], city_name_str)
...
def _geocode_address(address: str, city: str, country_iso2: str = "ZA") -> tuple:
    query = f"{address}, {city}, {country_iso2}"
bugs.fix: Select `city, country` in the listing_row query and call `_geocode_address(street_address, listing_row['city'] or city_name_str, (listing_row['country'] or 'ZA'))`; skip geocoding when no country is known.

bugs.title: World Heritage auto-linking never runs for Stays and Experiences because the allow-list tests for 'adventures' but adverts are stored as 'adventures_accommodation' / 'adventures_experiences'
bugs.scenario: A guest house published from the sell flow has category 'adventures_accommodation' (sfListingCategory). _publish_autolinks compares the lower-cased category with ('property', 'adventures'), so it is skipped and linked_wonders stays empty - the ruling was Property + Adventures. _CAT_AFFINITY has no key for the stored names either, so the affinity weights are never used.
bugs.evidence:
_wcat = ((cat_row["category"] or "") if cat_row else "").strip().lower()
if city_row and city_row["lat"] and city_row["lng"] and _wcat in ("property", "adventures"):
bugs.fix: Test `_wcat == 'property' or _wcat.startswith('adventures')`, and in auto_link_wonders normalise the key (`cat_key = cat_key.replace('adventures_', '')`) so 'accommodation' / 'experiences' hit their _CAT_AFFINITY rows.

bugs.title: The duplicate-ID test counts every ledger row, so anyone who merely types another person's ID number locks the real owner out of verification.
bugs.scenario: Account A enters B's ID number once; whatever the outcome (failed, unavailable or duplicate_hash) a row with that hash is written. When B later tries her own ID, step 2 finds A's row, returns duplicate_hash and B never reaches the supplier. The message says support has been notified, but nothing notifies anyone.
bugs.evidence:
"""SELECT email FROM id_verification_ledger
   WHERE id_hash=? AND lower(email)<>? LIMIT 1""",
bugs.fix: Treat an ID as taken only when another account holds a VERIFIED result for it: add "AND outcome='verified'" to the query, keep the other rows as review flags, and send the support notice the message promises.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.

bugs.title: After one failed Home Affairs check a seller can never be verified with that ID, because the stored answer is keyed on the ID number alone and ignores the name.
bugs.scenario: Seller types her ID with a nickname or a typo in the surname. The supplier answers PARTIAL_MATCH: 1T is charged, the outcome is 'failed', and she is told to check the names on her document. She corrects the name and tries again; step 3 finds the earlier row for the same hash and returns cached_fail without asking the supplier - every time.
bugs.evidence:
WHERE id_hash=? AND lower(email)=? AND outcome IN ('verified','failed')
return {"outcome": f"cached_{'pass' if prior['outcome']=='verified' else 'fail'}",
bugs.fix: Store a hash of the normalised full name on each ledger row and reuse a 'failed' row only when both the ID hash and the name hash match; a changed name runs a new paid query (still under the daily cap).

bugs.title: The AI Coach, its status route and the buyer-token route look the account up by the exact typed spelling, so an email with a capital letter is 'not registered'.
bugs.scenario: Same cause as the 402 on introductions: the gate leaves 'Thandi@Gmail.com' as typed when it matches the session after lower-casing. aa_coach then answers 401 'No TrustSquare seller account for Thandi@Gmail.com', aa_status reports registered false and balance 0, and mint_buyer_token finds no row and hands out a new unlinked token on every call, so her wishlist never follows her to another device.
bugs.evidence:
"SELECT aa_free_used, aa_sessions_remaining, trust_score FROM users WHERE email = ?",
(req.email,)
line 11975: "SELECT buyer_token FROM users WHERE email = ?", (req.email,)
bugs.fix: Lower-case and strip the email at the top of aa_status, aa_coach and mint_buyer_token (use _sess in mint_buyer_token) and query with LOWER(email) = ?; the gate change named under the introduction 402 finding fixes all of them at once.

bugs.title: An advert published through the coach goes live in a 'coming soon' country and skips Kenya's consent, both of which the other publish doors enforce.
bugs.scenario: A seller with an accepted EULA sends POST /advert-agent/publish with country DE (or a Botswana or Mozambique city). quick_publish (line 4719) and publish_listing (5311-5317) refuse this; aa_publish only resolves the country and inserts the row as 'live'. A Kenyan Property advert likewise goes live without users.xborder_consent_at.
bugs.evidence:
"live" if _go_live else "draft",   # SEC-GATE-1 (24 Sep 2026): draft until the EULA is on record
_aa_geo_city_id, _aa_country),     # COACH-CITY-1
bugs.fix: After _aa_country is resolved (line 11427): if it is in COMING_SOON_COUNTRIES and not is_super, save as draft and answer 409 with _coming_soon_detail(...); if it is 'KE', the category is property and _ke_consent_given is false, save as draft and answer 428 CONSENT_REQUIRED_DETAIL.

bugs.title: A Local Market cooling-off never ends by itself: the publish check ignores the date and the restore hook only runs when the stored score changes
bugs.scenario: A seller serves her 30-day cooling-off with a Trust Score back above 30. _lm_check_seller_can_publish returns 'cooling_off_until_<date>' for any active suspension row without comparing the date to now, and _lm_try_restore is reached only from trust_score_breakdown when no category is passed AND the score differs from the stored one (15030). With a stable score she stays blocked and her listings stay hidden indefinitely.
bugs.evidence:
if susp and susp.get("cooling_off_until"):
        return f"cooling_off_until_{susp['cooling_off_until']}"        (15030: if not category and prior_score != score_total:)
bugs.fix: Call _lm_try_restore(conn, seller) at the top of _lm_check_seller_can_publish and in the daily lifecycle sweep, and compare cooling_off_until with now before refusing.

bugs.title: Local Market publish without recorded Terms answers 409 + draft, but the form only opens the Terms step on 403, so the seller is stuck and each retry stores another draft
bugs.scenario: A seller whose first advert is Local Market accepts the Local Market box (lm_eula_accepted_at) and taps Publish. The server checks eula_accepted_at (main Terms), saves a draft and answers 409 need:'eula'; ms.js feaLmSubmit (14383) opens the Terms step only for status 403 with 'eula|terms', so she sees 'Error: Your listing is saved as a draft...' with no way to accept, and every further tap inserts another draft row.
bugs.evidence:
return _JR(status_code=409, content={
            "id": new_id, "live": False, "need": "eula",
bugs.fix: Pick one contract: either refuse BEFORE the INSERT with 403 'EULA not accepted' (what the form already handles, as the other publish door does at 5296), or keep the draft and have feaLmSubmit handle 409 need==='eula' by opening _tsSellerTermsGate and then publishing that draft id instead of posting again.

bugs.title: The no-show penalty is saved under the buyer's email, but the buyer score given to sellers at request time is read by buyer_token
bugs.scenario: A signed-in buyer misses a meeting and ops upholds the report: lm_complaints.buyer_token holds intro.buyer_email (her email), so -3 lands on buyer_trust['her@email']. On her next request lm_create_intro reads _buyer_trust(conn, req.buyer_token) - the device token, which has no row - and tells the next seller 'buyer_trust_score: 40'. The penalty never reaches the seller who is deciding.
bugs.evidence: _set_buyer_trust(conn, row["buyer_token"], -LM_BUYER_NOSHOW_PENALTY)        (13736: buyer_score = _buyer_trust(conn, req.buyer_token))
bugs.fix: Use one key everywhere: in lm_create_intro read the score with the same identity that is stored in intro_requests.buyer_email (the session email when signed in).

bugs.title: 'Zero ignored introductions (rolling 90 days)' only looks at requests that are still pending, and compares two different timestamp formats
bugs.scenario: A seller ignores a request: at 96 h the sweep marks it 'expired', the query (status = 'pending') no longer sees it and the +10 comes straight back, beside her 'Unanswered introduction -5' penalty - nothing is rolling 90 days. In the other direction created_at is stored 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' and compared with an ISO 'T...+00:00' string, so a request made on the cutoff's calendar day counts as ignored when it is only 24-48 h old and she loses the 10 points while she still has time to answer.
bugs.evidence:
WHERE l.seller_email = ? AND i.status = 'pending'
             AND i.created_at < ?""",
        (email, (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=48)).isoformat())
bugs.fix: Count intro_penalties rows (or intros with status 'expired') in the last 90 days plus pending ones older than 48 h, and build the cutoff with _sql_since(hours=48) so both sides share one format.

bugs.title: Replacement chains are applied one link only, so a higher credential does not cancel a lower one two steps down (double count)
bugs.scenario: A tutor holds the diploma (6) and Honours (14) credentials but no Bachelor row. Honours replaces bachelor and bachelor replaces diploma; with bachelor absent nothing marks the diploma as replaced, so she scores 20 instead of 14. The same happens for TGCSA 3-star + 5-star (36 instead of 22) and the FIDE titles; _earned_display (14849) repeats the logic, so the visible list agrees with the wrong total.
bugs.fix: Walk the whole chain: for each active id follow 'replaces' repeatedly and add every ancestor that is active to replaced_ids; put it in one helper used by both _sum_earned_with_replaces and _earned_display.

bugs.title: Trust coach and upload comment look the category up without normalising it, so Services, Adventures, Cars and Local Market sellers get no category credentials
bugs.scenario: ms.js sends normCat() values ('Services', 'Adventures', 'Cars', 'LocalMarket') while _CATEGORY_SIGNALS is keyed 'Services-Casuals', 'Adventures-Experiences', 'Cars_private', 'local_market'. A nanny's plan therefore never mentions the police clearance that opens her advert to strangers, and after an upload the comment says the document is worth '+0 pts'.
bugs.evidence: cat_signals       = _CATEGORY_SIGNALS.get(req.category, {})        (15867: all_signals = {**_TRUST_SIGNALS, **_CATEGORY_SIGNALS.get(req.category, {})})
bugs.fix: Use _norm_cat_key(req.category, service_class) at both places, as trust_score_breakdown does, and drop baseline_q4 entries while that switch is off (as _trust_evidence does) so the coach never asks for evidence that scores nothing.

bugs.title: Document Hub calls act on the operator's own account (or answer 401) because _actor only recognises X-Admin-Key while the admin console sends X-Admin-Token.
bugs.scenario: An operator signed in to the admin console (its fetch wrapper adds X-Admin-Token, never X-Admin-Key) opens a seller in the Document Hub and runs 'Verify ID'. The gate admits the token, but _actor sees no admin key and returns the operator's own session email, so the seller's ID hash, id_name and the id_ai_verified credential are written to the operator's user row; with no ts_user cookie it answers 401. The same happens at 16011 (upload), 16172 (list), 16308 (delete) and 17074 (identity-status).
bugs.evidence: email = _actor(ts_user, email, "verify-identity", x_admin_key)
bugs.fix: Give these handlers an admin-token lane: add x_admin_token: str = Header(default=None) and, when _gate_is_admin-style validation (_admin_claims(x_admin_token)) succeeds, use the path email unchanged instead of calling _actor - or extend _actor itself with an admin_token parameter checked the same way.

bugs.title: The certificate name check awards 'Certificate name matches ID' whatever the result, including when the file could not be read or the names differ.
bugs.scenario: A seller with an ID name on file uploads any certificate (a PDF the vision call cannot parse returns confidence 0 and no name). All three branches set new_status = 'earned', so category.lm.cert_name_verified (2 points, shown as a name match) is granted every time. The call also passes no email, so the per-seller AI cost ceiling and spend log do not apply to it.
bugs.fix: Award only on a real match, as the docstring states: write 'earned' only when confidence >= 0.75 and name_match >= 0.70, and write nothing otherwise (not measured); pass email=email to _vision_verify_identity.

bugs.title: The launch board's 'Complaints (24h)' undercounts because an ISO 'T' cutoff is string-compared with SQLite 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' stamps.
bugs.scenario: lm_complaints.filed_at is filled by DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP ('2026-10-03 14:00:00'); the cutoff is datetime.isoformat() ('2026-10-03T09:15:00.1+00:00'). A space sorts before 'T', so every complaint filed on the cutoff's calendar day is excluded: at 00:30 UTC a complaint filed at 23:00 is not counted, yet the tile reports measured=True.
bugs.evidence:
_c24 = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()
        v, ok, note = _count(
            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM lm_complaints WHERE filed_at >= ?", (_c24,))
bugs.fix: Bind the cutoff in the stored shape: replace _c24 with _sql_since(days=1), the helper at line 189 that the other windows in this file use.

bugs.title: The sign-in email promises a button that works for 7 days, but /auth/verify refuses any link older than 72 hours.
bugs.scenario: SIGNIN-LINK-7D (3 Oct) set _SIGNIN_LINK_DAYS = 7 and the email copy to '7 days', and the token's exp is 7 days. auth_verify (line 20344) still applies the 24 Sep SIGNIN-ONCE-1 age check, so a person who taps the button on day 4 to 7 gets 'This sign-in link is too old - request a new one' - the blocker the 3 Oct change was meant to remove.
bugs.fix: In auth_verify replace 72 * 3600 with _SIGNIN_LINK_DAYS * 86400 (this amends the 72-hour limit of the 24 Sep SIGNIN-ONCE-1 ruling; single-use stays). If 72 hours must stay, change _SIGNIN_LINK_DAYS and both email texts (19550, 19555) to 3 days instead.

bugs.title: Re-inviting an agent who was removed leaves them removed, while the API answers 'invited'.
bugs.scenario: An admin removes an agent (status='removed') and later invites the same email again. The upsert only updates listing_cap/name/city/country, so status stays 'removed'; the agent never appears in the console (get_agency filters removed), imports count them as 'not on your roster', and first sign-in only activates rows that are 'invited'. The response still says status 'invited' and an invite email is sent.
bugs.fix: Add to the DO UPDATE: status = CASE WHEN agency_members.status='removed' THEN 'invited' ELSE agency_members.status END (same fix in estate_agents.bulk_onboard_agents), and return the row's real status.

bugs.title: The new tester cap counts invites from a table that nothing creates, and hides the error, so only already-granted testers are counted
bugs.scenario: TESTER-CAP-1 adds tester_invites rows to the count, but no code in the backend creates or writes that table (the tester allow-list is a file read by _review_emails). The SELECT raises, 'except Exception: pass' leaves _inv = 0, and the cap only counts people who already hold a tester_grant: with 4 invited and none granted yet, 4 further people can still be granted. If the table is ever added, a tester who claimed an invite and then got a grant is counted twice (once in each query), so the list reads 'full' at 2 real testers.
bugs.fix: Count ONE set of people: the union of tester_grant holders and the allow-list addresses from _review_emails(), excluding dmcontiki2* and @trustsquare.co, and refuse when that set (plus the new address) exceeds 4. Remove the tester_invites query, or create the table and exclude rows whose claimed_by already holds a grant; log instead of pass.

bugs.title: Internal comps mix rentals into sale medians and count AI examples and non-live adverts as market evidence
bugs.scenario: Once the column fault above is fixed, a 1T check on a house FOR SALE takes its median from every Property row in the city: rentals_only is only set when the subject is a rental, so R12 500/month rents sit beside R2 450 000 prices. AI example listings (is_demo / super_example / house accounts) and draft, archived or blocked adverts are counted too, and 'To Let' rentals are dropped from rental comps because the filter looks for the letters 'rent'. The buyer is charged 1T for 'VERIFIED MARKET DATA' built on that set; line 25459 fills a missing purchase price the same way.
bugs.evidence:
if rentals_only and "rent" not in ((r["lt"] or "").lower()):
_rentals = (tierkey == "property" and _is_rental_listing())
bugs.fix: Give _comp_amounts a deal argument (sale | rent): keep only rows whose listing_type matches the subject's deal (rent = /rent|let/), exclude rows matching _example_sql(), and require listing_status='live'. Apply the same rules in _comp_count so the chip is offered only when 8 true comparables exist.

bugs.title: The 'priced well below the verified market' warning never fires for prices saved by the app, because the asking price is parsed with a float() that fails on spaced thousands
bugs.scenario: The app stores prices as 'R1 250 000' (toLocaleString('en-ZA') puts a no-break space between thousands, and 'R12 500 / month' for rents). float() raises on the inner spaces, asking_zar stays None, price_caution returns None, so a R1 000 000 house listed at R300 000 against a verified R1 000 000 median gets no warning and no 'below_verified_market' verdict. yield-calc was fixed for the same format on 30 Sep (YIELD-READ-1); this parser was not.
bugs.evidence: asking_zar = float(str(price).replace("R", "").replace(",", "").strip())
bugs.fix: Replace the try block with asking_zar = _parse_money(price) (already defined at line 24797 and tolerant of spaces), or reuse the YIELD-READ-1 regex so 'R12 500 / month' reads as 12500.

bugs.title: Yield calculator decides 'rental' from the letters 'rent' anywhere in the title or description, so sale listings are treated as rentals (and 'Commercial Rental' as a sale)
bugs.scenario: A property with listing_type empty or 'Commercial Sale' whose description says 'current tenant', 'rental income' or 'parents' is classed as a rental: its R1 450 000 sale price becomes the MONTHLY RENT, the buyer is asked for a purchase price, and is charged 1T for a yield of several hundred percent. The reverse also happens: 'Commercial Rental' does not match \b(rent|let)\b, so its monthly rent is used as the purchase price.
bugs.evidence: is_rental = bool(re.search(r"\b(rent|let)\b", lt)) or ("rent" in (title + " " + desc).lower() and "for sale" not in lt)
bugs.fix: Decide from listing_type first: rental if it matches /rent|let|hire/ (substring, so 'Rental' counts), sale if it matches /sale/. Only when listing_type is empty fall back to the phrase test already used in _is_rental_listing ('for rent', 'to let', 'per month', 'monthly rent'). Refuse to compute when gross yield is outside 0.5%-40% and ask the user to confirm which figure is which.

bugs.title: SELF-REPLY-GUARD-1 does not stop the acknowledgement: our own system mail is still answered, and the AI call is still paid for
bugs.scenario: A system email from *.trustsquare.co lands on support@. The guard sets can_auto=False and status='system', but the later branch at line 26451 only tests category, fault_code and MAINT_ACK_SEND, so 'Thank you - we have your message' is mailed to our own bounce address. The guard also sits after _classify_email, so the AI call the guard was written to save has already been made.
bugs.fix: Compute _own = _is_own_system_mail(from_addr) at the top of _triage_message; when true skip _classify_email (use the fallback result) and add 'and not _own' to the acknowledgement branch at line 26451.

bugs.title: A prospect who replies 'unsubscribe' to an outreach email is only drafted for the queue; the address is never put on the suppression list
bugs.scenario: A tutor answers a wave email with 'remove me'. The classifier returns outreach_optout, the row is stored as 'drafted' with a reply that says we will not contact them again, and nothing else happens: _record_optout is only called from the /optout link route. The next wave or demand invite mails the same address again.
bugs.evidence:
"- outreach_optout: not interested, unsubscribe, remove me, stop emailing, or "
            status = "drafted"
            _update_triage_status(fault_code, status)
bugs.fix: In the outreach branch of _triage_message add: if category == 'outreach_optout': _record_optout(parseaddr(from_addr)[1], 'reply-optout') before the status update, and store status 'optout_recorded' so the queue shows it was applied.

bugs.title: When the sweep's email cap is reached the penalty, fade, removal or block still happens but the person is never told.
bugs.scenario: One counter (default 50) is shared by all lifecycle mails and the EULA 1.19 notices run first (line 28526), so until 12 Oct 2026 they can use the whole cap. After that _mail returns 'capped', yet the code has already stamped fade_nudge_sent_at, hidden the listing, written the -5 penalty, expired the introduction or blocked the seller. The seller gets no warning before her advert is hidden and the buyer is never told his request was closed. A failed send behaves the same, and the hourly reminder sweep advances reminder_stage on 'capped'/'failed' too (29924).
bugs.evidence:
if dry_run or sent[0] >= email_cap:
    return "capped"
conn.execute("UPDATE listings SET fade_nudge_sent_at=? WHERE id=?",
res["eula_notices"] = _eula_send_notices(conn, _mail, dry_run)
bugs.fix: Give the EULA notices their own counter; exempt notices that accompany a state change (penalty, removal, block, fade) from the cap; write fade_nudge_sent_at / reminder_stage only when the send returned 'sent' or 'skipped', and do not fade a listing whose warning never went out.

bugs.title: A buzz to a link-key account with no push device is reported as sent by email, but nothing is sent.
bugs.scenario: The receiver signed in with a private link (address ends @key.trustsquare.co, no inbox) and has no push subscription. devices is 0, the code sets channel 'email' and queues _send_html_email, which skips key identities (line 19306). The sender sees delivered: 'email' and the buzz never arrives - the silent outcome this endpoint promises not to have.
bugs.evidence:
channel = "email"
background_tasks.add_task(_send_html_email, receiver, "Buzz from " + name,
bugs.fix: Before queuing the mail, check _is_key_identity(receiver): if true and devices == 0, return delivered 'none' with a plain reason ('they have no way to receive a buzz yet') and log channel 'none'.

bugs.title: Un-pausing (and Keep live) puts a listing back to live without checking the plan's slot limit.
bugs.scenario: The publish guard counts only live listings (lines 5361-5366 and 11439-11445). A Free seller publishes 2, pauses both, publishes 2 more, then un-pauses the first two: 4 live adverts on a 2-slot plan, repeatable without end. keep-live does the same for faded adverts (30013).
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("UPDATE listings SET listing_status=?, status_changed_at=?, auto_paused_intro_id=NULL WHERE id=?",
             (want, now_iso, listing_id))
bugs.fix: In pause_listing (want == 'live') and keep_listing_live (faded -> live) count the seller's live listings against users.slot_limit (superusers exempt, same query as line 5361) and answer 409 with the slot message when full; or count paused listings in the publish guard.

bugs.title: Any 'N year old' in a brief is treated as a child, so cars and collectables get rewritten as 'a learner'.
bugs.scenario: 'Looking for a 3 year old Toyota Corolla' matches the last branch of _MINOR_RX, is flagged is_minor, and is stored and sent as 'Looking for a a learner Toyota Corolla' (tested; same for '12 year old single malt'). The buyer's brief is corrupted and marked as a child brief.
bugs.evidence:
|\b(\d{1,2})\s*(yr|yrs|years?)\s*old\b", re.I)
t = re.sub(r"\b(\d{1,2})[- ]?year[- ]?old\b", "a learner", t, flags=re.I)
bugs.fix: Only apply the minor test when the category is Tutors/Services (or the age is followed by son/daughter/child/boy/girl/learner, or preceded by my/our); leave bare ages alone in Cars, Collectors, Property and Travel.

bugs.title: Actor binding does not canonicalise case (suspicion a CONFIRMED): a typed address that equals the session address apart from case or spaces is passed through as typed
bugs.scenario: The gate rewrites only when _norm(typed) != session. Session is always lower-case (bea_main.py:8354). A page that remembers 'Bob@X.com' therefore reaches the handler as 'Bob@X.com'. Handlers that use the value as-is then miss: POST /advert-agent/coach looks up users WHERE email = ? and transactions WHERE user_email = ? (bea_main.py:10754, 10781) -> 'No TrustSquare seller account for Bob@X.com' or 402 'Insufficient Tuppence' on a funded wallet; POST /users stores a second, mixed-case users row (email is case-sensitive UNIQUE, bea_main.py:7385) so the person now has two rows.
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:396  if name in path_params and _norm(path_params[name]) != session:  ||  security_gate.py:401  if vals and any(_norm(v) != session for v in vals):  ||  security_gate.py:406  if cur not in (None, "") and _norm(cur) != session:
bugs.fix: Compare the raw value: rewrite whenever the typed value is not exactly the session string (path: path_params[name] != session; query/form: any(v != session ...); json: cur != session), so every bound parameter always arrives as the lower-case session email. For multipart keep the refusal only when _norm differs.

bugs.title: Choosing a budget band returns zero results because the chosen label is matched against bands rebuilt from the whole set, not the set it was offered from
bugs.scenario: Reproduced: Buy > Arcadia > 3 beds > Apartment > budget '1 000 000 - 2 000 000' returns total=0 and offers to drop 'Buy'. The option labels are built from the narrowed set, but once chosen the label is matched against bands rebuilt from ALL rows (rentals included), so no row carries it. Flag-dark today (baseline_q4); breaks the funnel the day it is armed.
bugs.evidence:
bfn, blabels = _price_band_factory(pre if "budget" not in chosen else rows)
...
budget["fn"], _ = _price_band_factory(remaining)
bugs.fix: Stop matching on a label: put the numeric bounds in the chip value (e.g. '1000000-2000000') and filter price_num against them; or, when 'budget' is in chosen, rebuild the bands from the same set the question was asked over (rows with budget's earlier chips applied) instead of `rows`.

bugs.title: Auto-collapsed chips come back from the client as ordinary chips and become hard filters, so widening returns too few (or zero) results
bugs.scenario: Rent > Hatfield: every match is an Apartment, so prop_type=Apartment (and a one-band budget 'Under 10 000') are auto-applied and returned in chips[]. ms.js stores all chips and resends them; when the user drops Hatfield the request still carries prop_type and budget, so the city-wide rent list shows 0 instead of 35 (reproduced).
bugs.evidence:
chosen[f["id"]] = v
auto.append({"facet": f["id"], "v": v, "label": _chip_label(f, v)})
bugs.fix: In ms.js _zoomChipStr() send only chips where auto is false (the engine re-derives auto chips every call); also skip auto-collapse for 'budget' so a single artificial band is never applied.

bugs.title: Credential claims hit UNIQUE(source, credential_id): the Tier-A displacement and a claim after someone else's rejected claim both end in a 500
bugs.scenario: (1) An ID-verified trainer claims a FIDE id that a Tier-B account holds: the holder row is only marked 'displaced', then a second row with the same (source, credential_id) is INSERTed -> sqlite3.IntegrityError -> 500 and rollback, after the holder was already notified. (2) A claim that staff 'rejected' is kept; the next account to claim that id reaches the else-branch, whose DELETE only removes 'displaced'/'revoked' rows, and the INSERT fails the same way - the credential is locked for everyone.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("UPDATE credential_claims SET status='displaced', reviewed_at=? WHERE id=?", (now, holder["id"]))
...
conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential_claims (user_id, email, source, credential_id, ...) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
bugs.fix: In the displacement branch and for any holder whose status is not active/pending, reuse the row: `UPDATE credential_claims SET user_id=?, email=?, claimed_name=?, tier=?, status=?, similarity=?, claimed_at=?, reviewed_at=NULL, reviewed_by=NULL WHERE id=?` (keep history in a separate log if needed), and send the displaced notice only after commit.

bugs.title: Any failure in the Google or Apple callback leaves the person on a raw JSON error page (or a 500) instead of back in the app.
bugs.scenario: The callback is a top-level browser navigation, but _oauth_complete raises HTTPException for an expired state, a missing or overwritten ts_oauth_nonce cookie (two sign-in tabs, or choosing the account again after pressing Back), a refused code or a provider outage, and _pyjwt.decode errors in _oauth_verify_id_token are not caught at all. The person sees {"detail":"That sign-in attempt expired. Please tap the button again."} with no button to tap.
bugs.evidence: _out, nxt = _oauth_complete("google", code, state, resp, request.cookies.get("ts_oauth_nonce"))
bugs.fix: Wrap the _oauth_complete call in both callbacks (19857, 19873) in try/except (HTTPException, _pyjwt.PyJWTError, Exception): log it and return RedirectResponse('/?go=signin&oauth=failed', 302) so the app's own sign-in screen opens with a plain message.

bugs.title: The draft photo route rebuilds the photo strip from photo_urls alone, wiping photos and captions that were added through /listings/photo
bugs.scenario: A draft got five photos through POST /listings/photo (which writes only the [photos:url::caption|...] prefix; photo_urls stays NULL). The seller resumes it in the guided flow, which uploads through /listings/{id}/photo/draft: photo_urls is read as empty, the new URL is appended, and the whole prefix is replaced with '[photos:<new>]' and the cover with the new photo. The five earlier photos disappear from the advert; captions are always dropped.
bugs.fix: Seed existing_photo_urls from the existing prefix when photo_urls is empty (parse entries, keep 'url::caption' text per URL), append the new URL to that list, and write the prefix back with captions preserved; re-read the description after the upload rather than using the row read before the scan.

bugs.title: create_user stores the email exactly as typed, so 'John@x.com' becomes a second users row beside the session's 'john@x.com'
bugs.scenario: The gate only rewrites the body email when it differs from the session after lower-casing, so a capitalised spelling of the caller's own address (phone keyboards capitalise the first letter) reaches the handler unchanged. users.email is UNIQUE case-sensitively, so INSERT OR IGNORE adds a duplicate account row and credits it. Later reads use `WHERE email = ?` in some places and `WHERE LOWER(email)=?` in others, so EULA acceptance, slot limit and profile can be read from different rows.
bugs.evidence:
result = conn.execute(
    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO users (email, name) VALUES (?,?)",
    (user.email, user.name)
)
bugs.fix: Normalise first: `user.email = (user.email or '').strip().lower()` (400 if empty/invalid) before the INSERT, and run a one-off merge of existing case-variant rows; add a unique index on LOWER(email).

bugs.title: Closing an account leaves its adverts live and its open introductions running.
bugs.scenario: A seller closes her account (DELETE /users/{email}). account_closure.close_account moves the wallet, bumps session_version and stamps closed_at, and nothing else: her listings stay 'live', buyers can still request introductions and have 1T held for up to 96 hours for a seller who is gone, and a pending request she made as a buyer can still be accepted and burned after she left.
bugs.evidence:
result = account_closure.close_account(conn, email, closure_type, cause)
account_closure.py:130  conn.execute("UPDATE users SET closed_at=? WHERE lower(email)=?", (_now(), email))
bugs.fix: In close_user_account, inside the same transaction: set the account's live listings to 'paused' or 'archived'; for each pending intro_request on those listings and each pending request where she is the buyer, set status 'withdrawn' and call _release_intro_hold and _commitment_resume. Also force closure_type='user' and cause=None for callers without the admin key - today a user can record her own closure as breach B5.

bugs.title: The no-category breakdown call writes the primary-category score onto every listing of the seller, overwriting the per-category badges
bugs.scenario: A seller has a Tutors advert and a Services advert with different category credentials. Any call without ?category= that finds a changed score (the trust hub, trust_employer_confirm, trust_experience, admin uphold) sets listings.trust_score for ALL her adverts to the primary-category score; the edit screen (15061), the buyer panel (7649) and CRED-SCORE-SYNC-1 (15171) then write per-category values back. The badge on a card flips with whichever screen ran last - the bug class TRUST-ONE-SET-1 set out to end.
bugs.evidence:
"UPDATE listings SET trust_score = ? WHERE LOWER(seller_email) = LOWER(?)",
            (score_total, email)
bugs.fix: Replace this UPDATE with the per-listing loop already written for CRED-SCORE-SYNC-1 (score each distinct category/service_class with _trust_evidence and write only that category's rows); keep users.trust_score as the primary-category value.

bugs.title: The admin photo re-scan (apply=1 by default) permanently strips a listing's photos when the scan merely could not run.
bugs.scenario: An admin re-scans a listing while the AI lane is down, the seller's or platform's daily AI ceiling is reached, or a photo fetch times out. _anon_photo_pass reports those as held ('ai-ceiling', 'scan-failed', 'fetch-failed'), the handler treats every held photo as 'removed', and with apply=1 it writes thumb_url/medium_url NULL and drops the photo strip from the description. A live advert loses all its pictures although nothing was found wrong with them.
bugs.fix: Split the notes into 'not anonymous' (flyer-or-unsafe, not-anonymous, needs-replacement, redact-unverified, inappropriate, low-confidence) and 'could not check' (ai-ceiling, scan-failed, dns/fetch/http errors, upload-failed). If any photo is in the second group, do not write the row: return applied=false with the reason so the admin re-runs later.

bugs.title: A fare refresh run without the supplier token marks every cached route 'none', hiding all good fares, and reports a clean run
bugs.scenario: Reproduced: refresh() started where TRAVELPAYOUTS_TOKEN is not in the environment (cron, or the unit not exporting .env): _tp_fetch returns None before any call, refresh() treats None as 'thin route' and sets status='none' on all 10 routes; get_indicative then answers 'no indicative fare cached' for fares fetched yesterday. Result line shows failed: 0.
bugs.evidence:
if not TOKEN:
        return None
...
ON CONFLICT(origin,destination,currency) DO UPDATE SET
                               status='none', fetched_at=excluded.fetched_at
bugs.fix: Raise in _tp_fetch when TOKEN is empty or the body has success=false (so refresh counts it as failed and leaves the cache alone); only overwrite an 'ok' row with 'none' when the supplier answered success=true with empty data.

bugs.title: Bulk agency onboarding throws away the credential numbers it was given; ops gets a pending claim with nothing to verify
bugs.scenario: An agency uploads ppra_number, ffc_year, asata_number, cipc_number etc. _cred_pending stores only signal_id + 'pending' (no notes/evidence), so GET /trust-score/credentials/pending shows the claim with evidence_url and notes NULL and the number is lost.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("""INSERT INTO user_credentials (email, signal_id, status, listing_category, updated_at)
                        VALUES (?,?,'pending','Property',?)""", (email, signal_id, _now()))
bugs.fix: Pass the submitted value into _cred_pending and store it in user_credentials.notes (e.g. 'agency claim: ppra_number=...'); derive listing_category from the signal prefix instead of hardcoding 'Property'.

bugs.title: The plain-text filter deletes everything between a '<' and the next '>' in titles, prices, descriptions and messages
bugs.scenario: A buyer writes 'budget <R5000 but >R3000 ok' or a seller writes 'rooms <10 m2 ... -> call me'. _pt() treats '<R5000 but >' as a tag and removes it, so the other side reads 'budget R3000 ok' - the meaning is reversed with no warning; the match also runs across line breaks. When the owner edits and saves, the shortened text is stored for good. Verified on the module: description 'budget <R5000 but >R3000 ok' -> 'budget R3000 ok'.
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:605-606  if "<" in v or ">" in v:\n            v = re.sub(r"<[^>]*>", "", v).replace("<", "\u2039").replace(">", "\u203a")
bugs.fix: Do not delete: only neutralise. Replace the re.sub with the two character swaps ('<' -> U+2039, '>' -> U+203A), or strip only real tags with r'</?[A-Za-z][^<>]*>'. Apply the same change to _plain_text() at bea_main.py:30763.

bugs.title: A top-up can be paid and then refused, because the price is worked out again at verify time from a rate that may have changed.
bugs.scenario: Checkout charges tuppence x $2 at the live rate (say R17.20, so R34 for 1T). Before verify runs the process restarts and both rate feeds fail, so fx_rates_sync falls back to the fixed R18.50: the handler now needs 95% of R37 = R35.15, the R34 paid is 'not enough', verify answers 400 and the webhook answers 200 without crediting (line 10018). The buyer has paid and holds nothing.
bugs.evidence:
if tuppence <= 0 or not _paystack_paid_enough(result["data"], usd_to_zar_amount(tuppence * 2), reference):
    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="The amount paid does not match this top-up.")
bugs.fix: At /payment/initialize store one row per payment (reference, account email, tuppence, amount in cents). At verify and in the webhook compare Paystack's amount with that stored amount instead of a recomputed price, and take the email and tuppence from that row instead of from metadata.

bugs.title: A seller who pays for a plan and does not come back through the redirect is charged and gets no plan, because the Paystack webhook only credits Tuppence.
bugs.scenario: Seller pays R90 for Starter and closes the tab or loses signal before the callback page calls /payment/seller-subscription/verify. The webhook receives charge.success, finds tuppence 0 in the metadata, credits nothing and answers 200, so Paystack does not retry. The plan is never applied.
bugs.evidence:
tuppence  = int(metadata.get("tuppence", 0) or 0)
if (tuppence > 0 or ai_sessions > 0) and not _claim_payment_ref(conn, reference, "tuppence"):
bugs.fix: In paystack_webhook, when metadata.get('type') == 'seller_subscription', run the same apply step as verify_seller_subscription (move lines 10199-10263 into one helper that takes the verified data dict) under the 'seller_subscription' claim; do the same for wishlist_global payments.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.

bugs.title: The 'is_downgrade' flag and tier are taken from Paystack metadata and switch off the amount check; the hourly worker then applies that tier without checking it is lower
bugs.scenario: The code's own PAY-AMOUNT-1 note says metadata is set by whoever starts the transaction (the merchant public key is visible to every payer on Paystack's checkout). A transaction for R1 with metadata {type:'seller_subscription', tier:'pro', email:<self>, is_downgrade:true} passes verify (amount check skipped), sets pending_downgrade_tier='pro', and _apply_pending_downgrades() makes the account Pro at billing_period_end. The same flag with a victim's email schedules a downgrade for somebody else.
bugs.evidence: bea_main.py:10212  if not is_downgrade and not _paystack_paid_enough(result["data"], plan["amount_rands"], reference):  ||  bea_main.py:1905  "UPDATE users SET seller_tier=?, slot_limit=?, pending_downgrade_tier=NULL "
bugs.fix: Never read is_downgrade from metadata: recompute it in verify from the account's current seller_tier (downgrade only if the paid tier ranks below it), always run _paystack_paid_enough for the tier being bought, and have _apply_pending_downgrades skip a pending tier that is not lower than the current one.
bugs.lead: Found independently by two reviewers.

bugs.title: The AI Coach charges 1T, or uses up the one free session, when the AI reply could not be read and the seller gets an empty result.
bugs.scenario: The model's JSON is cut off at max_tokens 1800 or wrapped in text. Both parse attempts fail, coaching_json becomes {} with empty defaults, and the code goes straight on to mark aa_free_used = 1 or deduct 1T. The seller pays for a coaching screen with nothing on it.
bugs.fix: After parsing, if coaching_json is not a dict or has neither 'fields' nor 'trust_score_actions' content, close the connection and raise HTTPException(502, 'AI Coach unavailable - you were not charged') before lines 11035-11046. Also claim the free use atomically before the AI call (UPDATE users SET aa_free_used=1 WHERE ... AND COALESCE(aa_free_used,0)=0, checked by rowcount, undone on failure): today parallel first calls all run free.

bugs.title: The no-show credit is issued per upheld complaint and is not tied to what the seller actually paid
bugs.scenario: A Local Market seller pays once per listing (1T, or 2T boosted, on her first accept) but may report every accepted introduction. Three upheld no-shows on one listing credit 3T against 1T paid, and a seller whose charge was waived (burn switch off) is credited 1T for nothing. Two simultaneous uphold calls also both pass the status check and apply the penalty and credit twice.
bugs.evidence:
credit_amount = LM_INTRO_COST_T
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO transactions (user_email, type, amount, description) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
bugs.fix: Credit only when this listing has an lm_intro_deduct / lm_boost_deduct row and no earlier lm_credit, and credit the amount charged; make the status change 'UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status="pending"' first and act only when rowcount == 1.

bugs.title: A seller keeps paid multi-city reach after moving to the Free plan, because no downgrade removes the listing_cities rows.
bugs.scenario: A seller pays for Starter for one month, extends a listing to many cities (the tier is checked only when a row is inserted), then downgrades. downgrade_to_free and _plan_changed only rebalance listing slots, and the browse queries (3776, 3948) join listing_cities with no tier check, so the Free seller's listing stays shown in every extended city indefinitely.
bugs.evidence:
"UPDATE users SET seller_tier='free', slot_limit=?, pending_downgrade_tier=NULL WHERE LOWER(email)=?",
            (free_limit, email)
        )
        res = _plan_changed(conn, email, "free", lowered=True)
bugs.fix: In _plan_changed, when new_tier is not in _PAID_TIERS, run DELETE FROM listing_cities WHERE listing_id IN (SELECT id FROM listings WHERE LOWER(seller_email)=?) - or, to keep her choices for a later upgrade, add a seller-tier condition to the listing_cities joins at 3776 and 3948.

bugs.title: An AI hold that is never settled is never given back.
bugs.scenario: /tuppence/ai-commit writes a negative ai_hold row; only /tuppence/ai-settle turns it into a burn or a release. If the AdvertAgent service crashes, times out or is redeployed between the two calls, the row stays ai_hold for ever and the user's Tuppence is gone with nothing delivered. Nothing in the file sweeps old holds.
bugs.evidence: (email, "ai_hold", -amount, f"AI feature hold \u00b7 {function_id} \u00b7 job {job_id}"))
bugs.fix: Add a sweep (the hourly loop is the natural place) that releases ai_hold rows older than a safe limit, e.g. 30 minutes, exactly as the 'failed' branch of ai-settle does (type -> ai_hold_released plus an ai_release row).

bugs.title: The Global-to-Starter fold gives Starter with no end date, although it is meant to last only until the paid reach expires.
bugs.scenario: When baseline_q4 is armed every live $5 Global buyer is set to seller_tier 'starter' with billing_period_end = the reach expiry, but pending_downgrade_tier is left empty. The only job that ends a tier (_apply_pending_downgrades, line 1896) acts only on rows with a pending downgrade, so a single 30-day $5 payment keeps 10 slots and global reach for ever.
bugs.evidence: conn.execute("UPDATE users SET seller_tier='starter', slot_limit=?, billing_period_end=COALESCE(billing_period_end, ?) WHERE LOWER(email)=?",
bugs.fix: In the fold also set pending_downgrade_tier='free' for accounts that had no paid seller plan, so the hourly plan loop returns them to Free when billing_period_end passes (a renewal clears it, as line 10255 already does).

bugs.title: The monthly Tuppence grant is keyed on the calendar month while the plan runs 30 days from payment, so two payments in one calendar month give one grant
bugs.scenario: A Starter/Pro seller pays on 1 October (period '2026-10' granted) and renews 30 days later on 31 October: period is '2026-10' again, INSERT OR IGNORE inserts nothing and the function returns None - she paid for a second month and received no allocation for it. The same happens to a Starter who upgrades to Pro in the same month: she gets 2T, not Pro's 10T.
bugs.evidence: launch_redemption.py:240  period = period or datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m")  ||  launch_redemption.py:247-248  if cur.rowcount == 0:\n        return None  # already granted this period
bugs.fix: Key the grant on the payment, not the month: pass the Paystack reference (or paid_at date) as the period key from verify_seller_subscription, and on a same-period upgrade credit the difference between the new tier's allocation and what was already granted.

bugs.title: Rent/price benchmark lookups silently return the national default for any unlisted place, and the buyer is charged 1T for it as an 'area' figure
bugs.scenario: US listing in New York with suburb 'Brooklyn': bea_main looks up suburb first, us_area('Brooklyn') misses the 10-city table and returns the $1,700 default labelled 'HUD Fair Market Rent ... area FMR', although New York is $2,730; the 1T 'Verified yield' is computed and charged on it. Same for uk_region (keyed by region, queried by city) and za_city ('Typical asking prices in Stellenbosch' = national default).
bugs.evidence:
rec = us["areas"].get(_norm(area), us["default"])
rec = uk["regions"].get(_norm(region), uk["default"])
bugs.fix: Return {} (so the resolvers return None and nothing is charged) when the place is not in the table, or add 'is_default': True and have tier_resolvers label it 'national benchmark' and refuse it for 1T; in bea_main._yield_fill_missing try city when the suburb misses.

bugs.title: An unsubscribe is written only to the CityLauncher database, while the backend's own invite sender checks a different ledger, so an opted-out address can still be mailed
bugs.scenario: A prospect confirms /optout and is told 'We will not email this address again'. _record_optout writes the CityLauncher suppression table only. The demand-invite sender (_demand_match_and_compose, line 12229) excludes addresses only by outreach_ledger.suppressed in the main database, which /optout never writes, so once the demand loop is switched on that prospect is still eligible for an invite.
bugs.evidence:
conn = _sq.connect(_OPTOUT_DB, timeout=15)
...
conn.execute("INSERT INTO suppression (email, source) VALUES (?,?) "
bugs.fix: In _record_optout, after the CityLauncher write, also insert into the main database: INSERT INTO outreach_ledger (email_hash, channel, campaign, suppressed) VALUES (sha256(addr)[:32], 'optout', source, 1) - the same hash shape the import uses at line 893 - and return True only when both writes landed.

bugs.title: The contact-detail scrub covers only title and description; price, suburb, area, availability and the other free-text fields go live unscrubbed
bugs.scenario: E2E-HMI-1 closed 'phone me on 082 555 1234' in the description. The same seller now types it in another field: POST/PUT /listings with price='R500 - call 082 555 1234' or area='WhatsApp 0825551234' is stored as sent and shown on the card, so buyers reach the seller without an introduction. Suburb values from any draft are also offered to every other seller through GET /suburbs.
bugs.evidence:
listing.title, listing.description, _scrubbed = _private_text_scrub(
    listing.title, listing.description, listing.seller_email or "", "create")   # E2E-HMI-1
bugs.fix: Run _plain_text + _anon_regex_clean over every buyer-visible free-text field in create_listing and update_listing (price, suburb, area, availability, subject, level, mode, service_type, variant, colour, make, model, condition, collectible_type), and have GET /suburbs read suburbs from live listings only.

bugs.title: The take-down link tells the seller 'Your photographs have been deleted' while most of them stay public
bugs.scenario: A seller with eight photos taps the withdraw link. Only photo_urls, thumb_url and medium_url are collected, but photos uploaded through /listings/photo live only in the [photos:...] description prefix (photo_urls is NULL), so seven of eight objects are never deleted and the prefix itself stays in the row. Every object is also mirrored to /var/www/marketsquare/media/<key> (served at /media/), and that copy is never removed. With no failures counted, the page confirms deletion.
bugs.evidence:
for u in list(_urls) + [row["thumb_url"], row["medium_url"]]:
...
_s3.delete_object(Bucket=HETZNER_S3_BUCKET, Key=k)
...
note = ("Your photographs have been deleted." if failed == 0 else
bugs.fix: Also parse the [photos:url::caption|...] prefix into the key list, strip the prefix from description in the UPDATE, and delete the local mirror file (os.remove under _LOCAL_MEDIA_DIR, path-confined) for each key; count a photo as deleted only when both copies are gone. Give DELETE /listings/{id}/seller the same storage clean-up - today it deletes the row and leaves every photo public.

bugs.title: Listing create and edit accept any image URL from the browser (thumb_url, medium_url, photo_urls), so a seller can show buyers a photo that never passed the anonymity scan
bugs.scenario: The fail-closed photo gate (plates, signage, phone numbers) runs only inside the upload routes. A seller then sends PUT /listings/{id} with photo_urls='["https://her-host/card-with-phone.jpg"]' (or thumb_url on POST /listings): the URLs are stored, written into the [photos:] prefix and shown to every buyer. The image can also be swapped at the remote host after publishing. Only quick-publish strips these fields (AUDIT-Q2).
bugs.evidence:
_new_urls = [u for u in (_new_urls or []) if isinstance(u, str) and u.strip()]
...
_prefix = "[photos:" + "|".join(u + ("::" + _caps[u] if u in _caps else "") for u in _new_urls) + "]"
d.setdefault("thumb_url", _new_urls[0])
bugs.fix: In create_listing and update_listing accept an image URL only when it starts with R2_PUBLIC_URL + '/' or the local media base (LOCAL_MEDIA_URL), contains none of '|', ']' or '::', and reject (400) anything else; apply the same test to thumb_url and medium_url.

bugs.title: Two public routes answer questions about any typed email: whether it is a TrustSquare seller with an ID on file, and whether it is registered at all.
bugs.scenario: GET /users/{email}/id-status has level public and no binding: an anonymous caller learns for any address whether an ID is pending, on file or Home Affairs verified. POST /advert-agent/market-note (public) answers 401 'Unrecognised account' for an unknown address and 200 for a registered one, and books the AI spend and the daily per-user ceiling against the typed address, so a stranger can use up a seller's AI allowance for the day.
bugs.fix: route_policy.json: make GET /users/{email}/id-status level 'user' with bind email in path (ms.js 8820 and 23459 need credentials:'include'). In aa_market_note take the account from _session_email(ts_user) as draft-from-photo does at line 10659 and drop the typed-email existence check.

bugs.title: The coach's publish door stores any photo it cannot decode exactly as uploaded, with no anonymity check.
bugs.scenario: A seller uploads a file PIL cannot open on this server (an AVIF, or a HEIC where the HEIF plug-in is missing) showing her phone number or number plate. Image.open raises, the broad except keeps raw_data, and the file is stored and set as the advert's photo without ever reaching _seller_photo_anon_gate. Every other photo door refuses or skips such a file.
bugs.fix: Replace the fallback with a skip: append 'photo%d:held:could not be read' to _anon_notes and continue, exactly as the HTTPException branch at 11374-11376 does. Never store raw_data. Also cap the list (for example photos[:12]), since each photo is one paid vision call.

bugs.title: Deleting a document removes only the database row; the ID or certificate file stays in the private store and the credential it earned stays earned.
bugs.scenario: A seller deletes her uploaded ID photo. delete_seller_document deletes the seller_documents row and nothing else: no code in the back end ever removes a file under the private store, so the image stays on the server and remains readable by any admin or enrolled device at the same /private-docs/ URL. The credential the upload earned is also left in user_credentials, so the score keeps points for evidence that is no longer listed.
bugs.evidence: conn.execute("DELETE FROM seller_documents WHERE id=?", (doc_id,))
bugs.fix: Select url and signal_id with the row; after the DELETE, if url starts with '/private-docs/' call os.remove(_private_path(url[len('/private-docs/'):])) inside try/except, and set the matching user_credentials row back to 'missing' (delete it) when no other document of this seller carries that signal_id.

bugs.title: The stored ID hash is an unsalted SHA-256 of the digits only, so a South African ID number is recoverable from it and passport numbers that differ only in letters collide.
bugs.scenario: users.id_number_hash and id_verification_ledger.id_hash hold sha256(digits). A 13-digit SA ID has roughly a billion valid values, so anyone holding the database or a backup recovers every ID number in seconds - the 'never store the raw number' rule is not met. Separately, re.sub(r"\D", ...) strips letters (the .upper() after it shows they were meant to stay), so passports A1234567 and B1234567 hash the same and the second person is refused by the NPR duplicate check as 'already registered to a different account'.
bugs.evidence:
normalised = re.sub(r"\D", "", id_number).upper()
    return hashlib.sha256(normalised.encode()).hexdigest()
bugs.fix: Normalise with re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z]", "", id_number).upper() and replace the bare hash with hmac.new(ID_HASH_KEY, normalised.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest(), where ID_HASH_KEY is a server-only secret read through ai_provider.envkey; existing hashes cannot be converted, so keep a legacy lookup for old rows.

bugs.title: The agency console returns the real name, trust score, listing counts, intro count, tier and credentials of ANY email the admin has merely invited.
bugs.scenario: An agency admin invites someone's email (no consent needed), then calls GET /agencies/{id}. The member list includes status 'invited' rows and _agency_agent_rollup reads users.name, trust_score, live/draft listing counts, intro_requests count, seller_tier and credential statuses for that address. A stranger with a console link can therefore confirm that a given email is a TrustSquare seller and read the account name and activity before that person has agreed to anything.
bugs.evidence:
"WHERE agency_id=? AND status!='removed' ORDER BY role DESC, agent_email", (agency_id,)).fetchall()
            r = _agency_agent_rollup(conn, m["agent_email"])
"name": (u["name"] if u and u["name"] else email.split("@")[0]),
bugs.fix: For members whose status is 'invited' return only {email, agent_name as typed by the agency, status, listing_cap}; run _agency_agent_rollup only for status='active' (joined by their own sign-in).

bugs.title: The agency import anonymises only title and description; price text, area, suburb, city and about 15 other free-text fields are stored exactly as sent.
bugs.scenario: A feed row carries price 'R1.2m - call Sipho 082 555 1234', area '12 Kerk Street, Sasolburg' or availability 'Phone Acme Realty 011 ...'. Those values go straight into the draft (area/suburb/price uncapped, the _imp_s fields up to 160 characters, vehicle_specs up to 4000) without _anon_regex_clean, and the row is not flagged needs_review, so the agent can publish a draft that identifies the agency.
bugs.evidence:
_imp_vals = [t_clean, _price_txt,
                         str(ad.get("category") or "Property"), city,
                         str(ad.get("area") or city), str(ad.get("suburb") or city),
_price_txt = str(ad.get("price") or "POA")
_imp_s("service_class"), _imp_s("service_type"), _imp_s("availability"),
bugs.fix: Run every free-text import field (price text, city, area, suburb and all _imp_s values, plus string values inside vehicle_specs) through _anon_regex_clean, cap their length, and set row_needs_review when any of them produced a hit.

bugs.title: POST /buzz/pair trusts a client-supplied 'source', which switches on the name display for any typed email address.
bugs.scenario: A signed-in user posts {to_email: anyone@example.com, source: 'reference'} and then reads GET /buzz/pairs. Because the pair's source is 'reference', other_name is the registered name of that address even though that person never agreed to anything. This is the name lookup the 24 Sep fix was written to stop.
bugs.evidence:
(a, b, me, req.source or "link", me))
if (v["they_allow_me"] or (v.get("source") in ("regular-link", "reference")))
bugs.fix: Ignore req.source on the public route: always store 'link' (the server-side flows at line 15363 and in ripple_features write 'reference' / 'regular-link' themselves).

bugs.title: The Buzz email fallback puts the sender's real email address in Reply-To, which the 29 Sep anonymity rule says must stay on the server.
bugs.scenario: A customer joined a seller's Buzz link; the seller has no push device, so the buzz goes by email with Reply-To set to the customer's address. The seller now holds the customer's email although BUZZ-ANON-1 (RUL-171(d), 29 Sep) removed addresses from every Buzz screen. Only the receiver's switch is checked, not 'both sides', as the comment claims. This line follows the earlier BUZZ-REPLY-1 note (27 Sep); the two rulings conflict and the later one is not applied here.
bugs.evidence:
background_tasks.add_task(_send_html_email, receiver, "Buzz from " + name,
                          None if _is_key_identity(sender) else sender)
bugs.fix: Send without the sender's address (default support reply-to) and say in the mail 'open Buzz to answer'; or set Reply-To only when the pair's source is one where both already hold each other's address. This changes BUZZ-REPLY-1, so it needs David's yes.

bugs.title: The child-brief minimiser leaves the child's name and Afrikaans-style school names in the text.
bugs.scenario: 'My son Thabo is in grade 8 at Hoërskool Waterkloof' becomes 'a learner Thabo is in grade 8 at Hoërskool Waterkloof' (tested). That text is stored, sent to the AI provider, and goes to sellers whenever the template brief or the buyer's own text is used. The name is only removed after the words named/called, and a school only when capitalised words come BEFORE School/High/Laerskool.
bugs.evidence:
t = re.sub(r"\b(my|our)\s+(son|daughter|child|kid|boy|girl)\b", "a learner", t, flags=re.I)
t = re.sub(r"\s*\b(named|called|name is)\s+[A-Z][\w'-]+", "", t)
bugs.fix: After 'my son/daughter/child' also drop the following capitalised word(s); extend _SCHOOL_RX to '(Laerskool|Hoërskool|Primary|High|College|Academy)\s+[A-Z]\w+(\s+[A-Z]\w+)*'; and never fall back to the buyer's raw words for a minor brief - use the chips-only template.

bugs.title: Agent profile anonymisation covers only headline and bio; city, suburbs, specialties and languages go to the public list unfiltered
bugs.scenario: An agent (or an agency roster) puts 'Call 082 555 1234 - Jane, Acme Realty' in specialties or suburbs. /agents/nearby and /agents/pitch (public) return it verbatim, so the seller phones the agent directly: the 'no name, no agency brand, no contact' rule and the 1T lead fee are both bypassed.
bugs.evidence:
(head, bio, p.years_experience, p.properties_sold, sold_source,
             (p.city or "").strip(), (p.suburbs or "").strip(), (p.specialties or "").strip(),
             (p.languages or "").strip(), ...
bugs.fix: Run city, suburbs, specialties and languages through _anon() in _upsert_profile (both INSERT and UPDATE branches) and cap their length; reject the save if the stripper reports hits.

bugs.title: Private-field stripping is switched off for a whole object (and everything nested in it) as soon as ANY of seven email keys equals the caller - including buyer_email
bugs.scenario: _scrub() returns the object untouched when seller_email, email, owner_email, agent_email, admin_email, buyer_email or user_email equals the session. So an introduction or match object that carries the caller as buyer_email keeps the SELLER's hidden keys, and a wrapper such as {'email': <caller>, 'results': [other people's records]} keeps every nested street_address. Verified on the module: _scrub({'buyer_email':'me','seller_email':'s','street_address':'1 Main'}, hide, 'me') returns all three keys. Also: GLOBAL_PRIVATE_KEYS are only added on public/token/reviewer/device routes, so a signed-in stranger on a 'user' route with no hide list gets no stripping at all.
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:545-546  if session and any(_norm(obj.get(k)) == session for k in _OWNER_KEYS if obj.get(k)):\n            return obj                          # the caller's own record: untouched
bugs.fix: Exempt only on the key that names the record's owner for that route (add an optional 'owner_key' to the policy entry, default seller_email/email), never on buyer_email, and still recurse into nested lists/dicts of an exempt wrapper. Add GLOBAL_PRIVATE_KEYS for level 'user' as well.

bugs.title: Quick one-tap save hands a signed-in session to any stranger who types an unused @key.trustsquare.co address (no inbox proof, bypasses EMAIL-ANCHOR-1)
bugs.scenario: A signed-out caller POSTs /listings/quick-publish with email 'w-anything@key.trustsquare.co'. No account exists, so a users row is created for that typed address, and because _is_key_identity(em) is true the answer carries open_url=_mint_signin_url(em,...) - a working sign-in token. The stranger now holds a signed-in account with no reachable inbox, which LINK_KEY_NEW_ON=False and AUDIT-Q1 ('an email save is never signed in by a typed address') were written to prevent.
bugs.fix: Refuse a typed address in the key domain: after em is computed in the else-branch add `if not sess and _is_key_identity(em): raise HTTPException(400, 'Please type an email address we can reach you on.')`, and change the hand-back test at line 4851 to `if sess and _is_key_identity(em):`.

bugs.title: Status card reads its picture from a path built out of the listing's client-set thumb_url/medium_url, so '../' reaches any image file on the server
bugs.scenario: A seller saves thumb_url='https://x/static/../../../lib/trustsquare-private/ids/id_<name>.jpg' (POST or PUT /listings accept any string), publishes, then fetches the public GET /listings/{id}/status-card.png. status_card._role_picture joins everything after '/static/' onto STATIC_DIR without normalising, opens the file with Pillow and pastes it into the PNG. Any image the app process can read - including private ID documents and certificates when their file name is known - is served publicly, bypassing /private-docs/.
bugs.evidence:
png = status_card.render(l, link, make, first_name=first_name, trust=trust)
# status_card.py:45
if u and "/static/" in u:
    cands.append(os.path.join(STATIC_DIR, u.split("/static/", 1)[1].split("?")[0]))
bugs.fix: In status_card._role_picture resolve and confine the path: `p = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(STATIC_DIR, rel)); if not p.startswith(os.path.realpath(STATIC_DIR) + os.sep): continue`. Also stop accepting free-form thumb_url/medium_url on listing writes (see the image-URL finding).

bugs.title: Any draft can be archived and its photos permanently deleted by a stranger who knows the seller's email (GET /listings/{id}/withdraw legacy lane), and no code ever mints the signed token that was meant to replace it
bugs.scenario: GET /listings/123/withdraw?email=victim@x.com&confirm=1 with no token: for a draft, _legacy_ok is true on the address alone, so the row is archived and its photos are deleted from object storage - irreversible. Listing ids are sequential. Meanwhile _withdraw_link_token() has no caller anywhere, so the signed lane the comment describes is unused and a live advert has no working take-down link at all.
bugs.fix: Have every recovery letter build its link with _withdraw_link_token(listing_id, seller_email), then close the legacy lane (drop _legacy_ok, or limit it to drafts created before 24 Sep 2026 so already-posted letters still work).

bugs.title: Wearable registration stores any URL as push_endpoint and the server later POSTs to it (blind SSRF)
bugs.scenario: POST /wishlist/wearable/register needs no sign-in for an unlinked token. A caller registers push_endpoint pointing at an internal address (for example a service listening on 127.0.0.1, such as the self-hosted n8n) plus an explicit signal that matches common adverts; each time a matching advert is published the server's pywebpush call POSTs to that internal address.
bugs.evidence:
if not req.push_endpoint or not req.push_keys:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="push_endpoint and push_keys required")
bugs.fix: Accept only https endpoints whose host is a known push service (fcm.googleapis.com, updates.push.services.mozilla.com, *.push.apple.com, *.notify.windows.com) and bound the length; reject everything else with 400.

bugs.title: The Local Market publish gate is skipped by a different letter case in the typed email, and a first suspension does not block a new advert
bugs.scenario: A permanently banned seller signed in as bob@x.com posts seller_email 'Bob@x.com': the gate leaves it (equal after lowercasing), _lm_is_banned / _lm_active_suspension run case-sensitive lookups on the raw value and find nothing, and the advert is published under the lowercased address. Separately, a seller under a first suspension (no cooling-off yet) passes the check, and her new advert is inserted with suspension_reason NULL, so it is public while her older ones are hidden.
bugs.evidence: err = _lm_check_seller_can_publish(conn, listing.seller_email)
bugs.fix: Pass _lm_seller (lowercased two lines above) and compare LOWER(email)/LOWER(seller_email) in the helpers; treat any active suspension row as a refusal (or insert the new advert with the same suspension_reason).

bugs.title: The Local Market intro door has no self-intro guard and no one-pending-request guard, so a seller can farm 'successful introductions' on her own advert
bugs.scenario: A seller requests an introduction on her own Local Market listing (free for the buyer) and accepts it; POST /intros refuses this ('You cannot request an introduction to your own listing') but /local-market/intro does not. Twenty self-accepted requests cost her 1T once and earn track_record.intro_1/5/20 = +15 Trust points, because intro_count at 14588 counts every accepted intro. The same buyer can also stack up to 10 pending requests a day on one listing (INTRO-ONCE-1 is missing here).
bugs.evidence:
cur = conn.execute(
        """INSERT INTO intro_requests
             (listing_id, buyer_email, buyer_name, message, intro_type)
bugs.fix: Before the INSERT add the two guards create_intro has: refuse when the buyer is the listing's seller, and refuse a second pending request from the same buyer on the same listing; in _compute_universal_track_status count only intros whose buyer is not the seller.

bugs.title: A registered passkey can never be removed: there is no delete route, 'sign out everywhere' does not touch it, and account closure leaves it in place.
bugs.scenario: A user adds Face ID sign-in on a phone that is later lost, sold or shared, then taps Sign out (which bumps session_version to end every session). The passkey row stays, so that phone signs straight back in through /auth/passkey/login and gets a fresh 180-day session; nothing in the app or admin console can revoke it. The feature is dormant until migration 064 runs, so this bites the moment the 10-person test starts.
bugs.fix: Add GET /auth/passkey/list and DELETE /auth/passkey/{id} (level user, own rows only), delete the account's passkeys in account_closure, and offer 'also remove Face ID sign-in on other phones' on sign-out.

bugs.title: A team PIN alone yields a full admin token and the global budget still allows about 4,300 guesses a day; temporary PINs may be only 4 digits.
bugs.scenario: The wrong-PIN ceiling is 30 per 10 minutes across all sources (4,320 a day) and no username is needed: every guess is tested against all active team members at /admin/login or /admin/change-pin. A 4-digit temporary PIN created by POST /admin/users falls in at most 2.3 days, a 6-digit PIN in about 4 months on average, and the winner receives a token with the same rights as the master password. (No exposure while admin_users is empty.)
bugs.fix: Require the team member's name with the PIN (per-name failure budget and lock), make temporary PINs 8 digits and expire them unused after 24 h, and lengthen the global window (e.g. 30 wrong PINs per day, with an alert to David on the first trip).

bugs.title: The platform-wide wrong-master-password ceiling is checked before the password, so strangers can keep the correct master password (and every team PIN) locked out.
bugs.scenario: An attacker sends 60 junk non-numeric passwords to /admin/login every 10 minutes from six or more addresses (10 per IP). From then on line 21892 answers 429 to everyone before the password is compared, so David's correct master password and all team PINs are refused for as long as the flood continues. Only an already-enrolled device still gets in, which contradicts ADMIN-NOLOCK-2 ('never locked out by traffic he did not generate').
bugs.fix: Do not let the global ceiling refuse a request that carries a valid, unrevoked ts_device cookie (the non-lapsing credential David already holds), and move the team-PIN branch out from behind the master ceiling. Keep the ceiling for callers with no device pass.

bugs.title: The auth_fail_closed safety switch does not cover the token-only admin routes, including the Tuppence grant.
bugs.scenario: During a suspected token compromise the operator flips auth_fail_closed ('admin surface narrows to the env-only key; the JWT path is refused outright'). Only routes using _require_admin_or_key obey it. Routes guarded by _require_admin (tuppence/grant, tuppence/lookup, anon-rescan-listing, ai-restore, ai-test, demand/sweep, services-status) still accept the JWT, so a stolen token can keep granting Tuppence and rewriting listing photos while the switch reports the door closed.
bugs.evidence:
def _require_admin(x_admin_token: str = Header(default=None)):
    ...
        return _admin_claims(x_admin_token)   # SEC-GATE-1: typed admin token only
(line 159, the only place the switch is read:)  if _bit_flag("auth_fail_closed", False):
bugs.fix: Make _require_admin accept X-Admin-Key and apply the same auth_fail_closed refusal as _require_admin_or_key, with POST /admin/flags as the one explicit exception (so the switch can still be turned off from the token console).
