price_raw = (listing.get("price") or "").replace(",", "")
price_match = _re_match.search(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)?", price_raw)
bugs.fix: Use the numeric mirror that already exists: price_val = listing.get('price_num') or _price_number(listing.get('price')).

bugs.title: A boost marks its matches 'Featured' and top-sorted for ever, and matches made before the boost are never promoted
bugs.scenario: boost_rank is written once when the match row is created and never reset. A match created during a 7-day, 2T boost keeps boost_rank = 1, so the card stays FEATURED and sorts above newer matches after the boost has ended, while a buyer matched before the boost keeps rank 0 (run_match_job cannot re-insert). The route has no caller in ms.js today, so this is reachable only by direct API call.
bugs.evidence: "is_featured":     bool(is_boosted) or (d.get("boost_rank") or 0) > 0,        (12579: ORDER BY m.boost_rank DESC, m.matched_at DESC)
bugs.fix: Decide both from the listing at read time: ORDER BY (l.boost_until > :now) DESC, m.matched_at DESC and is_featured = is_boosted.

bugs.title: Local Market search scores only the newest `limit` rows, and `limit` is unbounded on two public lists
bugs.scenario: The SQL takes the newest 60 adverts in the city and the keyword scoring runs afterwards, so in a city with more than 60 adverts an older item that matches the buyer's words is never found. limit is passed straight to SQL on GET /local-market/listings and GET /wishlist/showcase, so limit=-1 returns every row.
bugs.evidence:
if q and q.strip():
        sig = {"raw_text": q, "category": None}        (13604: params + [limit])
bugs.fix: When q is given, fetch without the page limit (or a high cap such as 500), score, then slice to the page size; clamp limit to 1..100 on both routes as get_wishlist_feed does.

bugs.title: An unanswered Local Market request never closes: the 'auto_closed' status has no writer and the expiry sweep skips Local Market
bugs.scenario: A buyer is told 'seller has 48 hours to respond' (ms.js 17917). RESP-1 (28621) excludes local_market and nothing in the code ever sets status 'auto_closed', so the request stays pending forever, the buyer hears nothing, and the cooldown branch for auto-closed requests can never fire.
bugs.evidence: AND status IN ('declined', 'auto_closed')
bugs.fix: Add a Local Market pass to _lifecycle_sweep that sets status='auto_closed' after the promised window and mails the buyer, or drop the promise and the dead status.

bugs.title: The three 'system tracked' Collectors transaction signals (20 points) are never computed or written
bugs.scenario: A Collectors seller is told 'Complete introductions - system tracked' for 8 + 6 + 6 points. _trust_evidence builds category items with an empty computed map and no code writes category.collectors.tx_* to user_credentials, so the points never arrive however many introductions she completes (the only way to get them is the upload loophole above).
bugs.evidence: "category.collectors.tx_1_4":         {"name": "1–4 successful transactions", "points": 8, "how_to_earn": "Complete introductions — system tracked."},
bugs.fix: Compute them in _trust_evidence from accepted introductions on the seller's Collectors listings (>=1, >=5, >=15) and pass that map to _build_breakdown_items for the category group, or remove the three rows.

bugs.title: The 'best next step' tip offers items that are already uploaded or cannot be done, and promises points the caps will not give
bugs.scenario: _haiko_tip treats every status except 'earned' as open, so a certificate waiting for review is recommended again as 'Upload now'. For a Local Market seller exactly 2 points below a tier the gap-closer picks category.lm.phone_verified and the tip reads 'Not offered: TrustSquare sends no SMS... This adds 2 points - enough to reach ... tier'. 'This adds N points' also ignores the 40/30/40 group caps.
bugs.evidence: if it["status"] not in ("earned",):
bugs.fix: Skip items with status 'pending', items whose how_to_earn is 'Not offered', claim_only items, and compute the gain as _trust_math(with the item) - current score so capped groups show the true number.

bugs.title: The employer-confirmation page is never told that a link is already used
bugs.scenario: trust_employer_confirm stores verified_by as 'employer-link:<nonce>|by:<hash>', but trust_employer_who compares it for equality with 'employer-link:<nonce>'. _used is therefore always false, so a spent link still answers already_confirmed:false and the page offers the confirm button again (the POST then returns points_awarded 0).
bugs.evidence: _used = bool(_nonce) and any((r["verified_by"] or "") == "employer-link:" + _nonce for r in _earned)
bugs.fix: Compare the part before '|by:': (r['verified_by'] or '').split('|by:')[0] == 'employer-link:' + _nonce.

bugs.title: The coach treats system-calculated signals as never earned, so 'Complete your seller profile' and the verified-client steps are recommended for ever
bugs.scenario: earned_map is built from user_credentials plus three users flags; profile_complete and referral_1/3/5plus are computed live and never stored there. A seller with a complete profile and five verified clients still gets 'Complete your seller profile' as step one or two (effort rank 1) each time she asks for a plan.
bugs.evidence:
if earned_map.get(sig_id) == "earned":
            universal_earned_pts += sig["points"]
bugs.fix: Merge _compute_universal_track_status(conn, email) into earned_map before the loop (the connection must stay open until then).

bugs.title: A HEIC document is converted to JPEG but stored under its original .heic name, so /private-docs/ serves it as a download instead of a viewable image.
bugs.scenario: An iPhone photo of a certificate arrives as IMG_0012.HEIC. The bytes are converted to JPEG and ct is set to image/jpeg, but the storage key is built from the original filename; private_document picks the media type from the extension, finds no entry for 'heic' and answers application/octet-stream with nosniff. The reviewer or buyer who taps View gets a file download named .HEIC that holds a JPEG - the unviewable document the conversion was added to prevent.
bugs.evidence:
raw = _dbuf.getvalue(); ct = "image/jpeg"
...
    orig_name = (file.filename or "document").replace(" ", "_")
    key = f"docs/{uuid.uuid4().hex}_{orig_name}"
bugs.fix: After a successful conversion rename the file: orig_name = orig_name.rsplit('.', 1)[0] + '.jpg' before the key is built (set a flag in the conversion block).

bugs.title: The approved 0.60-0.75 confidence band for ID verification is dead code, because 'verified' is already false below 0.75.
bugs.scenario: ID-MATCH-1 (24 Sep, approved) says a document that matches the typed name and number earns at confidence 0.60 to 0.75. _vision_verify_identity folds confidence >= 0.75 into 'verified', so the elif needing verified AND confidence >= 0.60 can never be true: a matching ID read at 0.70 earns nothing and falls to the 'Low AI confidence' note.
bugs.evidence:
verified = (result.get("name_match") and result.get("id_match") and
                    result.get("confidence", 0) >= 0.75 and
...
    elif ai["verified"] and ai["confidence"] >= 0.60:
bugs.fix: Return a separate 'matched' flag from _vision_verify_identity (name_match and id_match and document_appears_genuine, without the confidence test) and use ai['matched'] and ai['confidence'] >= 0.60 in the elif at 16764.

bugs.title: downgrade-free always treats the call as a lowering, so a seller who is already on Free loses her grandfathered regulars allowance.
bugs.scenario: With circle caps on, a Free seller grandfathered at 30 regulars taps 'Select Free' (the current-plan button is only disabled after a separate fetch succeeds). The handler does not check that her tier is already free and calls _plan_changed(..., lowered=True), which sets circle_grandfather to NULL, so 20 of her regulars go to resting although her plan did not change. set_seller_tier computes lowered correctly.
bugs.evidence: res = _plan_changed(conn, email, "free", lowered=True)
bugs.fix: Return early when (user['seller_tier'] or 'free').lower() == 'free' and no downgrade is pending, or pass lowered=(free_limit < _tier_slot_limit(current_tier)) as set_seller_tier does at line 17256.

bugs.title: Cancelling Google sign-in shows 'This sign-in link is not valid', because the callback returns to /?signin=cancelled and the app reads signin= as a magic-link token.
bugs.scenario: A person taps Cancel on Google's screen. The callback redirects to /?signin=cancelled; ms.js (line 1223) treats any signin value as a token, posts 'cancelled' to /auth/verify, gets 401 and shows the invalid-link toast.
bugs.evidence:
if error or not code:
        return RedirectResponse(url="/?signin=cancelled", status_code=302)
bugs.fix: Redirect to '/?go=signin' (the app's existing open-the-sign-in-screen parameter) at 19854 and 19870 instead of reusing the signin key.

bugs.title: TrustSquare superusers pass the gate on the agency seat routes but the handler then refuses them, so the ops console cannot change a cap or remove an agent in someone else's organisation.
bugs.scenario: A signed-in superuser opens another organisation in the ops console (the gate lets superusers through ownership; invite and view work) and taps Remove. _agency_admin_or_refuse accepts only that agency's admin_email or X-Admin-Key, which the app never sends, so the call answers 403 'Only this agency's admin can do that'.
bugs.evidence:
_agency_admin_or_refuse(agency_id, ts_user, x_admin_key, "agent-cap")
(8512)  row = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM agencies WHERE id=? AND LOWER(admin_email)=?",
                           (agency_id, sess)).fetchone()
bugs.fix: In _agency_admin_or_refuse, also return True when the session email is a superuser (same rule the gate applies), or drop the handler check and rely on the gate's ownership rule alone.

bugs.title: Removing an agent leaves their agency tier and slot limit in place, and the tier sync keeps treating removed members as members.
bugs.scenario: An admin removes an agent from a verified agency. The row is only marked 'removed'; users.seller_tier stays 'agency' and slot_limit stays at the agency cap, and _sync_agency_member_tiers has no status filter, so a later verify/un-verify of the agency still re-tiers people who were removed.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("UPDATE agency_members SET status='removed' WHERE agency_id=? AND LOWER(agent_email)=?", (agency_id, email))
             FROM agency_members m
             LEFT JOIN users u ON LOWER(u.email) = LOWER(m.agent_email)
            WHERE m.agency_id = ?""", (agency_id,)).fetchall()
bugs.fix: On removal, if the member has no seat_paid/billing_period_end and holds 'agency' or 'starter' from this agency, reset seller_tier and slot_limit to the free plan (unless another active membership justifies them). Add AND m.status != 'removed' to the sync query.

bugs.title: Import photos beyond the sixth are dropped without being counted or mentioned.
bugs.scenario: An advert arrives with 10 photos. Only the first 6 are scanned; the other 4 are neither attached nor counted as held, the row is not marked needs_review, and the report shows received 10 with attached + held adding up to 6.
bugs.evidence: for src in list(photo_srcs)[:_ANON_PHOTO_MAX]:
bugs.fix: After the loop add the overflow to the notes (e.g. notes.append("skipped:over-6-photo-limit x4")) and surface it in the import row so the agency knows which pictures to add by hand.

bugs.title: The Tuppence 'find a person' search deletes underscores from what was typed, so an email containing '_' cannot be found by typing it.
bugs.scenario: The admin types john_smith@gmail.com (or just john_smith) on the grant card. The pattern becomes %johnsmith@gmail.com%, which does not match the stored address, so the person is not listed although the docstring promises 'any email used in the app is findable here'.
bugs.evidence: like = "%" + q.replace("%", "").replace("_", "") + "%"
bugs.fix: Escape instead of deleting: like = "%" + q.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_") + "%" and add ESCAPE '\' to both LIKE clauses.

bugs.title: The recent-listers card shows a title, category and city that can each come from a different advert.
bugs.scenario: A seller has two live adverts ('Zebra print', Collectors, Pretoria) and ('Apartment to let', Property, Cape Town). MIN() is applied to each column separately, so the card shows 'Apartment to let · Collectors · Cape Town' - a combination that matches no real listing. Grouping is also case-sensitive on seller_email, so one seller can appear twice.
bugs.evidence:
"SELECT l.seller_email AS email, MIN(l.created_at) AS first_listing, COUNT(*) AS n, "
            "MIN(l.title) AS title, MIN(l.category) AS category, MIN(l.city) AS city "
bugs.fix: Group by LOWER(seller_email) and take title/category/city from the earliest row (join back on the MIN(id) per seller) instead of independent MIN() calls.

bugs.title: The intraday-price warning on price-check is decided from two variables that do not exist in the function, so gold and coin listings never get it
bugs.scenario: locals().get('subject') and locals().get('_cat') are always None in ai_price_check, so _is_volatile_item only sees source ('numista', 'web_comps') and verdict. A Krugerrand priced through Numista or web comps returns volatile=false and the standard disclaimer, without the 'spot price can move within minutes' wording the helper exists to add.
bugs.evidence: volatile=_is_volatile_item(source, verdict, locals().get("subject"), locals().get("_cat"))
bugs.fix: Pass the real values: _is_volatile_item(source, verdict, title, category).

bugs.title: Yield results print every amount with an 'R' although UK and US listings are computed in pounds and dollars
bugs.scenario: A London listing run on the 1T tier takes its rent from uk_market_rent (currency GBP) and its price from HM Land Registry (GBP). The answer shows 'monthly_rent_used: R1,250' and the model is told 'Purchase price: R450,000', so a buyer reads pounds as rand; on a narration failure the fallback benchmark is also the South African one.
bugs.evidence:
"purchase_price_used":    f"R{buy_price:,.0f}",
"monthly_rent_used":      f"R{monthly_rent:,.0f}",
bugs.fix: Take the symbol from a small map {'ZA':'R','UK':'£','US':'$','AU':'A$'} keyed by _country_y (_CURRENCY_MAP says 'GB', this function says 'UK') and use it in user_prompt, the fallback market_context, gross_formula and the four *_used fields; choose the fallback benchmark sentence from _BENCHMARKS[_country_y].

bugs.title: batch-cards throws away the bound account email and charges the raw typed one, so a capital letter in the stored address gives a false 'Insufficient Tuppence'
bugs.scenario: ms.js sends seller_email from localStorage. If it is 'John@Gmail.com' while the session is 'john@gmail.com', the gate does not rewrite it (same after normalising) and the handler ignores the value _bind_charged_email returns. _require_tuppence('John@Gmail.com', 2) matches no ledger rows (user_email = ? is case-sensitive) and answers 402 although the wallet has Tuppence.
bugs.evidence:
_bind_charged_email(req.seller_email, ts_user, "ai5-batch-cards")   # ACCOUNT-BIND-1
_require_tuppence(req.seller_email, 2)   # F2 fix (5 Aug 2026): pre-flight only — charge on delivery
bugs.fix: email = _bind_charged_email(req.seller_email, ts_user, 'ai5-batch-cards') and use email in _check_cost_ceiling, _require_tuppence, _log_ai_spend and _deduct_tuppence. Also wrap img_b64.split(',', 1) (line 25778) so a 'data:' string without a comma answers 400, not 500.

bugs.title: Listings whose status is empty are never faded, although the rest of the app treats them as live.
bugs.scenario: The publish guard, coverage count and keep lists all read 'listing_status IS NULL' as live. The fade sweep selects only 'live' and 'paused', so an old row with no status never gets a warning and is never hidden however long it is idle.
bugs.evidence: WHERE l.listing_status IN ('live','paused')
bugs.fix: Use (l.listing_status IS NULL OR l.listing_status IN ('live','paused')), or backfill NULL to 'live' in a one-time migration.

bugs.title: Reinstating a blocked seller makes every blocked advert live, whatever state it was in before the block.
bugs.scenario: The block overwrites live, paused, faded and resting adverts with 'blocked'. Unblock sets all of them to 'live', so adverts the seller had paused, adverts resting above her plan's slots and adverts that had faded all become visible to buyers, above the slot limit.
bugs.evidence:
cur = conn.execute("UPDATE listings SET listing_status='live', block_cause=NULL, status_changed_at=? "
                   "WHERE LOWER(seller_email) = LOWER(?) AND listing_status = 'blocked'",
bugs.fix: Store the prior status when blocking (e.g. a status_before_block column) and restore it on unblock; then call _rebalance_listings for the seller's slot limit.

bugs.title: The 'choose which listings stay live' check uses the current plan's limit, not the lower plan she is moving to.
bugs.scenario: A Pro seller (30 slots) with a pending downgrade to Free (2) may tick 30 listings; cap is computed as 2 but never enforced. On the downgrade day only 2 stay live, chosen by recency among the 30 ticked - not the ones she meant - although the docstring promises 'at most what ... the lower plan she is moving to holds'.
bugs.evidence:
cap = min(cap, _tier_slot_limit(u["pending_downgrade_tier"]))
if len(want) > limit_n:
bugs.fix: Compare len(want) with cap (and use cap in the message) when a downgrade is pending.

bugs.title: Keep live answers 'live' for a paused listing that is still paused.
bugs.scenario: For a paused advert the handler only clears the fade stamp, but returns listing_status 'live'. The seller's hub shows the advert as live while buyers cannot see it.
bugs.evidence: return {"listing_id": listing_id, "listing_status": "live"}
bugs.fix: Return the real status: 'live' only for the faded/live branches, st ('paused') otherwise.

bugs.title: A years-of-experience value that is not a plain number is silently dropped while the profile reports saved.
bugs.scenario: The seller types '5 years' or '10+'. int() raises ValueError, the bare except swallows it and the answer is {ok: true} with no experience and no error, so the screen says saved and the Trust Score points never arrive.
bugs.fix: Take the first run of digits (re.search(r'\d+')) and, when there is none, set out['experience_error'] = 'Please give your years of experience as a number.'

bugs.title: When the AI cost ceiling is reached, creating a Squire brief fails instead of using the template.
bugs.scenario: _check_cost_ceiling raises a 429 HTTPException; _squire_draft_brief re-raises it, so POST /squire/brief answers 429 and the buyer's typed need is lost. The function's own docstring says the template answers 'when ... the ceiling refuses, so a brief is never lost'.
bugs.fix: Remove the 'except HTTPException: raise' pair (let the generic except fall through to 'return template').

bugs.title: The same listing can be approached again and again, and each tap spends one of the 20 monthly approaches.
bugs.scenario: squire_approach inserts a new row every call with no check for an existing approach on that brief and listing, and the allowance is read outside any lock. A double tap spends two units and the seller gets the brief twice; two parallel calls at 1 remaining both pass.
bugs.evidence: cur = conn.execute("INSERT INTO squire_approaches (brief_id, listing_id, email, text, status, created_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)",
bugs.fix: Take BEGIN IMMEDIATE before reading the allowance, and return the existing approach (no new row, no charge) when one already exists for (brief_id, listing_id).

bugs.title: The AI funds gauge shows more head-room than there is.
bugs.scenario: ceiling_left_today_usd subtracts only that one function's spend from the platform-wide daily ceiling, so with a $5 ceiling, $1 on 'fast' and $3.50 on 'reason' the rows read $4.00 and $1.50 left when $0.50 is left. Spend on the as_of day is also left out of 'used since' because the cut-off is written with a 'T' ('2026-10-01T00:00:00Z') while logged_at is stored with a space, and two legacy model keys that fold to the same function overwrite each other at 31342 instead of adding up.
bugs.evidence:
"ceiling_left_today_usd": (round(ceiling - spend["today_usd"], 2) if ceiling is not None else None),
since = datetime.fromisoformat(as_of[:10]).replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z")
bugs.fix: Subtract today's total spend across all lanes from the ceiling; build 'since' and the 30-day cut-off as '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; accumulate into by_lane_task instead of assigning.

bugs.title: A cached fare whose departure date has already passed is still served as a price with a booking link
bugs.scenario: The supplier is unreachable for a week (refresh counts 'failed', cache kept). A fare fetched for departure 13 Sep is still returned on 20 Sep as available with depart_date in the past and a 'Check current fares' link to a search for that past date; only fetched_at is checked.
bugs.fix: In get_indicative return available:False when depart_date is set and earlier than today's date (UTC).

bugs.title: Re-adding a removed agent through the roster reports 'onboarded' and emails a link, but the membership stays 'removed'
bugs.scenario: Agency removes an agent (status='removed'), later uploads them again. ON CONFLICT updates listing_cap/name/city only, status is left 'removed', _member is false so no seat is provisioned, yet the report says ok and an invite is sent. The agent can never be re-attached.
bugs.evidence:
ON CONFLICT(agency_id, agent_email) DO UPDATE SET listing_cap=excluded.listing_cap,
                agent_name=COALESCE(excluded.agent_name, agent_name), city=COALESCE(excluded.city, city),
bugs.fix: Add status=CASE WHEN agency_members.status='removed' THEN 'invited' ELSE agency_members.status END to the DO UPDATE clause (same SQL exists in bea_main.invite_agent).

bugs.title: The redeem refusal names two plans that no longer exist
bugs.scenario: A Starter or Free seller who redeems a launch number is told 'The launch special requires an active Business ($40) or Elite ($100) subscription', but the only qualifying tier is Pro ($20) (QUALIFYING_TIERS) and Business/Elite were purged on 7 Sep 2026 - she cannot buy what the message asks for.
bugs.evidence: launch_redemption.py:370-372  if tier not in QUALIFYING_TIERS:\n            raise HTTPException(status_code=403,\n                                detail="The launch special requires an active Business ($40) or Elite ($100) subscription.")
bugs.fix: Change the text to 'The launch special requires an active Pro ($20) plan.' (build it from _TIER_LABELS so it cannot drift again).

bugs.title: Headline overflow guard trims only the last line, so a long unbroken first word runs off the card
bugs.scenario: Role/title 'Supercalifragilistic-Handyman-Services x' wraps to two lines at 76px; the first line is 2303px wide (card allows 960). The guard shortens only the second line ('x...') and the first is drawn past the right edge.
bugs.fix: Trim every line that exceeds W-120 (loop over _lines), or hard-break over-long words inside _wrap.

bugs.title: BrickLink lookup puts the whole listing title, unescaped, into the URL path as the set number
bugs.scenario: bea_main calls bricklink_price(title) with e.g. 'LEGO Star Wars 75192 Millennium Falcon': the request goes to /items/SET/LEGO Star Wars 75192.../price and can never match, and a title containing '/', '..' or '?' changes which BrickLink endpoint is called with the shop's token. Dark until a BrickLink key is set.
bugs.evidence:
r = await c.get("https://api.bricklink.com/api/store/v1/items/SET/"
                            f"{query}/price", params={"guide_type": "sold", "new_or_used": "U"})
bugs.fix: Extract the set number from the title with a regex (\b\d{4,6}(-\d)?\b, default suffix -1), return None when none is found, and pass it through urllib.parse.quote(..., safe='').

bugs.title: Numista price is always labelled 'grade VF' even when the figure used is the F, XF or median price
bugs.scenario: A coin issue has no VF estimate: the code falls back to F, then XF, then the median of all grades, but the provenance shown to the buyer (who pays 1T) still says 'grade VF'.
bugs.evidence:
val = by_grade.get("vf") or by_grade.get("f") or by_grade.get("xf") \
            or vals[len(vals) // 2]
...
+ ", grade VF - collector reference, not a sale price"),
bugs.fix: Record which grade supplied the value and print that grade (or 'median of listed grades') in the provenance string.

bugs.title: POST /quality/preview answers 500 when price, suburb, category or description arrives as a JSON number
bugs.scenario: Body {"price": 500} (public route). The coercion deliberately keeps ints and floats as numbers, then _import_quality_score calls (d.get('price') or '').strip() / re.match(..., d.get('description') or '') on them -> AttributeError/TypeError -> 500, the exact outcome the AUDIT-Q4 comment says cannot happen.
bugs.evidence:
row[k] = None if v is None else (v if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) else str(v)[:4000])
...
if (d.get("price") or "").strip() and ...
bugs.fix: Keep numbers only for the numeric keys: `num = ('beds','baths','vehicle_year','mileage_km')`; for every other key store str(v)[:4000].

bugs.title: Malformed passkey input raises errors that are not _PasskeyError, so the public passkey login answers 500 instead of a clean refusal.
bugs.scenario: The callers catch only _PasskeyError. _pk_ub64u raises binascii.Error on a bad base64 length, _pk_cbor raises IndexError / struct.error / RecursionError / TypeError on truncated, deeply nested or list-keyed CBOR, and _pk_check_client raises AttributeError when clientDataJSON is a JSON list. POST /auth/passkey/login with clientDataJSON='a' returns 500. Dormant until the passkeys table exists.
bugs.fix: Make the helpers fail in one shape: wrap the bodies of _pk_ub64u, _pk_cbor_loads, _pk_check_client and _pk_pubkey in try/except Exception -> raise _PasskeyError('malformed passkey data'), letting an existing _PasskeyError pass through.

bugs.title: Malformed passkey data raises errors the handlers do not catch, so the answer is a 500 instead of a clean refusal (and the challenge is already spent).
bugs.scenario: A login for a known credential id (or a registration) sends clientDataJSON/authenticatorData that is not valid base64, an attestation with truncated or deeply nested CBOR, or a COSE key that is not a map. _pk_ub64u raises binascii.Error and the CBOR/struct code raises IndexError, struct.error, UnicodeDecodeError, AttributeError or RecursionError; only _PasskeyError is caught, so the user sees 'Internal Server Error'.
bugs.fix: In passkey_login and passkey_register catch Exception around the verify call (log the type) and answer the same 401/400 as for _PasskeyError; add a depth limit to _pk_cbor.

bugs.title: vision-draft cleans the model's answer outside the try block, so an answer that is valid JSON but the wrong shape gives a bare 500
bugs.scenario: The model returns a JSON list, or category_confidence as 'high'. json.loads succeeds, then draft.pop(...) raises AttributeError or float('high') raises ValueError outside any handler, and the seller sees 'Internal Server Error' instead of the 422 'try describing instead' message the route promises.
bugs.evidence:
claude_warnings = draft.pop("warnings", []) or []
draft["category_confidence"] = min(1.0, max(0.0, float(draft.get("category_confidence") or 0.7)))
bugs.fix: Directly after json.loads add: if not isinstance(draft, dict): raise HTTPException(422, ...). Parse the two confidences through a small helper that returns the default on ValueError/TypeError.

bugs.title: The price reader turns a dot-separated price such as 'R1.200.000' into 1.2 and 'R120 m²' into 120 million
bugs.scenario: A seller types the price with dots as thousands separators; price_num is stored as 1.2, so the advert sorts as the cheapest and passes every price_max filter and facet range. A price per square metre written 'R120 m²' reads the m as million. Both confirmed by running _price_number.
bugs.fix: Accept '.' as a thousands separator when there are two or more 3-digit groups (\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{3}){2,}) and strip it like the others; change the multiplier lookahead to (?![a-z0-9²]) so 'm2'/'m²' is not read as million.

bugs.title: The startup re-import of the prospect pool deletes the pool before checking that the source file exists, and a failed import is kept half-done
bugs.scenario: With DEMAND_RM5_DB set and no prospect carrying a city_name, boot deletes demand_prospects and the rm5 ledger rows; the import that should refill them only runs if the file is still at that path, so a moved file leaves the pool empty. If the import raises midway the rows inserted so far are committed by the later conn.commit(), and the next boot sees a non-empty pool and never completes it.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("DELETE FROM demand_prospects")
conn.execute("DELETE FROM outreach_ledger WHERE channel IN ('rm5_wave','rm5_events')")
...
if _rm5 and os.path.exists(_rm5) and \
bugs.fix: Add 'and os.path.exists(_rm5)' to the clearing condition, and wrap clear + import in SAVEPOINT rm5 / ROLLBACK TO rm5 on exception so it is all or nothing.

bugs.title: POST /admin/refresh-pois clears a listing's nearby places before it knows it has coordinates to fetch new ones
bugs.scenario: For a listing with no stored coordinates and no city centroid (city not in geo_cities, or a city row with NULL lat), the handler commits nearby_pois=NULL and then answers 422 - or 500 from float(None) - so the places the listing had (found from its suburb at publish) are gone and nothing refetches them.
bugs.evidence:
conn.execute("UPDATE listings SET nearby_pois=NULL WHERE id=?", (listing_id,))
conn.commit()
...
lat, lng = float(city_row["lat"]), float(city_row["lng"])
bugs.fix: Resolve the coordinates first (guard NULL city lat/lng, and fall back to the suburb coordinates as _publish_autolinks does); clear nearby_pois only once a coordinate pair is in hand; close the connection in a finally.

bugs.title: A credential decision syncs listings.trust_score but not users.trust_score, which every Local Market card, the min-trust filter and the suspension check read
bugs.scenario: Ops verifies (or rejects) a Local Market seller's credential. CRED-SCORE-SYNC-1 rewrites listings.trust_score only; GET /local-market/listings and /local-market/listings/{id} show COALESCE(u.trust_score, 0) from users, so her card and the buyer's trust filter keep the old score until somebody opens her profile or hub.
bugs.evidence: conn.execute("UPDATE listings SET trust_score = ? WHERE LOWER(seller_email) = ? AND category = ? "
bugs.fix: In the same block also UPDATE users SET trust_score to the score under _category_key_for_user(conn, _em) and call _lm_recompute_seller_state(conn, _em).

bugs.title: A screen phrase with a line break in it can be cached half-translated for ever.
bugs.scenario: ms.js sends text nodes trimmed only at the ends, so a phrase wrapped over two lines in the HTML reaches the prompt as '3. first line\n second line'. If the model answers on two lines, the parser keeps only the numbered line; that half is cached permanently and every reader sees the cut-off sentence.
bugs.evidence:
numbered = "\n".join("%d. %s" % (i + 1, t) for i, t in enumerate(items))
m = re.match(r"^(\d+)[.)]\s*(.+)$", ln.strip())
bugs.fix: Collapse inner whitespace for the prompt (' '.join(t.split())) while keeping the original string as the cache key, and append un-numbered answer lines to the previous number instead of dropping them.

bugs.title: A top-up for zero or a negative number of Tuppence is sent to Paystack as a R1 charge that can never be credited.
bugs.scenario: POST /payment/initialize?tuppence=0 (or -3): usd_to_zar_amount returns max(1, ...) = R1, a checkout link is issued, the payer is charged R1, and verify then refuses it because tuppence <= 0.
bugs.evidence:
amount_rands = usd_to_zar_amount(tuppence * 2)
line 24195: return max(1, round(usd * fx_rates_sync()["ZAR"]))
bugs.fix: At the top of initialize_payment: if tuppence < 1 or tuppence > a sane ceiling (for example 500) raise HTTPException(422).

bugs.title: The once-per-person first-lister bonus is a check followed by an insert with no lock, so two quick clicks can credit it twice.
bugs.scenario: The grant button is tapped twice (or two operators grant the same person). Both requests run the 'prior' SELECT before either INSERT commits, both find nothing, and the seller is credited the bonus twice.
bugs.evidence:
prior = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, amount, created_at FROM transactions WHERE lower(user_email) = ? AND type = ?",
                (email, kind)).fetchone()
bugs.fix: Call _wallet_lock(conn) (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) before the prior-check so the check and the INSERT are one write transaction, or add a partial unique index on transactions(lower(user_email)) WHERE type='first_lister_bonus' and treat the conflict as 'already'.

bugs.title: Decline does not re-check 'pending' in its UPDATE, so a decline racing an accept leaves the agent charged 1T for a declined lead
bugs.scenario: Agent double-taps Accept and Decline. Decline reads status 'pending', accept commits (status accepted, -1T), then decline's unconditional UPDATE sets status='declined'. The agent paid 1T, the intro shows declined and neither side sees the contact.
bugs.evidence: conn.execute("UPDATE agent_intros SET status='declined', responded_at=? WHERE id=?", (_now(), intro_id))
bugs.fix: Use WHERE id=? AND status='pending' and return 409 when rowcount != 1, mirroring accept_agent_intro.

bugs.title: /zoom/next rows skip the language-layer clean-up that /listings applies, so unapproved draft translations and working text are public
bugs.scenario: GET /listings and GET /listings/{id} remove extra_back and search_en and withhold title_extra/desc_extra until extra_status is 'approved'. _zoom_public_row does neither, so /zoom/next returns a seller's unapproved machine translation, its back-translation and the English search layer.
bugs.fix: Move the three LANG-LAYER lines from get_listings (3847-3849) into one helper (e.g. _public_listing_row) and call it from get_listings, _zoom_public_row and the single-listing read.

bugs.title: Quick one-tap save tells a signed-out caller whether a typed email already has a TrustSquare account
bugs.scenario: A stranger POSTs /listings/quick-publish with someone's address. An existing member gets {verify:true, 'You already have a TrustSquare account...'}; an unknown address gets {need:'eula', ...}. Membership of the marketplace is disclosed for any address (10 probes per address, 50 per connection a day), and each probe also drops a draft and a letter on the victim.
bugs.fix: Return the same body for both cases to a signed-out caller (e.g. {id, live:false, need:'eula', identity:'email', detail:'Your listing is saved. We emailed you a link ...'}); the letter itself already carries the right next step.

bugs.title: GET /sellers/credentials/{listing_id} answers for drafts and for adverts hidden from strangers
bugs.scenario: STRANGER-GATE-1 closed the single-advert read, the status card and /sellers/summary for a worker who is not yet vouched, and E2E-HMI-1 made drafts unreadable. This route checks neither, so anyone walking listing ids gets the itemised trust evidence, penalties and accepted-introduction count of a hidden or unpublished seller (and each call also rewrites trust_score rows).
bugs.fix: Select listing_status too and return 404 unless it is 'live', and add the same test as seller_summary_for_listing: `if _session_email(ts_user) != owner and _hidden_from_strangers(conn, listing_id): 404`.

bugs.title: /review/request-link reveals whether an address is on the reviewer allowlist, although its comment says it does not.
bugs.scenario: For an off-list address the answer is {"ok": true}; for an allow-listed one it is {"ok": true, "delivery": "sent"}. A stranger can therefore test addresses (8 per 10 minutes per IP) and learn who the testers are, sending each real one an access email.
bugs.fix: Return the same body in both cases: answer {"ok": True, "delivery": "sent"} for an off-list address as well, and report a real transport failure only in the server log.

bugs.title: GET /users/{email}/id-status is declared public with no binding: a stranger can read the ID-check state of any email address
bugs.scenario: Anyone calls /users/victim@example.com/id-status and learns whether that address has an ID submitted, AI-checked or 'verified with Home Affairs', plus interim points. An unknown address answers 'none', so any other answer also proves the account exists. The only caller in the app passes the signed-in user's own address (ms.js:8820).
bugs.evidence: route_policy.json:493-498  "key": "GET /users/{email}/id-status", "level": "public", "hide": ["npr_verified_at"]
bugs.fix: Declare it {"level": "user", "bind": [{"in": "path", "name": "email"}]}; the buyer-facing warning already comes from listing-level endpoints that never take an email.

bugs.title: When object storage is not configured, ID documents and certificates are written into the public /media folder under the client's own filename.
bugs.scenario: With _S3_CONFIGURED false the upload skips _s3_upload (which sends docs/ keys to the private store and disarms unsafe extensions) and writes the bytes to /var/www/marketsquare/media/docs_<uuid>_<filename>, returning a public /media/ URL. A private document becomes readable by anyone holding the link, and a file named x.html declared as image/jpeg is served as a web page on the main origin. Latent: production has storage configured.
bugs.evidence:
safe = key.replace("/", "_")
        path = os.path.join(_LOCAL_MEDIA_DIR, safe)
...
        url = f"/media/{safe}"
bugs.fix: Replace the else branch with url = _private_store(raw, _safe_storage_key(key)) so the fallback also lands in the private store and is served only through /private-docs/.

bugs.title: If MS_JWT_SECRET is ever unset, the review/OAuth-state secret becomes a publicly computable constant and user-session signing does not fail closed.
bugs.scenario: With MS_JWT_SECRET and MS_REVIEW_SECRET both missing, _REVIEW_SECRET = sha256('trustsquare-review-scope|'), so anyone can mint a valid ts_review gate cookie and OAuth state. _establish_user_session (19618) also signs ts_user with the empty key with no guard, unlike _make_token and _admin_claims which refuse. QUICK-RETURN-GUARD-1 records a process that did run with the secret empty on 18 Sep.
bugs.evidence:
_REVIEW_SECRET     = os.environ.get("MS_REVIEW_SECRET") or hashlib.sha256(
                        ("trustsquare-review-scope|" + _JWT_SECRET).encode()).hexdigest()
bugs.fix: Fail closed like JWT-HARDEN-1: when _JWT_SECRET is empty set _REVIEW_SECRET = '' and have _grant_review_cookie, review_verify, auth_oauth_start, _oauth_complete and _establish_user_session raise HTTPException(503, 'Server auth not configured') before signing or decoding.

bugs.title: The fault closure letter is mailed to whatever address was typed on the report, and can be sent again on every call
bugs.scenario: /app/fault accepts any reporter_email (no format check, no proof) from a caller holding only the public app key; the 24 Sep fix stopped the ACK going to unproven addresses, but close-send later mails that same address a letter quoting the attacker's title and the fix note. The route has no 'already closed' test, so a retried call by the maintenance loop mails the letter again. The _require_maint docstring's claim that the key 'cannot be pointed at an arbitrary recipient' therefore does not hold.
bugs.evidence:
msg = _fault_close_email(row)
sent = _send_system_email(msg["to"], msg["subject"], msg["html"])
bugs.fix: Store ack_proven on the fault row at filing (session email or reviewer token) and send the closure letter only when it is set; validate reporter_email with the same pattern as /support/message; in close-send return early when status is already 'closed' or retest_sent_at is set.

bugs.title: The in-app check on the orchestrator routes accepts any request that merely carries an 'Authorization: Basic' header, so it adds nothing to the nginx realm it was meant to back up
bugs.scenario: The route policy level 'device' is not enforced by the gate, so _orch_require_device_or_admin is the only in-app check. Its third branch passes when X-Real-IP is present (nginx sets it on every request) and the Authorization header starts with 'basic ' - the credentials are never verified. If any nginx location ever forwards /orchestrator/approve or the defence map without auth_basic, a stranger sending 'Authorization: Basic x' can approve gated items for auto-ship and read the defence map.
bugs.evidence: if request.headers.get("x-real-ip") and (request.headers.get("authorization") or "").lower().startswith("basic "):
bugs.fix: Verify the credential in the app, the way _grading_review_auth does (decode the Basic header and compare_digest against the orchestrator user/password from the environment), or remove the branch and let the page send X-Admin-Token.

bugs.title: JSON binding and ownership are skipped when a JSON body is sent with a form or multipart content type
bugs.scenario: With Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded and a JSON body, parse_qsl returns a (junk) list, so the 'unreadable body' 415 guard does not fire, json_obj is None and every 'json' bind/own spec is silently skipped (multipart: _multipart_fields returns {} on a parse error, same result). A handler that reads the body with await request.json() - which ignores the content type - then acts on the unbound email / unowned id. Today the only such handler (POST /listings/{id}/wonders, bea_main.py:18481) re-checks with _actor(), so this is latent; the next raw-JSON handler would be open.
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:376-377  if body and media == "application/x-www-form-urlencoded":\n                form_pairs = parse_qsl(body.decode("latin-1"), keep_blank_values=True)  ||  security_gate.py:381-382  ... and json_obj is None and form_pairs is None and multipart is None):
bugs.fix: Refuse by declared location: if the policy has any 'json' spec and the body is non-empty, require json_obj to be a dict (else 415); if it has 'form' specs, require form_pairs/multipart. Make _multipart_fields return None on a parse failure.

bugs.title: The output encoder leaves three shapes untouched: objects nested under a photo key, anything nested under a text key's URL fields, and records that carry no 'id'
bugs.scenario: _url_field() returns dicts inside a list unchanged and _encode() does not descend into them, so {'photos':[{'url':'javascript:alert(1)','caption':''}]} leaves as written (verified on the module). A dict without 'id'/'pair_id' is not a 'record', so {'listing_id':5,'title':'
bugs.evidence: security_gate.py:635-637  if isinstance(v, list):\n        return [x for x in (_url_field(y) for y in v) if x or x == 0]\n    return v  ||  security_gate.py:644  record = "id" in obj or "pair_id" in obj
bugs.fix: In _url_field(), run dict items through _encode() with record=True and their url/src/href values through _URL_OK; in _encode(), treat every dict as a record for _TEXT_KEYS (the id test saves nothing) or at least any dict having a key ending in '_id'.

bugs.title: The 1T balance test and the daily cap for the paid ID check are read before the supplier call without a lock, so parallel requests buy several supplier queries for 1T.
bugs.scenario: An account with 1T sends ten verify-identity-npr requests at once with different ID numbers. All ten pass the balance and attempts checks and all ten consume a paid supplier query; nine then fail in _deduct_tuppence with 402 and write no ledger row, so the cost is ours and the cap never counts them.
bugs.fix: Reserve before the call: under _wallet_lock insert a -1 hold row and a ledger row with outcome 'in_progress', commit, call the supplier, then either keep the charge or insert a +1 release when the result is not billable. Count 'in_progress' rows in the daily cap.

bugs.title: The Paystack webhook is an async handler that makes blocking rate fetches and database calls, so it can freeze every request while it runs.
bugs.scenario: When the 12-hour rate cache is stale and the two rate feeds are slow or down, usd_to_zar_amount calls fx_rates_sync, which waits up to 8 seconds per feed on the event loop; the cache is not refreshed on failure, so each webhook event repeats the wait. All other requests stall for that time.
bugs.evidence:
async def paystack_webhook(request: Request):
if tuppence > 0 and not _paystack_paid_enough(data, usd_to_zar_amount(tuppence * 2), reference):
bugs.fix: Keep only 'raw_body = await request.body()' async and run the rest through await asyncio.to_thread(_handle_paystack_event, raw_body, signature); storing the charged amount at initialise (see the top-up refusal finding) removes the rate fetch from this path altogether.

bugs.title: The Apple callback is async but runs the blocking token exchange, key fetch and database writes on the event loop.
bugs.scenario: auth_oauth_apple_callback awaits request.form() and then calls the synchronous _oauth_complete (httpx.post timeout 20 s, PyJWKClient fetch, sqlite). Each Apple sign-in freezes every other request for the length of two HTTPS round trips, and for up to 20 s or more when Apple is slow. Only live once the Apple lane is configured.
bugs.evidence:
async def auth_oauth_apple_callback(request: Request):
...
    _out, nxt = _oauth_complete("apple", code, state, resp, request.cookies.get("ts_oauth_nonce"))
bugs.fix: Call it through the threadpool: _out, nxt = await run_in_threadpool(_oauth_complete, 'apple', code, state, resp, request.cookies.get('ts_oauth_nonce')) (from starlette.concurrency).

bugs.title: The breaker heartbeat runs blocking database calls on the event loop.
bugs.scenario: Whenever an AI lane is tripped, each minute the async loop itself opens SQLite, calls claim_probe, _check_cost_ceiling (which deletes expired holds) and _log_ai_spend. If another writer holds the lock (see the sweep finding) each call can wait up to 5 s, and during that time the whole server stops answering.
bugs.evidence:
_hb_conn = database.get_db()
_check_cost_ceiling("system:heartbeat")
_log_ai_spend("system:heartbeat", "/breaker/heartbeat", _t,
bugs.fix: Move the body of one tick into a plain function and run it with await asyncio.to_thread(...), as the probe call already is.

bugs.title: Signing in with the 6-digit code does not store the account name or join date that the link sign-in stores.
bugs.scenario: /auth/verify-code returns {ok, email, name}. The code path saves only the email and reloads; msAdoptSession then skips because an email is present. A returning seller who signs in by code shows as 'Your account' in the sell sheet and her name is not prefilled where ms_aa_name is read, while the same person signing in by link gets her name.
bugs.evidence:
try{ localStorage.setItem('ms_user_email', res.d.email);
     localStorage.setItem('ms_aa_email', res.d.email); }catch(e){}
bugs.fix: Mirror the link path (1234-1236): also set ms_aa_name = res.d.name || msShownEmail(res.d.email) and ms_joined_date if missing. One shared function for both doors.

bugs.title: If the agency lookup fails, the console tells a real agency admin 'No agency is linked to <email> yet'.
bugs.scenario: An agency admin opens the console link with a lapsed sign-in (401) or a network fault. The failed /agencies/by-admin call is swallowed, agencyId stays null, and the screen shows the 'no agency linked - apply by email' page. A signed-out visitor gets the same page instead of a sign-in prompt.
bugs.fix: Tell the three cases apart: no email or 401 -> go to sign-in (keep the console link to return to); network/5xx -> 'Could not load - Retry'; only a 200 with no agency_id (or 404) shows the create/apply page.

bugs.title: Opening Plans rewrites 'Apply as an agency' to 'Select Agency', which starts a payment the server always refuses, and a button disabled as 'Current plan' is never enabled again.
bugs.scenario: openPlans() relabels every button 'Select <tier>'. Tapping Select Agency runs setPlan('agency'), which posts to /payment/seller-subscription/initialize; the server answers 400 'The Agency plan is free - no payment needed. Apply via agency verification instead.' and nothing tells her how to apply. Separately, openPlans sets btn.disabled = true on the current plan and never clears it, so after an immediate switch to Free the old plan's button stays dead until the page is reloaded.
bugs.fix: In the reset loop set btn.disabled = false and keep the Agency label ('Apply as an agency'). In setPlan and _subSelectTier handle tier 'agency' before any payment call: open the agency console / the 'Apply by email' link from _agencyCreateHtml.

bugs.title: 'Clear all' in the Adventures sheet leaves the Stays/Experiences pill on, and the next 'Show results' throws the buyer back to All
bugs.scenario: On Stays, Clear all empties filterState.adventures.adventureType but advSubcat stays 'adventures_accommodation'. Re-opening the sheet shows no type selected; applying any other filter reads 'Any', sets sc='all' and mixes experiences back in (the fault ADV-SYNC-2 fixed for the open path).
bugs.evidence: filterState.adventures = { adventureType:'', environment:'', maxPrice:'', duration:'', groupSize:'', area:'' };
bugs.fix: In clearFilters('adventures') keep adventureType in step with advSubcat (or reset advSubcat and the pills to All in the same call).

bugs.title: Switching city keeps the previous city's search result ids, so the new city shows 'No matches' until the search is retyped
bugs.scenario: With text in the search box, selectCity swaps the listings but _msSearchIds still holds the old city's ids; none of the new city's adverts are in the set, so the grid reads 'No matches for “…”' although the box and the new city may well match.
bugs.evidence: for (let i = LISTINGS.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { if (LISTINGS[i].isLive) LISTINGS.splice(i, 1); } … renderGrid(); … loadLiveListings(0);
bugs.fix: After a city change call msRunSearch() when _msSearchQ is set (and zoomFetch() when the funnel is active).

bugs.title: After one AI failure the 'Analyse photos' button stays bound to goSkipPhotos for the rest of the page session (latent).
bugs.scenario: goVisionFallback assigns s1Next.onclick = goSkipPhotos; goResetStep1UI/goInit restore the label 'Analyse photos →' but not the handler, so new photos or a second listing skip straight to manual entry.
bugs.evidence: s1Next.onclick = () => goSkipPhotos();
bugs.fix: In goResetStep1UI add s1Next.onclick = goVisionNext;

bugs.title: goAnonReplace (and 9610) empties #go-photo-strip with innerHTML='', destroying the thumbnail container for the session (latent).
bugs.scenario: After an anonymity scrub the seller taps Replace and picks new photos; goRenderPhotoStrip finds no #go-photo-thumbs and returns, so no thumbnails, count or delete buttons appear.
bugs.evidence: if (stripEl) { stripEl.style.display = 'none'; stripEl.innerHTML = ''; }
bugs.fix: Clear only the thumbnails: const t=document.getElementById('go-photo-thumbs'); if(t) t.innerHTML='';

bugs.title: The 'You have an unfinished listing' banner is inserted again on every visit to sell-b, stacking duplicates with the same id (latent).
bugs.scenario: sbReset runs on each goTo('sell-b') and sbCheckResumeDraft never removes an existing #sb-draft-banner; Resume/Start fresh remove only the first, leaving a stale banner for a discarded draft.
bugs.evidence:
const banner=document.createElement('div');
banner.id='sb-draft-banner';
bugs.fix: Start sbCheckResumeDraft with: const old=document.getElementById('sb-draft-banner'); if(old) old.remove();

bugs.title: B3 re-render and B5 captions write seller/AI values into value="..." unescaped, truncating anything after a double quote (latent: Path B).
bugs.scenario: Headline 55" Samsung TV shows as '55' after Back from B4 or after tapping a sub-type (sbSetSubcat re-renders); touching the field saves the truncated value. AI captions with quotes (11088) break the same way, and "> injects markup.
bugs.evidence:
value="${val}"
value="${titleVal}"
value="${existing.caption||''}"
bugs.fix: Use the attribute-safe helper already in the file: value="${teEsc(val)}", value="${teEsc(titleVal)}", value="${teEsc(existing.caption||'')}"; render title/description in the B8 preview (11433-11434) with _lmEsc.

bugs.title: Document-hub buttons put the seller's email raw inside single-quoted inline onclick handlers, so an address containing an apostrophe (o'brien@...) breaks Declare and Upload Document.
bugs.scenario: Seller whose sign-in email is o'connor@example.com opens Edit -> the rendered handler is elDocHubUpload('o'connor@example.com') -> SyntaxError on tap, nothing happens and no message appears; the same applies to every 'Declare - Earn +N pts' button.
bugs.evidence:
<button onclick="elSubmitDeclaration('${email}','${sigId}')"
<button onclick="elDocHubUpload('${email}')"
bugs.fix: Do not pass the email through markup: read it inside the handlers from _msSignedEmail()/SELLERS[0]._email, or attach listeners with addEventListener after rendering.

bugs.title: lmOpenDetail never clears _lmCurrentListing, so if a detail fetch fails the 'View seller profile' shortcut and Request introduction act on the previously viewed listing.
bugs.scenario: Buyer viewed item A, returns, taps 'View seller profile' on item B; the B fetch fails (suspended/offline) but lmOpenDetailAndProfile still opens A's profile 100 ms later, whose CTA queues an introduction for A.
bugs.evidence:
const el = document.getElementById('lm-detail-container'); el.innerHTML = '
Loading…
'; // _lmCurrentListing not reset
bugs.fix: Set _lmCurrentListing = null at the top of lmOpenDetail and have it return true/false so lmOpenDetailAndProfile only opens the profile on success for the same id.

bugs.title: A successful credential claim re-runs msInit, which jumps the user from the Trust tab to Overview (flag-dark).
bugs.scenario: On the Trust tab the user claims a FIDE credential; msInit() ends with msTab('overview'), so the screen switches away and the claim result written to #ms-cred-out is no longer visible.
bugs.evidence: try{ if(typeof msInit==='function') msInit(); }catch(e){}
bugs.fix: Refresh only the trust part (re-fetch /users/{email}/trust and call msRenderTrust + msRenderLiveSignals) instead of msInit().

bugs.title: ID upload progress is written onto the first .ms-sig-action in the document, which is a Squire button when Squire is on (flag-dark).
bugs.scenario: With baseline_q4 armed and a Squire brief listed, the Squire card sits at the top of the Overview tab, before the Trust tab. Uploading an ID turns the brief's 'Shortlist' button into '⏳ Uploading…'/'ID under review' and disables it, while the real Upload ID button never changes.
bugs.evidence: const btn = document.querySelector('.ms-sig-action');
bugs.fix: Select the button by its action: document.querySelector('#ms-trust-signals [data-action="upload-id"]').

bugs.title: The sell flow's in-app ← buttons push a new history entry, so the phone's Back then goes forward to the step just left.
bugs.scenario: Seller goes Photos → Section A, taps the in-app ← (sfGo('photos') pushes another entry). Pressing the phone Back now returns her to Section A instead of the category picker; each in-app back/forward grows the stack and Back replays the zig-zag.
bugs.fix: For in-app back moves call history.back() when history.state.sf names the previous step (or pass a flag to sfGo that uses replaceState instead of pushState).

bugs.title: sfSkip's 1.6 s delayed sfGo(next) fires even after the seller has tapped Back or left the sell flow.
bugs.scenario: Seller taps 'Skip for now' on Step 2 (the warning shows), then taps ← within 1.6 s: she lands on Photos and is then pulled forward to Step 3; if she tapped Exit, sfGo pushes a sell-flow history entry on top of Home, so the next phone Back does nothing visible.
bugs.evidence: if(w && w.style.display!=='block'){ w.style.display='block'; setTimeout(function(){sfGo(next);},1600); }
bugs.fix: Capture var from=sfState.screen; in the timer only call sfGo(next) if sfFlowActive() && sfState.screen===from.

bugs.title: The Adventures tour-agent panel (and the cached Property/Cars agent panel) never reloads after a city change or a failed load.
bugs.scenario: A buyer opens the tour-agent panel in Pretoria, switches to Cape Town and opens it again: _advAgentsLoaded is already true, so it still shows Pretoria's agents ('near Pretoria'); a network failure on first open shows 'No accredited tour agents near …' for the rest of the visit. catAgentsRestore likewise repaints window._catAgentsHtml cached per vertical, not per city.
bugs.evidence:
if(!open && !_advAgentsLoaded){ advAgentsLoad(); }
  _advAgentsLoaded=true;
bugs.fix: Store the city the panel was loaded for (e.g. _advAgentsLoadedFor=city) and reload when activeCity.name differs; set it only when both fetches succeeded; key _catAgentsHtmlFor on v+'|'+city.

bugs.title: Face ID / passkey sign-in sets only ms_aa_email, so a previous account's ms_user_email (which signOut does not remove) keeps winning wherever the app reads ms_user_email first.
bugs.scenario: Account A signed in by code (both keys set), signs out (only ms_aa_email removed), B signs in with a passkey: msRenderIdVerifyCard (23493) reads ms_user_email||ms_aa_email and shows A's ID status from the public /users/{A}/id-status, and other readers (Paystack receipt prompt 17211, 18137, 18651) use A's address. sfAuthVerify (21509) sets both keys; this path does not.
bugs.evidence:
localStorage.setItem('ms_aa_email', d.email);
      localStorage.setItem('ms_aa_name', d.name || msShownEmail(d.email));
bugs.fix: Also localStorage.setItem('ms_user_email', d.email) here (and remove 'ms_user_email' in signOut, ms.js 2158).

bugs.title: ms_gate.js sends the seller to the sign-in screen on a 401 that the sell flow is already handling inline, so the coach question / agent introduction is abandoned.
bugs.scenario: sfCoachAskSend or sfAgentIntro POST while the cached sfMe() still says signed in (60 s cache) or /quick/me failed: the server answers 401 signin_required; the sell flow opens its inline 6-digit box (ASK-SIGNIN-1, 'your listing stays right here'), then ms_gate's async handler calls goTo('signin') and takes her off the step; after signing in there the question is never sent.
bugs.fix: Let callers opt out: skip the redirect when init.headers['X-Inline-Signin'] is set (send it from sfCoachAskSend and sfAgentIntro), or skip it while #screen-sell-flow is active and #sf-authbox exists.

bugs.title: The hub's ACTIVE count still includes adverts buyers cannot see: resting, faded and blocked adverts are mapped to 'active'.
bugs.scenario: /listings/mine returns every advert of the seller whatever its status. _dlStatus maps only draft, paused and archived; 'resting' (plan holds fewer slots), 'faded' and 'blocked' fall through to 'active'. A seller who moved to Free with 2 live and 3 resting adverts reads '5 ACTIVE' in the hub header while each card's own chip says resting - the same fault HUB-ACTIVE-COUNT-1 fixed for paused adverts.
bugs.evidence: function _dlStatus(ls){ ls = String(ls || 'live').toLowerCase(); return ls === 'draft' ? 'draft' : (ls === 'paused' ? 'paused' : (ls === 'archived' ? 'archived' : 'active')); }
bugs.fix: Return 'active' only for 'live' (and the still-visible fade warning state if one exists); map resting/faded/blocked to their own value (or 'paused') so updateDashStats() counts only adverts buyers can see.

bugs.title: A price in another currency shows its basis twice.
bugs.scenario: For a non-rand price formatZAR returns the seller's whole text, and _priceLabel then appends the basis it finds in that same text. Run in Node: 'US$1,450 per person' renders as 'US$1,450 per person per person' and '£80 pp' as '£80 pp pp' (outside Adventures).
bugs.fix: Skip the suffix when _base already contains it (the as-is branches of formatZAR): e.g. compute _suf only when formatZAR took the numeric path, or return a flag from formatZAR saying the text was passed through whole.

bugs.title: Inviting an agent always says 'magic link sent', even when the server reports the email failed.
bugs.scenario: POST /agencies/{id}/agents returns link: 'sent' | 'failed' | 'dry'. The app ignores it and toasts 'Invited x - magic link sent', so an admin waits for an agent who never received anything.
bugs.evidence: showToast('Invited '+email+' — magic link sent'); _renderAgency(window._agencyId);
bugs.fix: Read d.link: 'sent' -> current message; otherwise 'Added x, but the email could not be sent - ask them to sign in at trustsquare.co with this address' (they join on first sign-in).

bugs.title: The Adventures country sheet does not tick Kenya, Botswana or Germany, and 'Europe' excludes German adverts
bugs.scenario: The tick loop lists ten codes without KE, BW and DE, so with one of those saved the sheet opens with nothing ticked. The filter compares codes exactly, so choosing 'Europe' (EU) hides listings whose country is DE.
bugs.evidence: ['ZA','NA','MZ','US','CA','GB','EU','AU','NZ','ALL'].forEach(c=>{ … })   …   if(lc !== advCountry) return false;
bugs.fix: Tick by iterating .adv-country-option (as selectAdvCountry does) and treat EU as a group: match when lc is EU or one of its member codes.

bugs.title: Adventures 'Duration' and 'Group Size' filters never narrow real adverts
bugs.scenario: The mapped listing carries neither duration nor groupSize/group_size, and the test only runs when the listing has a value, so choosing 'Half day' or 'Couple' raises the filter badge but leaves the list unchanged.
bugs.evidence: if(fa.duration && fa.duration!=='' && l.duration && l.duration!==fa.duration) return false;  if(fa.groupSize && … (l.groupSize||l.group_size) && …) return false;
bugs.fix: Read the seller's 'Duration' and 'Group size' lines in _msMapBeaListing (as done for Environment) and map them to the sheet's buckets, or remove the two sections until the data exists.

bugs.title: The map popup shows 'NaNkm' for an advert that has its own pin but no suburb coordinates
bugs.scenario: With the buyer's location known, the marker is placed from listing_lat/lng but the distance is computed from suburb_lat/lng; when those are missing the popup reads '· NaNkm'.
bugs.evidence: const dist=buyerLat!=null?` · ${_haversineKm(buyerLat,buyerLng,l.suburb_lat,l.suburb_lng).toFixed(1)}km`:'';
bugs.fix: Compute the distance from the same lat/lng pair used for the marker.

bugs.title: The country filter added to the Browse grid for adventures never runs
bugs.scenario: The test reads l.category, but mapped listings only have l.cat (and advType); l.category is always undefined, so with a country picked the Browse 'All' grid still shows adventures from every country.
bugs.evidence: if (advCountry && advCountry !== 'ALL' && (l.category||'').toLowerCase().indexOf('adventure') !== -1) {
bugs.fix: Use normCat(l.cat)==='Adventures' (or isBorderlessCat(normCat(l.cat))).

bugs.title: openDetail builds the accepted-introduction key with 0 for a missing sellerIdx, but the accept path stores it with 'null', so the description is never unmasked for live adverts.
bugs.scenario: Live (BEA) adverts all carry sellerIdx:null (mapper line 486); the accept path adds `${listing.sellerIdx}-${listing.id}` = 'null-bea_12' (line 12181) while openDetail checks '0-bea_12', so maskContactInfo keeps masking even after acceptance; the two keys can never match.
bugs.evidence: const _introKey = `${l.sellerIdx==null?0:l.sellerIdx}-${l.id}`;  vs  acceptedIntros.add(`${listing.sellerIdx}-${listing.id}`);
bugs.fix: Use one key builder for both sites, e.g. function _introKeyOf(l){ return (l.sellerIdx==null?'x':l.sellerIdx)+'-'+l.id; }, and call it at 6028, 5805 and 12181.

bugs.title: A failed balance lookup is treated as a zero balance, so a buyer with Tuppence is sent to the top-up sheet.
bugs.scenario: When the session cookie has lapsed (localStorage still holds the email) or the network blips, GET /tuppence/balance fails (401/err), bal stays 0 and tvsPriceCheck calls topUpShort(need) - 'You need 1T more - quick top-up open' - although she holds Tuppence; tvsYieldCalc toasts 'Insufficient Tuppence' for the same reason.
bugs.evidence: let bal=0; try{const br=await fetch(BEA_URL+'/tuppence/balance?email='+encodeURIComponent(email),{headers:{'X-Api-Key':API_KEY}}); if(br.ok){...}}catch(_){ }  const need=tier==='2T'?2:1; if(bal<need){ topUpShort(need-bal); return; }
bugs.fix: Only treat bal as known when br.ok; on 401 prompt sign-in, on other failures skip the client pre-check (the server answers 402 when short) - or use the in-memory `tuppence` value kept by _msTnSync.

bugs.title: After a slot-limit 402 the batch loop breaks but then falls through to the generic failure toast or the success screen.
bugs.scenario: Seller has 1 free slot and publishes 3 cards: the first succeeds, the second returns 402, plans open, the loop breaks, then published>0 sends her to the 'published!' success step over the plans sheet; with 0 published she instead sees 'Publishing failed - check your connection' on top of the plans sheet, contradicting the slot message. The button is also left reading '⏳ Publish'.
bugs.evidence:
showToast('Slot limit reached'); openPlans('aa-publish', true);
        btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = '⏳ Publish'; break;
bugs.fix: Set a slotLimited flag on 402 and after the loop return early when it is set (no success step, no failure toast); if some were published, say 'N published - your plan has no free slot for the rest'; reset the label to 'Publish listings ->'.

bugs.title: A seller cannot clear her headline or 'about' text: an emptied box falls back to the old value on Save.
bugs.scenario: She deletes her headline and taps Save; value.trim() is '' so `|| s.headline` keeps the old headline, which is saved to the account again; the same applies to credential label/sub and availability rows.
bugs.evidence: s.headline  = document.getElementById('ce-headline')?.value.trim()   || s.headline;
bugs.fix: Read the box when it exists: const el=document.getElementById('ce-headline'); if(el) s.headline=el.value.trim(); (same for about and the per-row fields).

bugs.title: When only some drafts publish, the seller is shown full success with the FIRST draft's title even if that one failed, and the failure is hidden.
bugs.scenario: Drafts [Cars A, Services B]: A is refused 409 (attestation), B publishes; successCount=1 so phase 4 says '"A" is now live on TrustSquare.', the error written to the phase-3 errEl is never seen, and 'View my listing' / 'Put it on my WhatsApp Status' open draft A, which is still a draft.
bugs.evidence:
titleEl.textContent = count === 1
      ? `"${first.title}" is now live on TrustSquare.`
bugs.fix: Collect the drafts that actually published (push draft on success) and use that list for the title, View and Share buttons; when failCount>0 add a line on the success screen naming the drafts that did not go live and why.

bugs.title: The 'Undo' link after Improve wording can never work: JSON.stringify puts double quotes inside a double-quoted onclick attribute (latent).
bugs.scenario: The attribute is cut at the first quote (onclick="goUndoImprove("), so tapping Undo throws a SyntaxError and the original description is lost; text with < or > also injects markup.
bugs.evidence: onclick="goUndoImprove(' + JSON.stringify(oldText) + ')">Undo';
bugs.fix: Create the link with createElement and a closure: u.textContent='Undo'; u.onclick=()=>goUndoImprove(oldText); statusEl.textContent='✓ Improved · '; statusEl.appendChild(u);

bugs.title: The 'we emailed you a link straight back to this listing' toast is shown even when the server sent no letter.
bugs.scenario: POST /listings only queues the way-back letter when _draft_mail_allowed passes (per-address/IP daily cap, bea_main.py 4251-4259); a seller making a second or third draft that day, or several sellers on one office IP, is told an email is on its way that never arrives. In the publish-now path the same toast says 'Draft saved' while the advert is about to go live.
bugs.evidence: : '✓ Draft saved — we emailed ' + goState.email + ' a link straight back to this listing. It works for a week.', 6000);
bugs.fix: Return a 'return_mailed' boolean from POST /listings and keep the response in goHandoff; show the email sentence only when it is true (else '✓ Draft saved — it is waiting in your Seller Hub'), and skip the toast when !opts.draftOnly && opts.sellFlow (publish follows).

bugs.title: Market-note prompts hard-code 'Pretoria', so sellers elsewhere get Pretoria prices (latent: guided and Path B flows).
bugs.scenario: A Cape Town seller's prompt becomes '... property in Sea Point, Pretoria' and tutors/services always say 'in Pretoria' (also 9972-9981), so the AI answers with Pretoria price ranges.
bugs.evidence: prompt=`In 1 sentence, give a market context note for a ${beds}-bed, ${baths}-bath property in ${sub}, Pretoria${price?' asking '+price:''}. ...`;
bugs.fix: Replace the literal 'Pretoria' with activeCity.name (goState.city in goFetchMarketNote) in every market-note prompt.

bugs.title: The fallback market note presents a fixed R1.8m-R3.2m 'based on recent listings' for every property, rentals and other cities included (latent: Path B).
bugs.scenario: B3 shows the fallback immediately and whenever the AI call fails, so a flat To Rent in Durban is told comparable properties 'are currently asking R1.8m–R3.2m' (and 'A -bed home' while bedrooms is empty).
bugs.evidence: return `A ${beds}-bed home in ${sub} — based on recent listings, comparable properties are currently asking R1.8m–R3.2m depending on finish and size.`;
bugs.fix: Return a neutral 'Add bedrooms and suburb for a market note' when beds is empty and drop the invented range (or derive it from LISTINGS with the same category, city and listing_type).

bugs.title: Description drafts and 'Improve wording' are sent to /advert-agent/market-note, which forces exactly one sentence in at most 120 tokens (latent: all five callers are in dormant flows).
bugs.scenario: B4 asks for 'a 3–5 sentence listing description' and goImproveDescription (9815) for a rewrite 'under 4 sentences', but the server system prompt says 'Respond in exactly 1 sentence ... Mention real price ranges' with max_tokens=120 (bea_main.py 10487-10492); the seller gets a one-sentence, possibly truncated description with an invented price range.
bugs.evidence:
let prompt=`Write a 3–5 sentence listing description for a ${cat} listing ...`;
const res=await fetch(BEA_URL+'/advert-agent/market-note',{
bugs.fix: Use a description endpoint (or a mode:'description' flag on market-note that swaps the system prompt and raises max_tokens to ~400) for sbRenderB4 and goImproveDescription.

bugs.title: msPauseListing sends no email, so Pause/Resume always fails with 'Not your listing' whenever identity binding is in shadow mode.
bugs.scenario: With BUZZ_BIND=0 (the documented no-deploy fallback), _actor returns the passed email unchanged (bea_main.py 8531-8537); the body has none, so actor is '' and pause_listing answers 403 'Not your listing' for the real owner. msKeepLive, beside it, does send email.
bugs.evidence: body: JSON.stringify({pause: !!pause})
bugs.fix: Send the signed-in address like msKeepLive does: body: JSON.stringify({pause: !!pause, email: _msSignedEmail()}) (the gate rebinds it to the session).

bugs.title: Editing a stay's nightly/per-person price when the stored price is 'POA' (or starts with a word) saves a broken price such as 'POA1500 / night'.
bugs.scenario: A stay saved with price 'POA' (dashPublish seeds 'POA' as the default) -> seller types 1500 into 'Price per night' -> the currency symbol is taken as the first 1-3 non-digit characters of the stored price -> payload.price = 'POA1500 / night' (or 'Fro1500 / night' for 'From R...'), which is what buyers then see.
bugs.evidence:
const sym = (stored.match(/^\s*([^0-9\s]{1,3})/) || [])[1] || aaCurrency().symbol;
payload.price = sym + amt + (id === 'price_per_night' ? ' / night' : ' / person');
bugs.fix: Only accept a real currency symbol/code from the stored price (e.g. /^\s*(R|KSh|\$|\u20ac|\u00a3|[A-Z]{3}\s?)(?=\d)/) and otherwise fall back to aaCurrency().symbol; same guard in _elRateWithBasis.

bugs.title: 'My Requests' lists the seller's OWN listings as 'Intro sent', because acceptedIntros is only ever filled when she accepts a request as a seller.
bugs.scenario: Seller accepts a buyer's request in her hub -> handleIntro adds her listing to acceptedIntros (the only writer of that Set) -> she opens My Requests (buyer tab) and sees her own advert with an 'Intro sent' badge, mixed with the introductions she really asked for (and, with the title-match bug, possibly another seller's advert).
bugs.evidence: [...acceptedIntros].forEach(key=>{ ... interacted.push(l); }); const badge=hasIntro?'...Intro sent':...
bugs.fix: Drop the acceptedIntros block from renderMyRequests (msMyIntros already lists her real buyer introductions from the server), or skip listings whose seller is the signed-in user.

bugs.title: 'Apply' on an AI rate suggestion written with a thousands separator (e.g. 'R1,500/month') sets the amount to 1 and blanks the unit.
bugs.scenario: Regex /R?(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(.+)?/ captures '1' and ',500/month'; unitEl.value is set to a non-existent option (blank) and the preview is not refreshed, so the field silently becomes 'R1 /hr' on save.
bugs.fix: Strip grouping (raw.replace(/(\d)[ ,](?=\d{3})/g,'$1')) before matching, only set the unit if an <option> with that value exists, and dispatch 'input' on the amount so the preview updates.

bugs.title: The Coach 'How it works' (?) sheet is blank for Services, Cars and LocalMarket because AA_FLOWS has no entry for those keys.
bugs.scenario: On the details screen with Services selected, '?' calls aaShowFlowSheet('Services'); AA_FLOWS has only 'Services · Technical'/'Services · Casuals' and nothing for Cars/LocalMarket, so aaRenderFlow returns early, no chip is selected and the card area is empty (or shows the previous card).
bugs.evidence:
const flow = AA_FLOWS[cat];
  if (!flow) return;
bugs.fix: Map the selected category (+service_class) to an AA_FLOWS key ('Services · '+label), add Cars and Local Market flows, and fall back to 'Property' instead of returning.

bugs.title: bzEnablePush sends the localStorage email to /buyer-token, which refuses (401) unless it equals the session email exactly, although buzzRender already knows the server's spelling.
bugs.scenario: localStorage holds 'David@x.com' or an old address while the session is 'david@x.com'; /buyer-token compares _sess != req.email.strip().lower() -> 401 'Please sign in to link this device', and the switch toast says 'Could not link this account to push' with no reason.
bugs.evidence: body: JSON.stringify({email: email})   // email = bzEmail() = localStorage ms_aa_email
bugs.fix: Pass the email returned by /buzz/me (store it in a module variable in buzzRender) and lowercase it; surface the server detail in the thrown Error.

bugs.title: Trust score fallback is 15 although every account's baseline is 40.
bugs.scenario: First visit to My Space (no cached ms_trust_score) or a failed /trust fetch: the card shows 15% and '25 points to Some evidence', then jumps to 40 when the live call returns; offline it stays wrong. Same constant at 18784.
bugs.evidence: const storedTrust = parseInt(localStorage.getItem('ms_trust_score')) || 15;
bugs.fix: Use 40 (the 'Established base') as the fallback in both places, or show '–' until the live score arrives.

bugs.title: Intro list dates parse SQLite timestamps with new Date(raw), unlike the rest of the slice.
bugs.scenario: intro_requests.created_at is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' in UTC. new Date() reads it as local time, so a request made between 22:00 and 24:00 UTC shows the previous day for a South African user, and older iOS Safari returns Invalid Date, so the row reads 'Listing #12 · Invalid Date'. _fmtDate (18324) already does replace(' ','T')+'Z'.
bugs.evidence: (i.created_at ? new Date(i.created_at).toLocaleDateString('en-ZA',{day:'numeric',month:'short'}) : '–')
bugs.fix: Use new Date(String(i.created_at).replace(' ','T') + (/[zZ]|[+-]\d\d:?\d\d$/.test(i.created_at)?'':'Z')) and guard isNaN.

bugs.title: With the batch photo grid on (switched off: DCB-001), a photo the multi-photo AI read rejects as off-category is removed from sfState.files but not from sfState.dcb.items, so it comes back and is uploaded.
bugs.scenario: DCB on, seller adds a boat photo as photo 3 of a Cars listing; sfRunMultiVision deletes sfState.files[k] and toasts 'removed', but the next cover tap / move / drag runs sfDcbApply, which rebuilds sfState.files from d.items and restores it; mvSig is unchanged so it is never re-checked and it publishes.
bugs.evidence:
if(!sfDcbOn()) sfRevokeUrl(sfState.previews[k]);   // PHOTO-SMALL-1 (DCB tiles still show theirs)
      delete sfState.files[k]; delete sfState.previews[k];
bugs.fix: When sfDcbOn(), also remove the item from sfState.dcb.items (match it.slot===k), revoke its preview and call sfDcbApply(true); or mark it.rejected=true and make sfDcbApply skip rejected items for every slot, not only 'main'.

bugs.title: The area box keeps offering the previous city's suburbs after the city changes, because the list is only replaced when the new city has suburbs and the datalist ignores which city it belongs to.
bugs.scenario: A seller who browsed Pretoria (118 seeded suburbs) switches to Durban and sells: /suburbs?city=Durban returns [], sfLoadSuburbs keeps _sfSuburbs/_sfSuburbsCity as Pretoria, and sfSpecS still adds list="sf-area-dl" with Pretoria's suburbs to the Durban listing's area field.
bugs.evidence:
if(Array.isArray(list)&&list.length){ _sfSuburbs=list; _sfSuburbsCity=city; ... }
var _dl=(root && id==='__area' && _sfSuburbs.length)?' list="sf-area-dl"':'';
bugs.fix: In sfLoadSuburbs set _sfSuburbs=list||[] and _sfSuburbsCity=city on every answer; in sfSpecS require _sfSuburbsCity===(sfState.city||activeCity.name) before adding the datalist.

bugs.title: A structured error from the plan payment call is shown as '[object Object]'
bugs.scenario: If the Terms/consent loop ends still on HTTP 428 (detail is an object) or the server answers 422 (detail is a list), the toast prints the object instead of a message.
bugs.evidence: showToast(d.detail || 'Payment init failed');
bugs.fix: Show typeof d.detail==='string' ? d.detail : (d.detail && d.detail.message) || 'Could not start the payment — please try again.'

bugs.title: The seller profile shows 'Loading credential evidence…' for ever when the credentials request fails
bugs.scenario: For a listing with no stored signals the block starts as 'Loading credential evidence…'. If /sellers/credentials answers 404/500 or the network drops, the code returns without touching the element and the catch is empty.
bugs.evidence: var el=document.getElementById('bea-creds-'+l.id); if(!el||!d) return;   …   }).catch(function(){});
bugs.fix: On !d or catch write a final state, e.g. 'No verified credentials to show yet.' / 'Could not load — tap to retry'.

bugs.title: saveCVEdit writes base64 certificate photos into localStorage without a try/catch, so a large photo makes Save throw and do nothing.
