bugs.scenario: handleCredPhoto keeps any file up to 2 MB as a raw data URL (about 2.7 M characters) in editingSeller.creds; with the profile photo already stored, localStorage.setItem('ms_seller_profile', ...) exceeds the quota and throws QuotaExceededError - the server save, the toast and the return to the dashboard never run, so the Save button appears dead.
bugs.evidence: localStorage.setItem('ms_seller_profile', JSON.stringify(s));
bugs.fix: Wrap the setItem in try/catch and store the profile without photo data (strip creds[i].photo or keep only a server URL); always compress certificate photos with aaCompressImage rather than only above 2 MB.

bugs.title: 'Link copied' is shown even when the clipboard write is refused.
bugs.scenario: navigator.clipboard.writeText returns a promise; a permission refusal (common in in-app WebViews) rejects asynchronously, so the try/catch never sees it and the worker is told the employer link was copied when it was not.
bugs.evidence: try{ navigator.clipboard.writeText(j.url); showToast('Link copied', 2500); }catch(_){ showToast('Press and hold the link to copy it', 4000); }
bugs.fix: Chain the promise: navigator.clipboard.writeText(j.url).then(()=>showToast('Link copied',2500), ()=>showToast('Press and hold the link to copy it',4000)); keep the sync catch for a missing navigator.clipboard.

bugs.title: Listing-languages Approve and Remove buttons have no failure path for network errors (Remove has none for server errors either), so a failed tap shows nothing.
bugs.scenario: Seller taps 'Remove FR' and the server answers 4xx, or she is offline when tapping Approve -> post() rejects or r.ok is false -> no message is written to #el-lang-msg and no catch exists (unhandled rejection); she cannot tell whether her second language is live.
bugs.evidence: post('/lang/remove').then(function(r){ if(r.ok){ msg('Removed. ...'); refresh(); } }); };
bugs.fix: Add `else msg((r.j&&r.j.detail)||'Could not remove.',true)` and `.catch(function(){ msg('No connection \u2014 nothing changed.',true); })` to both Approve and Remove, as draft() already does; also make post() tolerate a non-JSON body (r.json() throws on a 502 HTML page).

bugs.title: On the first-publish Terms path (409 need=eula) the number of photos held back by the privacy check is dropped, although the server returns photos_held there too.
bugs.scenario: First-time seller publishes with a photo showing her house number; server returns 409 {need:'eula', photos_held:1}; the toast only says 'Saved. One step left…' and the photo silently disappears.
bugs.evidence: showToast('Saved. One step left: read and accept the Terms to go live.', 5000);
bugs.fix: Read _pj.photos_held and append the same 'N photo(s) held back … add another in Edit' text used on the success path.

bugs.title: Squire seller answer (and brief delete) swallow server failures (flag-dark).
bugs.scenario: A seller answers a brief and the server returns 404/401 (e.g. session expired): nothing happens, no toast, the text stays. sqDelete (18914) never checks r.ok and has no confirm, so a failed delete silently reloads the same list.
bugs.evidence: if(r.ok){ showToast('✓ Answer sent'); msRenderSquireInbox(); } }catch(e){}
bugs.fix: Add else-branches that toast the server detail (d.detail) and a catch toast 'Could not reach the server'; in sqDelete check r.ok and confirm() first.

bugs.title: Any poll answer without a known status (e.g. a 404/500 JSON from /ai/jobs/{id}) is reported as 'run failed — your hold was released, you were NOT charged'.
bugs.scenario: A transient server error returns {detail:'…'}: j.status is undefined, the poll stops and tells a paying user the run failed and was not charged, while the job may still finish and charge. The fetch never checks r.ok.
bugs.evidence: let j; try{ j = await (await fetch('/ai/jobs/'+jobId)).json(); }catch(e){ return; }
bugs.fix: Check r.ok and that j.status is one of queued/running/delivered/failed before acting; on anything else keep polling (with a retry cap) instead of declaring failure.

bugs.title: Guided onboarding reuses the seller's most recent draft and PUTs the new item onto it without category, and never checks the PUT result (latent).
bugs.scenario: A returning seller with an unfinished Property draft starts a Collectors item; goInit sets listingId = drafts[0].id, then goSaveAndNext/goHandoff PUT title/price/description onto that Property draft (no category in the body) and append the new photos, overwriting the old draft; a failed PUT (10049, 10255) is swallowed and the seller proceeds as if saved.
bugs.evidence:
if (drafts.length) goState.listingId = drafts[0].id;
await fetch(BEA_URL + '/listings/' + goState.listingId + '?email=' + ..., { method: 'PUT', ... }).catch(() => {});
bugs.fix: Only reuse a draft whose normCat(category) matches goState.cat (else create a new one), include category in the PUT body, and treat !res.ok as a failure that sets goPublishError and shows it.

bugs.title: Path B: edits to the B4 description are not saved after a resumed draft, so the old text is published (latent: sell-b is dormant while SF_ENABLED).
bugs.scenario: Seller resumes a saved draft after a reload; sbRenderB4 takes the early-return branch because sbState.description is set, so no input listener is attached (the textarea has no oninput in the markup) and sbDoPublish sends the old description (line 11536).
bugs.evidence:
if(sbState.description){ ... if(descTa)descTa.value=sbState.description; ... return; }
if(descTa) descTa.addEventListener('input',()=>{ sbState.description=descTa.value; });
bugs.fix: Bind before the early return with a property: descTa.oninput = () => { sbState.description = descTa.value; }; (also stops duplicate listeners on every re-generation).

bugs.title: The Property edit form shows a 'Street address' box that always opens empty and silently discards whatever the seller types.
bugs.scenario: Property seller opens Edit -> _elFieldVal has no 'street_address' entry (and the public GET hides it), so the box is blank -> she re-types her address and taps Save -> saveEditedListing never puts street_address in the payload, yet the toast says 'changes are live'; distance-to-schools data keeps the old/no address.
bugs.evidence:
const map = { title: raw.title || '', price: ..., suburb: raw.suburb || '', ... };   // no street_address
if (fd.suburb)       payload.suburb       = fd.suburb;   // no street_address line in saveEditedListing
bugs.fix: Either drop street_address from the edit form (filter it out in renderEditForm) or read it from the owner-only /listings/mine row and send `payload.street_address` when the typed value differs; never write it into the description.

bugs.title: lmSubmitIntro writes the 'Introduction request sent' wallet row before the server answers, so refused requests (Terms declined, 401, 402, 403, 410, 429, network) leave a phantom pending row.
bugs.scenario: Buyer in 7-day cooldown taps Request introduction; server returns 429 cooldown; toast explains, but the wallet history now shows a pending introduction that does not exist (and a second one after the sign-in retry path).
bugs.evidence: addTx('Introduction request sent', _lmEsc(lmTitle), 'pending', false);
bugs.fix: Move addTx after the resp.ok check (just before the success toast).

bugs.title: Leave-screen, plan-change and remove-agent questions use the browser's own confirm()/prompt() boxes, which the language layer cannot translate.
bugs.scenario: The app translates by re-wording page elements. A reader using isiZulu or Afrikaans who presses Back on a half-filled form, or switches plan, gets an English system box ('Leave this screen? What you have entered here will be lost.', 'Switch to Free (2 listing slots)? ...') on an otherwise translated screen.
bugs.evidence: !confirm('Leave this screen? What you have entered here will be lost.')){ stay(); return; }
bugs.fix: Replace confirm()/prompt() at 2437, 2444, 2499, 2733, 2923, 2937 and 2984 with an in-app confirm sheet built from normal elements (one helper returning a Promise), so the language layer and the app's own styling apply.

bugs.title: Native prompt()/confirm() dialogs carry English the translation layer can never reach, on screens the reader has switched to isiZulu/Afrikaans.
bugs.scenario: A reader with the page in Afrikaans taps 'Plan my trip with this agent' (prompt at 23261) or switches category/kind in Sell (confirm at 21181, 21197, 21205, 21213, 21624): the box is English only — the same reason SF-EMAIL-FIELD-1 removed the email prompt() — and some in-app browsers suppress prompt() entirely, so the introduction cannot be requested at all.
bugs.evidence:
var wish=prompt(_v==='travel'?'What are you dreaming of? (destination, dates, people — no phone numbers needed)':...,'');
if(!confirm('Start a new '+sfCatName(cat)+' listing?\n\nThe photos and answers of your '+sfCatName(sfState.cat)+' listing will be removed.')) return;
bugs.fix: Replace these with in-page sheets (a small textarea + Send under the agent card; a two-button confirm card in the sell flow) built from DOM text so the translation layer paints them.

bugs.title: Batch analysis checks for 1T although it costs 2T, so a seller with 1T confirms a 2T spend and then gets a bare 'Insufficient Tuppence'.
bugs.scenario: Balance is 1T: bal<1 is false, the confirm says 'This will use 2T', the server's _require_tuppence(2) answers 402, and the app toasts 'Insufficient Tuppence' with no top-up path (the short path, topUpShort(2-bal), is only reached at 0T).
bugs.evidence:
if (bal < 1) {
    topUpShort(2 - bal);
bugs.fix: Change the guard to if (bal < 2) and on the 402 branch call topUpShort(2) instead of a toast.

bugs.title: After a paid (1T) Coach call the app ignores tuppence_remaining, so the shown Tuppence balance stays 1T too high until a reload/sync.
bugs.scenario: Seller with 5T runs the Coach a second time; server deducts 1T and returns tuppence_remaining=4, but the header/wallet still show 5T.
bugs.evidence:
const data = await res.json();
    const coachSuggestions = data.coaching_json || {};
bugs.fix: After success: if (typeof data.tuppence_remaining==='number') { tuppence = data.tuppence_remaining; refresh the balance display } or call msSyncBalance().

bugs.title: The Tutors Coach flow tells tutors to photograph themselves ('A photo of you…'), and its only required slot is a 'Professional headshot', contradicting anonymity until both accept; the server's photo gate then blurs or holds it.
bugs.scenario: A tutor follows the explainer, uploads a headshot as the one required photo; either the face is published before any introduction, or the anonymity gate holds it and the advert goes live photo-less with a 'held back' toast.
bugs.evidence:
{ n:'2', col:'c-blue',  title:'Capture 1 required photo',
        sub:'A photo of you in your teaching environment' },   // slot definition ms.js 14723: {slot:'profile', label:'Profile photo', hint:'Professional headshot', required:true}
bugs.fix: Change the required Tutors slot to a teaching-workspace/material photo (no face) and reword the explainer accordingly.

bugs.title: goInit writes the URL-supplied invite name into innerHTML unescaped (reflected XSS via ?magic=1&name=), latent behind SF_ENABLED.
bugs.scenario: magicLink.name comes straight from the query string (ms.js 1276-1279). If guided-onboard is re-enabled for rollback, a link like /?magic=1&name=<img/src=x/onerror=...> runs script on trustsquare.co (split(' ') keeps a space-free payload whole). Today guided-onboard is only routed to when SF_ENABLED is false.
bugs.evidence: c1.innerHTML = 'Hi ' + goState.name.split(' ')[0] + '! Add 1–12 photos ...';
bugs.fix: Escape it: 'Hi ' + _lmEsc(goState.name.split(' ')[0]) + '! ...' (same at 9721 for the AI shot label, and _lmEsc the AI strings s.label/s.reason/t/warnings at 9577, 9653-9654, 9683).

bugs.title: AI text and the seller's own document labels are inserted into the edit screen as raw HTML (upload comment, anonymity warning, photo warning, rewrite/audit/yield results, document label).
bugs.scenario: A document label or listing field containing markup (or an AI reply steered by it, e.g. label 'Cert ') is echoed: d.label in the doc list, commentRes.comment after upload, cj.anonymity_warning in #el-ai-output and photoWarning under the cover photo all go through innerHTML unescaped. Today this is the seller's own data (self-XSS), but it is one shared render path away from other viewers.
bugs.evidence:
${d.label}
✨ ${commentRes.comment} ⚠️ ${cj.anonymity_warning}
bugs.fix: Wrap each in _lmEsc(): d.label, d.url (attribute), commentRes.comment, cj.anonymity_warning, photoWarning in elRenderPhotos (12799) and its , data.new_title/new_description (14035-14036), a.step/a.reason (14074-14075) and data.market_context (14148).

bugs.title: AI coach plan text (action, why, needs, intro, closing) is inserted as raw HTML.
bugs.scenario: /trust-score/guidance returns model-written JSON; any '<' or markup in s.action / s.why / data.closing is parsed as HTML in My Space (layout break at best, injected markup if the model echoes hostile text).
bugs.evidence:
'
'+(s.action||'')+'
'
bugs.fix: Escape every model field with _lmEsc() at 19447, 19458, 19459, 19570 and 19572.

bugs.title: Verified-tier cards (flag-dark) put model-supplied o.grad into a style attribute and o.emoji as raw HTML.
bugs.scenario: When verified_visible is armed, an 'options' JSON block with grad:'red" onmouseover="…' breaks out of style="…" and o.emoji can carry markup; both bypass the aiEsc used for the other fields.
bugs.evidence:
'
…'+(o.emoji||'\uD83D\uDCCD')+''
bugs.fix: Accept grad only if it matches /^linear-gradient\([#\d\w\s,.%()-]+\)$/ (else default) and aiEsc(o.emoji).

bugs.title: The 40 s vision timeout does not abort the fetch, so a late answer overwrites the title the seller typed since (latent).
bugs.scenario: Server answers at 40-45 s after the seller chose 'Fill in manually' and typed a title; goRevealDraft still sets goState.fields.title/price to the AI values (9694-9695) while the input keeps her text, and the AI title is saved.
bugs.evidence: const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => { ... goVisionFallback('AI analysis timed out. ...'); }, 40000);
bugs.fix: Use an AbortController: pass signal to fetch, ctl.abort() in the timeout, and return early on AbortError.

bugs.title: Advert detail wonders/POI strips have no request guard, so a slow answer for the previous advert paints into the one now open.
bugs.scenario: On a slow connection a buyer opens advert A then quickly advert B; A's /listings/A/wonders (or /listings/A POI fetch at 19158) resolves after B's and replaces B's strip with A's nearby wonders/amenities.
bugs.fix: Capture a token (e.g. const tok = ++_detailSeq or the listing id) before the await and return if the open detail is no longer that listing.

bugs.title: AI photo picker hangs forever on a file the browser cannot decode (no onerror on the Image/FileReader promises).
bugs.scenario: On Android Chrome a user picks a HEIC photo (accept=image/*): im.onload never fires, the for-loop awaits forever, later photos are never added, no thumbnail and no message, and the input is never reset.
bugs.evidence: const img = await new Promise(res=>{const im=new Image();im.onload=()=>res(im);im.src=url;});
bugs.fix: Add im.onerror=()=>res(null) (and r.onerror) and skip null images with showToast('That photo format is not supported — use JPG or PNG').

bugs.title: Door swipe counts any 55px horizontal drift as a category change, so a vertical scroll of the (now scrollable) door switches category and redraws it.
bugs.scenario: On a 360x640 phone the door scrolls (DOOR-FIT-1); a thumb scroll down to 'Pass Quick on' that drifts 60px sideways fires swipe(), the category changes and the door redraws, losing her scroll position and any open door card.
bugs.evidence:
var dx=e.changedTouches[0].clientX-sx; sx=null;
  if(Math.abs(dx)>55) swipe(dx<0?1:-1);  (2355-2356)
bugs.fix: Record clientY in touchstart and only swipe when Math.abs(dx)>55 && Math.abs(dx)>2*Math.abs(dy), and ignore touches that start inside a scrollable child or an overlay.

bugs.title: Escape and the phone back gesture call back.onclick directly, which neither closes the How guide overlay (its close is an addEventListener click) nor respects a focused text box.
bugs.scenario: A tester opens 'How' on a question and presses the phone's Back: popstate calls $('back').onclick(), Quick steps back underneath, but #qhov stays over the screen and the button still reads 'Quick'. Pressing Escape while typing her email on the draft likewise jumps back a question.
bugs.evidence: document.addEventListener('keydown',function(e){ if(mode){ if(e.key==='Escape') $('back').onclick(); return; }  (2358-2359)  |  ['back','home'].forEach(function(id){ var x=document.getElementById(id); if(x) x.addEventListener('click', qHelpClose); });  (1326)
bugs.fix: Call $('back').click() instead of .onclick() (in the keydown and popstate handlers) so every click listener runs, and close #qhov first if it is open; skip the Escape shortcut when e.target is an INPUT/TEXTAREA.

bugs.title: After the Google round trip the draft can be restored before /quick/me answers, and nothing redraws it, so a signed-in seller still sees the email/name boxes and 'Save my listing'.
bugs.scenario: restore() runs 60 ms after the door; qMeApply later sets QUICK.member/eula but does not repaint the draft. She sees 'Your email — introductions reach you here' after signing in with Google (and 'Save my listing' even if she can publish); the tap does use the session, so the boxes are dead.
bugs.evidence: if(window._qResumeNow){ window._qResumeNow=false; setTimeout(function(){ restore(w); }, 60); }
bugs.fix: Restore after window.qMe settles: (window.qMe||Promise.resolve()).then(function(){ restore(w); }); or make qMeApply call drawDraft() when mode==='sell' and the draft is on screen.

bugs.title: 'Quote first' (Casuals rate screen), 'Ask me' and 'Free quote' prices are sent as the literal text instead of POA, so the server awards the 6 price points the coaching says a quote does not earn, and the card price stays English.
bugs.scenario: A Casuals worker picks 'Quote first' on the rate screen (or types 'ask me' on the price card): the pick label goes through priceWithBasis unchanged, POST stores price='Quote first', _import_quality_score counts it as a price (+6; only 'POA' scores 0) and lsOf adds the same 6, while the coaching line says 'Put a price on it — asking for a quote scores nothing'. An Afrikaans or isiZulu seller's stored price is English.
bugs.evidence: if(!PRICE_BASIS[key] || !/\d/.test(l) || /\/|\bper\b|ask|quote|poa/i.test(l)) return l;  (1400)  |  if (d.get("price") or "").strip() and (d.get("price") or "").strip().upper() != "POA": score += 6  (bea_main.py 4649)
bugs.fix: In the base priceWithBasis return 'POA' when the label has no digit and matches /ask|quote/i, and in lsOf only add the 6 points when the pick label contains a digit (mirroring the server once it receives 'POA').

bugs.title: The Buzz example's reply button takes the first word of the sender's name, producing 'Buzz Mrs back', 'Buzz Mr back', 'Buzz Kruger back', 'Buzz Bekker back'.
bugs.scenario: Housekeeping draft -> 'See how it works' -> switch both permissions on -> choose 'Mrs Nkosi -> you' -> Buzz: the reply button reads 'Buzz Mrs back' (tutors: 'Buzz Mr back'; adventures: 'Buzz Kruger back').
bugs.evidence:
+'
' (2068)
bugs.fix: Use the full name when it starts with a title or is an organisation: e.g. var nm=/^(Mr|Mrs|Ms|Dr)\b/.test(f.name)||!/\s/.test(f.name)?f.name:f.name.split(' ')[0]; or simply 'Reply' / 'Buzz back'.

bugs.title: The asking-price parser treats any 'm' or 'k' after a digit as million/thousand, so '8 500 month' or '850 000 market related' becomes billions.
bugs.scenario: On 'What is the rent a month?' she types '8 500 month': /\d\s*m/ matches '0 m', mul=1e6, the label becomes 'R8 500 000 000 / month'. She must notice it in the Next button text.
bugs.evidence: mul=/\d\s*m/.test(raw)?1e6:(/\d\s*k/.test(raw)?1e3:1);
bugs.fix: Only accept a unit directly after the number and nothing alphabetic after it: var mm=/(\d[\d.,\s]*)\s*(m|mil|million|k)\b/i.exec(raw); and ignore words like 'month', 'market'.

bugs.title: Picking a one-city country clears the city that applyPack just set, so she is asked 'Which city?' with a single chip.
bugs.scenario: Change country -> Kenya: applyPack sets QCITY='Nairobi' (the 'one live city: nothing to ask' branch), then the click handler sets window.QCITY=null and drawStep shows drawCityPick with only Nairobi.
bugs.evidence: if(k!==QCC){ applyPack(k); localNames(); } window.QCITY=null; window.QCITY_OTHER=null; drawStep();
bugs.fix: Clear QCITY before applyPack, not after: window.QCITY=null; window.QCITY_OTHER=null; if(k!==QCC){ applyPack(k); localNames(); } else if(Object.keys(QP.cities).length===1) setCity(Object.keys(QP.cities)[0],false);

bugs.title: A member's banner city is set to the timezone default suburb (always 'Menlyn') instead of her own city.
bugs.scenario: A signed-in seller in Durban opens Quick: the localStorage branch sets QUICK.city=LOC.suburb ('Menlyn'); /quick/me only replaces it when users.last_city is non-empty, so a member with no last_city sees 'Saving as Thandi · Menlyn' on her draft. joinThen (1698) does the same.
bugs.evidence: QUICK.city=LOC.suburb;  (1360, 1698)  |  if(d.city){ QUICK.city=d.city; if(!mode) LOC.city=d.city; }  (1381)
bugs.fix: Initialise QUICK.city='' in the localStorage branch and joinThen, and fill it only from /quick/me d.city (or from the 'where' pick once she has answered).

bugs.title: Picking the 'Other' make chip stores make='Other', which earns the make field's listing-score points and titles the advert 'Bakkie — Other'.
bugs.scenario: Cars sell, 'Which make?' -> 'Other': make='Other' is sent as a real make, the server counts make as filled (+10 of the 50 field points) and draftTitle builds 'Bakkie — Other'; buyers searching by make never find it.
bugs.evidence: {"q": "Which make?", "key": "make", "kind": "chip", "tiles": [... {"t": "Other"}]}  (484)  |  var pk=pickOf(k); if(!pk) return; body[f]= ... pk.label;  (1436-1437)
bugs.fix: Make the 'Other' chip open drawFree (the 'Another option' card) instead of committing, or skip make in handoverPayload when the label is 'Other' so the field stays empty and the coaching asks for it.

bugs.title: Several strings on translated screens never translate: most trust-credential names in the score panel and four Buzz-screen strings.
bugs.scenario: With isiZulu or Afrikaans chosen, the draft's 'what raises your trust score' block shows 'Item provenance documentation', 'Roadworthy certificate', 'Formal trade certificate', 'Current first aid', 'SACE registration', 'Vehicle ownership (NaTIS)' etc. in English, and the Buzz screen shows 'You → Mrs Nkosi', 'Mrs Nkosi → you', 'On Mrs Nkosi’s phone, right now' and 'One line each way. Whoever answers, their name is on it too.' in English (checked by running qTr against QI18N for zu and af). The input placeholders K.sample and 'What X would say, in one line' are never passed through qTr, and the aria-labels 'Back', 'Start again', 'Previous category', 'Next category' stay English for screen-reader users.
bugs.evidence:
cars: [['Vehicle ownership (NaTIS)',10],['Roadworthy certificate',6]], (1056) | +'
' (2015) | box.innerHTML='
On '+phoneOf(t)+', right now
' (2064)
bugs.fix: Add the missing credential names and the Buzz sentences to roles/quick_i18n.json (the Buzz ones as regex entries with the name as a capture group, or split the name into its own node as was done for 'Let X buzz me'), wrap placeholders in qTr(), and set aria-labels through qTr in setNav/drawDoor.

bugs.title: Switching language leaves screens whose text was produced with qTr()/T() (Find results, placeholders, the area-count button) in the old language, even when switching back to English.
bugs.scenario: She searches in isiZulu; drawLookup builds every string with T() and qTranslate records that Zulu text as the node's 'English' (__en). She taps EN: qNextSetLang only redraws the door or the draft, qTranslate restores __en, so the results stay Zulu; a reviewer cannot flip this screen back as the language layer promises.
bugs.evidence: if(!mode) drawDoor(); else if(mode==='sell' && !atBuzz && step>=flow().steps.length) drawDraft();  /  if(n.__tr===undefined || n.nodeValue!==n.__tr) n.__en=n.nodeValue;
bugs.fix: In qNextSetLang also redraw the current screen: else if(mode==='find' && step>=flow().steps.length) drawLookup(); else if(mode) drawStep(); (and keep English source text in the DOM, translating only via qTranslate, so __en is real English).

bugs.title: The newest door strings are missing from the embedded dictionary, so they stay English on a translated door.
bugs.scenario: A Sepedi or isiZulu reader opens Quick: 'Listed with us before? Sign in', 'My listings', 'Your listing is waiting — open it to publish', 'See, edit or publish what you have listed', 'My TrustSquare', 'Continue with Google', 'or use your email', 'Browse everything on TrustSquare' and the two add-to-home-screen hints are not keys in QI18N.w, so qTr returns them unchanged.
bugs.evidence: html='<button type="button" class="qdoorin" id="qdoorhub">'+qTr('Listed with us before? Sign in')+' ›</button>';
bugs.fix: Add these nine strings to roles/quick_i18n.json (af/zu/xh/nso) and regenerate the QUICK-I18N block.

interface.issue: The site keeps three separate language settings (app = Afrikaans, Quick = English, help = Sepedi on your browser), so a person who chose Afrikaans in the app opens Quick in English.
interface.suggestion: Use one shared language setting for the app, Quick and help, and migrate the two older keys into it on first load.

interface.issue: The advert page is half translated: 'PRICE', 'Listing / To Rent', 'Type', 'Bedrooms', 'View on map' and 'Request introduction' stay English beside Afrikaans lines.
interface.suggestion: Route every label on the advert page through the dictionary and add a check that fails when a visible label on a translated screen has no entry.

interface.issue: The wallet card reads '365 {Tuppence}' — the curly braces of an unfilled placeholder are shown to the user.
interface.suggestion: Fill the placeholder before painting, and make the translate helper strip or log any '{…}' left in its output.

interface.area: All main screens — floating language pill
interface.issue: The floating 'Afrikaans' pill sits on top of content on Home, Browse, Wallet, My Space and Trust — it covered a heading, a card badge, the Tuppence price line and a trust row — and it repeats the language button already in the header.
interface.suggestion: Remove the floating pill and keep the header language button, or show the pill once on first visit and then retire it.

interface.issue: At 390px in Afrikaans the TrustSquare logo is squeezed to 43×30px and unreadable, because 'Verkopersentrum' takes 144px of the header.
interface.suggestion: Give the logo a fixed minimum width and shrink the hub button to an icon (or two lines) on narrow screens.

interface.issue: Most text is under 12px on a phone: Home 22 of 29 visible texts, Browse 17 of 37, Advert 17 of 30, Wallet 12 of 27 — the menu labels are 10px and some badges 8–9px.
interface.suggestion: Set a floor of 12px for labels and badges and 15–16px for body text, in one place in ms.css, and remove the smaller inline sizes.

interface.issue: The selected tab label has a contrast of 1.5 to 1 (dark blue on navy) and the '365 T' pill 1.6 to 1 — the tab you are on is the least readable thing on the screen.
interface.suggestion: Show the selected tab in white or gold with an underline, and give the balance pill light text.

interface.issue: The Publish button sits about two screens below the top of the draft (the language chips alone end near 1,010px on a 630px screen), so the main action is out of sight.
interface.suggestion: Pin a Publish bar to the bottom of the draft screen, with the score and language choices scrolling above it.

interface.issue: Many controls are smaller than a fingertip: Browse has 16 under 40px and the advert page 11 — Back is 34×34, filter chips 34 high, 'Alles →' 47×20, the examples switch 143×24.
interface.suggestion: Give every tappable control a 44×44px minimum hit area (padding, not bigger text).

interface.issue: The first advert starts three-quarters of the way down the first screen: the title, a Local Market banner, the chips, the search box, the filter button, the count row and an agent banner all come first.
interface.suggestion: Show adverts directly under the search box and move both banners below the first row of results.

interface.issue: The search hint stays English on the Afrikaans screen, is cut off mid-sentence, and offers 'BMW 1996' on the Property page.
interface.suggestion: Translate the hint, keep it to four or five words, and take its example from the category being browsed.

interface.issue: One wallet sentence switches language halfway ('…apart van die 1T-voorstellingsfooi: a report can lead you to a listing…') and the AI service descriptions are English.
interface.suggestion: Translate the whole paragraph and the service descriptions, or show the block in one language only.

interface.issue: My Space scrolls sideways at 390px, and the tab row is cut off at 'Fakturering' with nothing to show there are more tabs.
interface.suggestion: Remove the overflow and fade the right edge of the tab row (or wrap the tabs) so hidden tabs are discoverable.

interface.issue: On the 'Request introduction · 1T by aanvaarding' button the cost is the smallest text, in a different stretched font, and '1T' is not explained.
interface.suggestion: Write the cost in the same font at readable size, in words: 'Free to ask — 1 Tuppence (R33) only if the seller accepts'.

interface.issue: Points a seller has not earned yet are shown with a red ✗ and red '+15 beskikbaar', which reads as failure, and the 'Laai ID op' button is squeezed into the middle of its row.
interface.suggestion: Show unearned points in a neutral or blue 'available' style with a + icon, and put the action button on its own line.

interface.issue: The heading 'Bekende plekke naby' breaks into three lines because two dropdowns share its row.
interface.suggestion: Put the two dropdowns on their own row under the heading at phone width.

interface.issue: Every tap on Sell first asks the seller to confirm her account ('Gaan voort met hierdie rekening') before she can choose what to sell.
interface.suggestion: Skip this sheet when there is one account and keep 'Use another account' as a small link on the Sell screen.

interface.issue: With examples switched off, three of the six category tiles show '0 advertensies', so half of Home looks empty.
interface.suggestion: On an empty tile replace the count with an invitation ('Be the first — list here') or move empty categories to the end.

interface.issue: The door has two language controls — the 'EN' button at the top and a row of five language chips at the bottom.
interface.suggestion: Keep the chip row (full language names) on the door and drop the 'EN' code button there.

interface.issue: The Next button is at the bottom of the screen, far from the amount box, where the phone keyboard will cover it.
interface.suggestion: Place Next directly under the amount box.

interface.issue: A flat 'To Rent' shows 'R20,990' with no 'per month'.
interface.suggestion: Print the price basis beside every rental price.

interface.issue: Tile names in the stretched display font sit on busy photos and are hard to read, and all six tiles carry the same subtitle.
interface.suggestion: Put a dark band behind the tile name and give each tile its own one-line subtitle, or none.

interface.issue: The Tuppence balance appears three times on one screen (header pill, wallet card, menu badge).
interface.suggestion: Keep the wallet card and the menu badge and drop the header pill.

interface.issue: Working well, keep it: five taps took me from the door to a finished draft, each choice is shown back in the trail, and the Next button repeats the answer ('Next — R300 / day').
interface.suggestion: Use this flow as the pattern for the main app's Sell screens.

interface.issue: 300 tappable items are plain boxes with a click handler and only 2 of them are marked as buttons, so keyboard and screen-reader users cannot use most of the app.
interface.suggestion: Turn them into real <button> elements (or add role, tabindex and Enter/Space handling in one shared helper).

interface.issue: 27 of the 51 form fields have no label — 24 rely on grey hint text that disappears as soon as she types.
interface.suggestion: Give every field a visible label above it and keep the hint for an example.

interface.issue: The app uses the browser's own pop-ups 33 times (27 confirm, 6 prompt), including for money decisions; they cannot be translated, styled or explained.
interface.suggestion: Replace them with the app's own bottom sheet, with the cost and the consequence written out.

interface.issue: 436 messages are shown as short toasts and there is no live region, so a screen reader never announces them and long warnings vanish before they are read.
interface.suggestion: Add one aria-live region for toasts and keep any message longer than one line on screen until it is dismissed.

interface.area: Look and feel — colours and styles
interface.issue: There is no single palette: 161 different colour values in ms.css, 223 more inside ms.js, 100 in Quick, and 852 inline style attributes in the app's markup.
interface.suggestion: Define about 20 named colours and a type scale once and replace inline values as each screen is next touched.

interface.issue: Motion and dark-mode preferences are honoured in only one place each, and there are 13 focus styles against 31 'outline: none' rules, so keyboard focus is often invisible.
interface.suggestion: Add a visible focus ring to every control and respect 'reduce motion' on every animation.

interface.issue: A banned or cooling-off seller sees machine codes: the form prints 'Error: permanent_lm_ban' or 'Error: cooling_off_until_2026-11-02T09:14:03.123456+00:00'.
interface.suggestion: Return a plain sentence with a readable date (the wording already exists in lm_suspension_check at 14031 / 14041) and keep the code in a separate 'code' field.

interface.issue: The cooldown refusal is the bare code 'cooldown_7_days'; any client that does not special-case it shows that string to the buyer.
interface.suggestion: Send the sentence in detail ('You asked about this item recently - you can ask again on <date>') and the code in a 'code' field.

interface.issue: For Local Market the category group is uncapped but is returned with max 40, so the hub can show a subtotal above its own maximum (e.g. 55 of 40).
interface.suggestion: Return max: null (or the raw total) when the seller is scored under local_market, and let the hub drop the 'of 40'.

interface.area: Passkey sign-in (messages shown by ms.js showToast)
interface.issue: Every passkey message says 'Face ID' ('This phone's Face ID is not linked...', 'Face ID did not match'), also on Android phones and laptops that use a fingerprint or PIN.
interface.suggestion: Say 'Face ID or fingerprint' (or return a code and let the app pick the word for the device), matching the button label 'Sign in with Face ID or fingerprint'.

interface.issue: All sign-in refusals are English sentences written on the server and shown verbatim (showToast(d.detail)); with the language layer on, a Zulu or Afrikaans screen gets English error text, and the client has no code to translate from.
interface.suggestion: Add a stable machine code to each refusal (e.g. code_wrong, code_expired_resent, too_many_codes, link_used, link_too_old) alongside detail, and let ms.js / quick.html show their own translated sentence.

interface.issue: The email promises the button works for 7 days, but from day 4 the user is told 'This sign-in link is too old - request a new one' (see the 72-hour bug). The promise and the result disagree.
interface.suggestion: Fix the 72-hour check; until then the email must say 3 days. When a link is refused, send the fresh code automatically (as CODE-RESEND-1 does for codes) instead of a dead end.

interface.issue: After a wrong code the user is not told that only a few tries remain; after 12 wrong codes in an hour the address is blocked for an hour with no warning beforehand.
interface.suggestion: Return tries_left with the 401 and show 'x tries left' in the code box; mention the Sign in button in the email as the way through before the block lands.

interface.issue: When one hour is left the email reads 'In about 1 hours an unanswered introduction takes -5 trust points'; the 72h email has the same '1 hours'.
interface.suggestion: Write 'hour' when hrs_left is 1, or say 'within the hour'.

interface.issue: The refusal ends 'or move to $5 for 50', which does not say what $5 buys or what 50 means.
interface.suggestion: Say 'or move to the Starter plan ($5 a month), which holds 50 regulars' (and 'the Pro plan ($20 a month), which holds 200').

interface.issue: All lifecycle and reminder emails are written in English only, also for sellers who chose another language in the app.
interface.suggestion: Store the seller's chosen language on the account and send these few fixed emails from checked translations in that language.

interface.issue: After the code is accepted the whole page reloads and she lands on Home. A buyer who signed in from an advert to ask for an introduction loses her place and must find the advert again.
interface.suggestion: Remember the screen and advert before the reload (the BACK-RESTORE-1 key already does this for Quick) and reopen it, or sign in without a reload.

interface.issue: The pop-up closes and says 'Redirecting to secure payment…' before the server has answered. If the start fails she sees only 'Payment setup failed - please try again', the server's reason is dropped, and the amount she chose is gone.
interface.suggestion: Keep the pop-up open with a busy button until the answer arrives; on failure show the server's sentence inside the pop-up and keep the amount.

interface.issue: When the webhook credited first, the message is only 'Payment confirmed!' - no amount and no new balance.
interface.suggestion: Re-read the balance and say 'Payment confirmed - your wallet now holds N Tuppence'.

interface.area: Home / Browse while the listing feed fails
interface.issue: A failed listings download is shown only as 'Connecting…' / 'Could not connect' on the small Local Market tile. Browse itself gives no message and no way to try again.
interface.suggestion: Show a clear line with a Retry button in the grid area of Home and Browse when the feed cannot be loaded.

interface.issue: Every signed-in person, buyers included, sees the button 'Seller Hub'; a buyer has no obvious 'my account' door and Sign out sits only inside the Seller Hub.
interface.suggestion: Label it 'My account' (or 'My Hub') and open My Space for people with no listings.

interface.area: Add to home screen on iPhone
interface.issue: The only install help is a 6-second toast shown once; it is marked done even if she never did it, so it never comes back.
interface.suggestion: Show a small card with the Share icon pictured and a 'Not now' button; keep offering it from My Space until the app runs installed.

interface.issue: The agency's import key is printed in full, always visible, with no copy button. It is easy to leak in a screenshot or screen share and awkward to copy on a phone.
interface.suggestion: Mask it by default with 'Show' and 'Copy' buttons.

interface.issue: The action 'Pro seat? · $5' is cryptic, and the plan card says '$5 = Pro AI suite (20)' while the Pro plan itself costs $20 - two prices for 'Pro' with no explanation.
interface.suggestion: Label it 'Invite to Pro seat ($5/month, paid by the agent)' and name the seat differently from the $20 Pro plan.

interface.issue: 'Could not load agency.' is a dead end: no reason (not your agency / not signed in / no connection) and no Retry.
interface.suggestion: Say which it is and add Retry and Sign in buttons.

interface.issue: The Agency card shows 'By application' but its button says 'Upgrade →' and the question that follows says 'Upgrade to Agency ($0/mo)? You'll be redirected to Paystack' - then the server refuses.
interface.suggestion: Give the Agency card an 'Apply' button that opens the application (email link or agency console) and never the payment question.

interface.issue: 'You choose which stay active. The rest rest: hidden, never deleted' reads like a typing mistake, and the whole warning is shown inside a system box as one long paragraph.
interface.suggestion: Reword to 'The others are paused: hidden from buyers, never deleted.' and show it in an in-app sheet with the numbers on separate lines.

interface.issue: Several tappable items are far below a finger-sized target: the 'Demo example' badge (10px text, 2px padding), the 16px Founders spark, the 'AI examples on/off' switch (11px, 4px padding), the 'Show AI examples' text link and the × on the update bar.
interface.suggestion: Give each at least 44px of touch height (padding or an invisible hit area) and make 'Show AI examples' a real button.

interface.issue: 'Please sign in again - your sign-in on this device has lapsed.' appears as a passing toast and leaves her on a screen that keeps failing.
interface.suggestion: Take her to the sign-in screen with her email filled in (as msSessionEnded does), or add a 'Sign in' button to the message.

interface.issue: Times only ever read 'Xm / Xh / Xd ago' - an old request shows '45d ago' and a bad date shows 'Recently'.
interface.suggestion: After 7 days show the date (e.g. '12 Sep').

interface.issue: Any filter, category chip or search that finds nothing says 'No Adventures yet — Operators are being onboarded', which tells the buyer the market is empty when it is only their filter.
interface.suggestion: When a filter, country, chip or search is active say 'Nothing matches these filters' and name them, with 'Clear all filters'; keep the 'operators are being onboarded' text for a truly empty market.

interface.issue: Buttons read 'Request introduction · 1T on acceptance'. A first-time visitor does not know what '1T' is or that asking is free.
interface.suggestion: Write it out: 'Request introduction — free to ask' with a second line '1 Tuppence only if the seller accepts' (lines 3940, 5718, 5848).

interface.issue: Each tag has its own ×, but tapping any one clears every filter for the category.
interface.suggestion: Make each × remove only its own filter, and add one separate 'Clear all' tag at the end of the row.

interface.issue: The panels open with no loading state: the previous list (for example another country's cities) stays tappable until the download ends, and a failed download reads 'No countries available' / 'No cities available'.
interface.suggestion: Clear the list and show 'Loading…' when a panel opens; on failure show 'Could not load — tap to try again' instead of 'none available'.

interface.issue: The browser's location prompt appears as soon as the app loads, before the visitor has done anything or been told why.
interface.suggestion: Ask only when the visitor taps 'Near me' or opens the map, with one line of explanation first ('to show distance to listings').

interface.issue: Price filters and tags are fixed to Rand ('Max R…/hr', 'Min (R)', R0.00) in every market, including New York, London and Sydney.
interface.suggestion: Take the symbol from the active country (the table used for Adventures) for placeholders and tags.

interface.issue: 'Print / save the brief' prints the whole advert page (photos, map, navigation bar), not the brief; the print stylesheet only restyles the brief.
interface.suggestion: Add print rules that hide everything except .trip-essentials (body > * hidden, the panel shown), and put the advert title at the top of the printout.

interface.area: Zoom funnel — failure and typed shortcut
interface.issue: When the question cannot load the sheet says 'showing everything' beside '0 matches', with no retry; typed words the server did not understand (text_leftover) vanish without a word.
interface.suggestion: Add a 'Try again' button and hide the count on error; after a typed shortcut show 'Did not understand: …' from text_leftover.

interface.issue: The block is headed '◆ Universal · applies in every category' and the All sheet says 'The universal layer' — internal design language.
interface.suggestion: Head it 'Seller trust — applies to every category' and the All sheet 'Filter all categories'.

interface.issue: The same button is called 'Filter' on All, 'Filtered Search' on a category and 'Zoom · one question at a time' under the flag.
interface.suggestion: Use one word everywhere ('Filter'), with the count badge.

interface.issue: The bar shows '3 taps · 12 matches' and 'Widen: drop Automatic → 40'; the tap count means nothing to a buyer and the arrow notation is cryptic. The grab handle that hides the sheet is 4px tall.
interface.suggestion: Show '12 matches' only; word the offer 'Remove “Automatic” to see 40'; give the handle a 44px-high tap area.

interface.issue: The heart button is 28×28px and the filter tags and Zoom chips are about 24px high — below the 44px a thumb needs, and the heart sits on a card that opens on a miss-tap.
interface.suggestion: Give the heart and chips a 44px minimum hit area (padding or ::after) without changing their look.

interface.issue: The corner badge reads 'AI EXAMPLE GENERATED LISTING', which is hard to parse at 8.5px in capitals.
interface.suggestion: Use 'AI example — not a real listing' at a readable size (lines 4289, 5483).

interface.issue: A real advert with no price shows the abbreviation 'POA' (the mapper's default text), while the no-price fallbacks say 'Negotiable' on cards and the map and 'POA' in Featured — two terms, one of them jargon.
interface.suggestion: Pick one phrase ('Price on request') and use it for the stored default and all three fallbacks (lines 4819, 5499, 5551).

interface.issue: The sheet is titled 'Accommodation type' while the pill, cards and detail all say 'Stays'.
interface.suggestion: Title it 'Type of stay' / 'Type of experience', read from ADV_SUBCAT_LABELS.

interface.issue: The profile's avatar is the advert's own photo, blurred — it reads as a hidden face although it is a picture of the item.
interface.suggestion: Use the category icon avatar for anonymous sellers and keep the '🔒 Anonymous until introduction' line.

interface.issue: Tapping 'Any' clears the row but 'Any' itself never looks selected, so the row looks unanswered.
interface.suggestion: Highlight 'Any' when nothing else in the row is selected.

interface.issue: Adventure prices use the phone's locale ('R18 500' on a South African phone) while every other price uses commas ('R18,500').
interface.suggestion: Format all amounts through one helper.

interface.issue: A house for sale shows the rental pill '🟢 Available now', because every Property advert gets an availability label.
interface.suggestion: Show the pill only when the advert is a rental.

interface.issue: After confirming a yield check nothing on screen changes for up to 20 seconds; the buyer cannot tell whether her tap worked.
interface.suggestion: Swap the chips for a 'Calculating yield...' line with a spinner while the request runs, exactly as the price check does.

interface.issue: When the buyer is short of Tuppence the yield tool only toasts 'Insufficient Tuppence' - a dead end - while the price check on the same page opens the top-up sheet.
interface.suggestion: Call topUpShort(need-bal) here too so both tools offer the same way forward.

interface.issue: Money decisions use the browser's native confirm() and prompt() boxes ('Enter the expected MONTHLY RENT'), which look like a system warning on a phone, cannot be styled or translated, and some in-app browsers block them.
interface.suggestion: Use the app's own bottom sheet with a labelled numeric input (inputmode=decimal, 'R' prefix) and a clear 'Calculate - 1T only if a yield is produced' button.

interface.issue: A failed check only toasts 'Price check failed' / 'Price check error' - the buyer is not told whether Tuppence was taken or what to do.
interface.suggestion: Say 'We could not finish the price check - nothing was charged. Try again in a minute.' and keep the chips visible.

interface.area: Advert page - 'Several buyers can ask at once' steps
interface.issue: The fifth step repeats the third ('reply within 48 hours') and uses the green tick icon reserved for the accepted step, so the list reads as five steps where there are four.
interface.suggestion: Drop the fifth step and move 'No reply within 48 hours -> seller's Trust Score -5' into the sub-line of step 3.

interface.issue: The queue box promises 'Seller responds to all requests within 48 hours' while the steps above say sellers 'are asked to reply' - an absolute promise the platform cannot keep.
interface.suggestion: Use the same wording as the steps: 'Sellers are asked to reply within 48 hours'.

interface.issue: 'how scores work' is a 9.5px underlined div - far below a 44px tap target and not a button for screen readers.
interface.suggestion: Make it a <button> of at least 12-13px with padding giving a 44px hit area.

interface.issue: When the seller cannot receive introductions the CTA text changes to 'This listing cannot take introductions right now' but stays a tappable button with no reason or alternative.
interface.suggestion: Disable the button (aria-disabled) and add one line under it: why (seller not yet verified) and 'Save it - we will tell you when it opens', wired to the wishlist.

interface.issue: When the AI returns no drafts the seller reads 'No listings could be generated - try clearer photos.' but the server has already taken 2T (it charges even when drafts is empty) and the screen does not say so.
interface.suggestion: Show the balance line and either refund server-side when drafts is empty or say plainly '2T was used'; better, have the server charge only when at least one draft comes back.

interface.issue: The AI-written description is shown but cannot be edited before publishing, while title and price can.
interface.suggestion: Add a textarea bound to _sbBatchDrafts[i].description so the seller can correct the AI's text before it goes live.

interface.issue: Partial success says '(2 failed - try again.)' but the success screen has no retry and does not say which cards failed.
interface.suggestion: List the failed card titles with a 'Retry these' button that re-posts only the failed drafts.

interface.issue: 'Uploading certificate...' then 'Certificate photo saved' / '✓ Certificate photo uploaded' are shown although nothing is sent anywhere.
interface.suggestion: Say 'Added - saved when you tap Save Profile Changes' and only claim 'uploaded' after a server answer.

interface.issue: The section tells her to add credentials in My Space but then shows editable credential rows here too - two places for the same thing, and only one of them counts.
interface.suggestion: Remove the editable rows here and show a read-only list with a 'Manage in My Space' button.

interface.issue: The steps say 'No Tuppence deducted yet' when the request is sent, but the request form says '1 Tuppence is held when you send this' and the wallet drops by 1 the moment it is sent (submitIntro line 7225) - the buyer sees her balance fall right after being told nothing is deducted.
interface.suggestion: Use the hold wording on the advert page too: 'You send an introduction request - 1T is held, and only spent if the seller accepts; released if not.'

interface.issue: The 'what buyers will see' preview always shows '👥 Open to several buyers' and a 'Join queue' button, even for categories buyers see as 'One buyer at a time / Request introduction'.
interface.suggestion: Build the badge and CTA text from catCfg({cat:l.category}).model, as openDetail does.

interface.issue: 'No seller email found - please use the link sent to you by TrustSquare.' is a dead end for a seller who arrived without a link.
interface.suggestion: Offer the in-place 6-digit code box (_msCodeProof) with an email input, or a 'Sign in' button.

interface.issue: 'No draft listings found for this account. Please contact TrustSquare support.' gives no link and no next step.
interface.suggestion: Add 'Create a listing' (goTo sell-flow) and a support link.

interface.issue: The box states 'We have emailed a 6-digit code' although the send is fire-and-forget; when /auth/request-link refuses (rate limit, bad address) she waits for an email that never comes.
interface.suggestion: Await the request and show the server's detail on failure, as _msCodeProof does.

interface.issue: Errors read like developer logs: 'Error (draft 412): HTTP 500: ...' and 'Publish failed - HTTP 403: EULA not accepted'.
interface.suggestion: Map status codes to plain sentences (403 EULA -> 'Please accept the Terms above first'; 5xx -> 'Our server had a problem - nothing was lost, try again') and drop the draft id.

interface.issue: The 'Keep live' button that rescues a fading/hidden advert is styled padding:5px 12px; font-size:11px (about 24 px tall), well under a comfortable phone tap target, on the one action that stops an advert disappearing.
interface.suggestion: Give it at least 40-44 px height (padding:10px 14px; font-size:13px) and place it on its own line under the status chip.

interface.issue: When the seller taps 'Publish now', the toast says '✓ Draft saved — we emailed you a link... It works for a week' while the app goes on to publish, so she is unsure whether her advert is live or a draft.
interface.suggestion: In the publish-now path say nothing at this point (the publish confirmation follows); keep the draft/email toast for 'Finish later' only.

interface.issue: 'Pending' and 'Queued' both count waiting introduction requests (Queued is the same count minus Property), so a first-time seller sees two numbers for one thing.
interface.suggestion: Show one 'Requests waiting' counter, or rename to 'Requests waiting' and 'In queue (non-property)' with a one-line tooltip.

interface.issue: If the server answers with a non-JSON error page (502/504), r.json() throws and the toast reads 'Could not change it: Unexpected token <...', a developer message.
interface.suggestion: Use r.json().catch(()=>({})) as msKeepLive does, so the toast falls back to 'HTTP 502 — try again in a minute'.

interface.area: Path B - Save draft and exit
interface.issue: A native confirm() with 'OK = save draft and exit . Cancel = keep editing' is the only explanation that the draft is not live; on phones OK/Cancel do not match the sentence and the dialog is not translated.
interface.suggestion: Use the app's bottom sheet with two labelled buttons: 'Save draft — not visible to buyers yet' and 'Keep editing'.

interface.issue: Tips show raw slot keys ('Missing photo: bathroom main', 'street view') and flag the street view the prompt calls optional; Property tips speak of 'SA tenants' and 'rental decider' on For Sale listings.
interface.suggestion: Use sbSlotLabel(s.key), skip slots whose prompt says Optional, and word the security/backup tips for buyers when listing_type is For Sale.

interface.issue: On a 401/429/500 the code still shows the 'Market note' panel and writes an empty string into it, leaving an empty labelled box.
interface.suggestion: Check res.ok; on failure hide #go-market-note (as the catch already does) or say 'Market note unavailable right now'.

interface.issue: Each refused photo raises its own toast inside the upload loop, so with several failures only the last one stays visible and the seller does not know how many photos were dropped (sbDoPublish at 11604 already summarises).
interface.suggestion: Collect failures and show one summary after the loop, e.g. '2 of 5 photos were not added: photo 2 (HEIC), photo 4 (too large) — add them from Edit listing'.

interface.issue: Add Photo saves immediately ('added and saved') but Replace, Remove, Move and Make cover only change the screen and ask the seller to 'tap Save Changes'; two behaviours on one row of buttons means sellers leave thinking a replaced/removed photo is saved.
interface.suggestion: Make every photo action auto-save the same way elAddPhoto does (one PUT of photo_urls/thumb_url), or make Add also wait for Save Changes, and keep one toast wording for all.

interface.issue: 'Ask AI Coach' gives no hint that every use after the first deducts 1T (server _deduct_tuppence); the cost is only revealed afterwards as 'Tuppence remaining', while the neighbouring Market report button shows '5T'. The button text also changes from '💬 Ask AI Coach' to 'Ask AI' after the first run.
interface.suggestion: Label it 'Ask AI Coach · 1T (first one free)' or confirm before charging, and restore the original label text in the finally block.

interface.issue: Server refusals are printed raw: 'Error: permanent_lm_ban', 'Error: cooling_off_until_2026-10-20', and a full plan gives 'Error: Listing slot limit reached...' with no button to choose a plan (the hub opens openPlans for the same 402).
interface.suggestion: Map the codes to plain sentences ('Your Local Market access is paused until 20 Oct'), and on 402 call openPlans('sell', true) as dashPublish does.

interface.issue: 'Generating Trust Score action plan...' appears on every Edit open and then silently disappears (see bug), so the seller sees a promise that is never kept.
interface.suggestion: Show the plan (escaped) or remove the placeholder; if the AI fails, say 'The coach is unavailable right now' instead of hiding the box.

interface.issue: '+ Add prospect' shows a developer toast 'Add prospect — BEA coming' to whoever reaches the screen.
interface.suggestion: Hide the button until the feature exists, or word the toast for a person ('Adding prospects is coming soon').

interface.issue: Delete uses two native confirm() boxes and, for a device with no stored email, a native prompt() asking the seller to type her email - jarring on phones and the typed email is ignored by the server anyway (session-bound).
interface.suggestion: Use one in-app confirmation sheet naming the listing, and drop the email prompt (send the session request without it).

interface.issue: The hub tells the seller to tick "Visible after intro" but the checkbox is labelled 'Visible to buyer after introduction'; an upload error only says 'HTTP 413/415' etc.
interface.suggestion: Use the same words in both places and show the server's detail (file too big / type not allowed) on failure.

interface.area: Edit listing - Rewrite / Why No Introductions?
interface.issue: The panel says 'Our AI is rewriting your listing...' and the button 'Rewriting...' BEFORE the 1T confirm() appears, so the seller is asked to agree to a charge for something the screen claims is already running.
interface.suggestion: Ask the confirm first, then set the busy text; use an in-app sheet stating '1T' rather than a native confirm.

interface.issue: The bar always paints a grey 40% 'Base score' segment, so a seller whose penalties pulled her to e.g. 31 sees a bar that looks like 40+, contradicting the '31 / 100' beside it.
interface.suggestion: Draw the base segment as min(score, 40)% and colour the shortfall red with a one-line reason ('-9 for unanswered requests').

interface.issue: Accepting adds a wallet row whose value is the word 'accepted' in red (addTx pos=false), which reads like a charge or an error in the Tuppence history.
interface.suggestion: Show a neutral grey status ('Accepted') or no value, and keep red for actual deductions.

interface.issue: Chips show internal keys and codes: 'LocalMarket' as one word and an unexplained 'P2' tag on Adventures/Collectors.
interface.suggestion: Use display labels ('Local Market') and replace 'P2' with plain words such as 'New' or drop it.

interface.issue: A signed-in seller is asked to 'Enter your email to use the AI Coach' and the Publish screen asks 'Your email (for claim link)'; the server only accepts the signed-in address, so a different one gets a refusal.
interface.suggestion: Show 'Coaching as <signed-in account>' read-only; if not signed in, show a 'Sign in to use the AI Coach' button that opens the sign-in screen.

interface.issue: 'Delete' removes a draft with all its photos instantly, no confirmation or undo.
interface.suggestion: Ask 'Delete this draft and its photos?' or show an Undo toast for 5 seconds.

interface.issue: Slots filled by the AI report (blob photos) show only an emoji but say 'Tap to retake', so the seller cannot see which photo is there.
interface.suggestion: Render the real thumbnail for every stored photo (blob or dataUrl).

interface.issue: 'Compressing large photo…' has no failure message; an unreadable photo (e.g. HEIC on some browsers) gives no feedback.
interface.suggestion: Catch decode failures and say 'This photo format can't be used — please choose a JPG or PNG'.

interface.issue: After any coach error the button always resets to '✨ Get AI Suggestions' even when suggestions already exist (normally 'Re-run AI Coach').
interface.suggestion: Reset to the label aaRenderAIPanel would show (hasRun ? 'Re-run AI Coach' : 'Get AI Suggestions').

interface.issue: 'Email not recognised — use your onboarding email' uses jargon ('onboarding email') and the server never sends 404 here.
interface.suggestion: Remove the dead branch; for the server's 401 say 'Sign in with the email you registered with'.

interface.issue: All Buzz switches are plain <div>s with onclick: no role, no keyboard focus, no aria-checked, so screen-reader and keyboard users cannot operate them.
interface.suggestion: Render them as <button role="switch" aria-checked="true|false"> with an aria-label naming the person/phone.

interface.issue: 'Close Buzz with <name>' acts on the first tap (closes both ways and notifies the other person) with no confirmation; the link is small text.
interface.suggestion: Ask 'Close Buzz with <name>? They will be told.' and make the control a proper button with a 44px target.

interface.issue: 'Couldn't load feed.' is a dead end with no retry.
interface.suggestion: Add a 'Try again' button that calls wlLoadFeed().

interface.issue: Uses native prompt('Email for Paystack receipt:') and alert('Could not start subscription') — off-style, untranslated, and asks a signed-in user for an email again.
interface.suggestion: Use the signed-in email and an in-app sheet/toast for errors.

interface.issue: Any failure (including notifications blocked in the browser) says 'Please try again later', which will never work when permission is denied.
interface.suggestion: When permission is 'denied', say 'Notifications are blocked for TrustSquare — allow them in your browser settings, then try again'.

interface.issue: 'Could not load Local Market.' gives no retry.
interface.suggestion: Add a 'Try again' button that calls lmLoadGrid().

interface.issue: 'Negotiable — discuss with seller' although the buyer cannot contact the seller before an accepted introduction.
interface.suggestion: Say 'Price on request — ask in your introduction'.

interface.issue: Two steps repeat the same 48-hour message ('Sellers are asked to reply within 48 hours' and 'The seller is expected to reply within 48 hours').
interface.suggestion: Merge into one step and keep the five-step list to four.

interface.issue: 'Seller-pays model — no Tuppence deducted from you' uses business jargon.
interface.suggestion: Say 'Free for you — you pay nothing to ask'.

interface.issue: The profile promises 'Name, contact details and exact location are only revealed after both parties accept', while the detail page says emails stay private and you talk by replying to an email; the two screens describe different reveals.
interface.suggestion: Use one sentence on both screens describing exactly what the buyer gets after acceptance.

interface.area: My Space > Open actions / Intros (Accept, Decline)
interface.issue: Any server refusal (already answered, expired, 409/410) is shown as 'That did not go through — please sign in and try again', which sends a signed-in seller down the wrong path.
interface.suggestion: Have _introAnswerPut return the server detail on !res.ok and toast it; keep the sign-in wording only for 401.

interface.issue: The remove cross is a bare <span> with onclick: not focusable, no button role, and a small tap target on a phone.
interface.suggestion: Render it as <button type="button" aria-label="Remove this photo"> with at least a 32x32px hit area.

interface.issue: When /intros fails or the user is not signed in, the RECEIVED box says 'Introductions will appear here once you request one' — sent-side wording, and a network/401 failure looks identical to 'nothing yet'.
interface.suggestion: Received: 'Requests from buyers will appear here'. On a fetch failure show 'Could not load your introductions — pull down to retry' (and a Sign in button on 401).

interface.issue: The same card tells a Property seller she has '48 hours' to respond, and that the listing reopens 'after 4 days with no reply'; a first-time seller cannot tell which deadline matters.
interface.suggestion: State both in one line: 'Reply within 48 hours to protect your Trust Score; if you never reply, the request closes after 4 days and the listing reopens.'

interface.issue: Signed-out users see 'Sign in to view your transaction history' with no way to sign in from there (dead end).
interface.suggestion: Add a 'Sign in' button in _txEmptyState for that case that calls goTo('signin').

interface.issue: Property ranges read 'R450k–R3500k'; millions are shown as thousands of k, and the symbol is always R.
interface.suggestion: Format >= 1,000,000 as 'R3.5m' and use the active country's currency symbol.

interface.issue: 'Remove' deletes a brief and its shortlist instantly, with no confirmation and no feedback.
interface.suggestion: Confirm ('Remove this brief? Squire stops watching for it.') and toast 'Brief removed' only after r.ok.

interface.issue: The optional line to the seller is asked in a native window.prompt, which is cramped on phones, cannot be translated by the page translator, and the text kept on a cap hit (sessionStorage sq_draft_*) is never offered back.
interface.suggestion: Use an inline textarea under the shortlist row and pre-fill it from sq_draft_<listing> after a top-up.

interface.issue: Heading 'The two things you forgot:' reads as a reproach and assumes exactly two questions.
interface.suggestion: 'Sellers usually ask:' followed by however many questions the brief has.

interface.issue: The rejection text inserts the internal category key, so a Local Market seller reads 'This doesn't look like a local_market photo' and an Adventures seller 'a Adventures photo'; the multi-photo toast at 22161 has the same problem.
interface.suggestion: Use sfCatName(sfState.cat) (or the flow's label) and a neutral sentence: "This photo doesn't look like it belongs in Local Market".

interface.area: Sell flow - Boost your sale? (agent introduction)
interface.issue: The toast promises 'Agent X will see your trust score and property summary', but the introduction is made before the listing exists and sfAgentIntro sends no listing_id, so the agent's lead card shows only 'Property lead' and 'Private seller from the sell flow — <suburb>'.
interface.suggestion: Queue the chosen agent and send the introduction with listing_id once goHandoff returns an id, or change the copy to 'Agent X will see your trust score and suburb — your listing follows once it is published'.

interface.issue: 'Accept lead — 1T' spends Tuppence in one tap with no confirmation and no balance shown; a 402 only toasts the server text with no way to top up.
interface.suggestion: Confirm in a small sheet ('Accept this lead for 1 Tuppence? Balance: N T'), and on 402 show a 'Top up' button that opens the Tuppence screen.

interface.issue: 'Sign in first — your agent profile hangs off your seller account.' (and 'Sign in first.' on the leads tab, 22893) is plain text with no button: a dead end.
interface.suggestion: Add a 'Sign in with a 6-digit code' button that calls goTo('signin') (or reuse the sell flow's inline code box).

interface.issue: The red x that removes an extra photo is an 18×18 px span on a 56×42 px thumbnail: too small to hit reliably on a phone, and it has no aria-label.
interface.suggestion: Make the hit area at least 32×32 px (padding or a transparent ::before), use a <button aria-label="Remove photo">.

interface.issue: Long warnings (photos removed as off-category, agent introduction terms, draft saved with email) go through sfToast(t), which drops the duration argument (ms.js 20858), so they vanish after the default 2.6 s before a phone user can read them.
interface.suggestion: Make sfToast(t, ms) pass ms to showToast and give warnings and multi-clause messages 6000 ms.

interface.area: Sell flow / agent panels - empty vs failed
interface.issue: When /agents/nearby or /agents/pitch fails (network), the screen says 'No listed agents near X yet' — the same words as a genuinely empty city (also 23234, 23346, 23381).
interface.suggestion: Track the fetch outcome and show 'Could not load agents — check your connection' with a Try again link when the request failed.

interface.issue: The back link always reads '‹ Back to Services' and goes to Browse, even when the directory was opened from the Property or Cars banner.
interface.suggestion: Label it from where it was opened ('‹ Back to Property' / 'Cars') or simply '‹ Back', and return to that category's browse view.

interface.issue: The RANK ⓘ control is a <div onclick>: not focusable, no role, no accessible name for screen readers (also 23248).
interface.suggestion: Use <button type="button" aria-label="How scores and ranking work">.

interface.area: My Space - Home Affairs ID check
interface.issue: After a refusal or error the button is reset to 'Verify my ID · 1T' even when the lane price (lane.price_t) is different from 1.
interface.suggestion: Keep the rendered label (btn.dataset.label) and restore it instead of a hard-coded '1T'.

interface.issue: Local Market and car-hire listings have no legal step, yet the header still counts 'Step n of 6', so the last step the seller sees is 'Step 5 of 6'.
interface.suggestion: Compute the total from the flow (6 when sfLegalCard() exists, else 5).

interface.issue: Escape or a tap on the dark backdrop closes the sheet and throws away a half-typed report and pasted screenshot without asking.
interface.suggestion: If the text box or screenshot is filled, ask 'Discard this report?' before closing, or keep the draft in memory and restore it on the next open.

interface.issue: The card says 'MarketSquare is not a travel agency' while every other surface is branded TrustSquare.
interface.suggestion: Change the sentence to 'TrustSquare is not a travel agency…'.

interface.issue: Saving a profile always answers profile_status 'draft' and 'Upload FFC + PPRA under Trust Score to unlock go-live', even for a car dealer, tour agent or tutor, and even when the profile is already live.
interface.suggestion: Return the real profile_status and build the note from the vertical's own gate_label (e.g. 'Upload your MIRA dealer registration...').

interface.issue: The confirmation says the agent 'sees your trust score and property summary', but the sell flow (ms.js 22684) never sends listing_id, so the agent sees only 'Property lead'; holiday searchers get the same property wording.
interface.suggestion: Send the draft/listing id from the sell flow, and word the note by vertical ('...and your request' when no listing is attached).

interface.issue: The solid button text (#04140e) on the category colour is 3.08:1 on Cars (#5B4BD6) and 3.41:1 on Services (#B4441F) — below the 4.5:1 needed for 16px text — so 'Sell a car', 'Next — 3 days' and 'Save my listing' are hard to read in sunlight; the same colours used as text (.todo b points, .coach .big span, .sc u.avail) are 2.8-3.4:1.
interface.suggestion: Give Cars and Services a lighter button shade (e.g. Cars #7B6DF0, Services #D2603A) or white button text for those two, and use var(--bright) instead of var(--c) for small coloured text.

interface.area: Week step, score panel, Buzz screen
interface.issue: Much of the small print is under 12px: the day cell 'yes' 9.5px, score labels and 'available' 10px, Buzz badges 9px, Buzz fact labels 9.5px, section labels 10.5px, trail chips 11px — unreadable on a cheap phone held at arm's length.
interface.suggestion: Set a 12px floor for all text (.wd i, .sc i, .sc u, .bzsec h5, .bzsec h5 u, .bzfacts dt, .todolab, .trail span, .msline i, .onphone) and drop letter-spaced capitals for those labels.

interface.issue: Tap targets are under 44px: back/start-again circles are 40x40, the category arrows are about 32x41, the Buzz permission switches 46x27, the WIP close 'x' about 20x24, the Buzz direction buttons about 37px tall, and the 'Change this in TrustSquare' link is 11px text.
interface.suggestion: Make .ic 44x44, give .arw min-width/min-height 44px, wrap .sw in a 44px-tall hit area (padding on the .perm row), and give .qs-x / .whoch at least 44x44 padding.

interface.issue: Trail chips are white-space:nowrap with no max-width, so a typed answer (up to 80 chars) or a multi-area list ('Pretoria East, Centurion, Mamelodi, Menlyn') is wider than a 320-360px screen and is clipped by #app's overflow:hidden.
interface.suggestion: Add max-width:100%;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis to .trail span (and a title with the full text), or let the chip wrap.

interface.issue: Each tap swaps #screen's innerHTML but the question is a plain <div class="q">, there is no live region and focus stays on the removed button, so TalkBack/VoiceOver users are not told a new question appeared; the progress dots (#steps) have no text either.
interface.suggestion: Render the question as <h1 class="q" tabindex="-1"> and focus it after each draw, give #screen role="main", and set #steps aria-label='Question 2 of 5' (role="img") in paintSteps.

interface.issue: The text box has only a placeholder — no label — so a screen reader announces it as an unnamed edit field, and the placeholder disappears as soon as she starts typing.
interface.suggestion: Add aria-label set to the question (s.q, translated) on #frtxt, and keep the hint visible above the box.

interface.issue: With no area picked the Next button only looks faded (opacity .55) — it is still enabled, so tapping it does nothing and says nothing.
interface.suggestion: Set nb.disabled=true (and aria-disabled) until an area is picked, or on tap flash the line 'Tap every area you work in, then Next'.

interface.issue: Every Quick draft's top 'best next step' is 'Add your own photos +40', but Quick has no way to add a photo, so a first-time seller hunts for a button that is not there; with 1 photo needed it also reads 'Add 1 more photos'.
interface.suggestion: Word it as an app step: 'Add your photos in TrustSquare after you save (+40)', with the singular 'photo' when one is needed.

interface.issue: 'Confirm your number' is a tick-box task, but Quick never asks for or shows a phone number, so the seller cannot do it; ticking either item changes nothing.
interface.suggestion: Remove 'Confirm your number' from Quick (or replace with 'Check your email address' showing the address), and make 'Check the wording' scroll to the advert text.

interface.issue: The Ranking score shows a decimal (e.g. 47.5) beside whole-number Trust and Listing scores, and 'Buyers see the star alone' / '+25 available' are unexplained jargon to a first-time seller.
interface.suggestion: Round Ranking to a whole number and replace the lines with plain sentences: 'Buyers only see your trust stars', '25 more points you can still earn'.

interface.area: Draft title (Property, Cars, Tutors, Collectors, trips)
interface.issue: The advert title is just the first two answers — 'House — To sell', 'Bakkie — Toyota', 'Maths — High school', 'Safari — 2–3 nights' — with no area, beds or year, which is the line buyers scan in the grid.
interface.suggestion: Build the title per category from the key answers, e.g. '3-bed house for sale — Menlyn', 'Toyota bakkie, 2015–2019 — Centurion', 'Maths tutor, high school — Pretoria East'.

interface.issue: The ↻ button discards the advert in progress with one tap and no question; the only way back is a small 'Carry on' chip on the door that a first-time user may not notice.
interface.suggestion: Ask 'Start a new advert? Your answers so far are kept for 6 hours' with Carry on / Start new, or show the Carry on card prominently at the top of the door.

interface.issue: '12 taps to get here' under the save button is a design boast, not information the seller can use, and takes the slot where the save consequence should be.
interface.suggestion: Drop the tap count from the seller's view (keep it in qTrack meta) and use the line for what the tap does.

interface.issue: The Buzz page is long (four fact rows, two switches, three notes, a warning) for an example of one button, and the example names stay as 'Thandi Mokoena' even when Quick knows the seller's own name.
interface.suggestion: Lead with the live-looking push example and one sentence, fold the rules into a 'How it works' details element, and use QUICK.name for party A when it is known.

interface.issue: The aria-labels 'Back', 'Start again', 'Previous category', 'Next category', 'How it works' and the iframe title are fixed English, so an isiZulu or Sesotho screen-reader user hears English control names.
interface.suggestion: Set these aria-labels/titles through qTr() in setNav/drawDoor/qHelpButton and refresh them in qSetLang.

interface.issue: .bzfacts dt is white-space:nowrap in an auto-width grid column, so a long translated label ('How you met', 'Who paid') widens the label column and squeezes the answers into a narrow strip at 360px.
interface.suggestion: Allow the dt to wrap (white-space:normal) and cap the label column, e.g. grid-template-columns:minmax(0,38%) 1fr.

interface.issue: Tapping 'Save my listing' with no or a malformed email only turns the box border red and focuses it; there is no sentence saying what is wrong, and the red border stays after she fixes it.
interface.suggestion: Write qTr('Type your email so introductions can reach you.') into #pubhint and reset the border on input.

interface.issue: The top-bar language button shows the code (EN, ZU, NSO); LANG-NAMES-1 already found 'NSO meant nothing to a Sepedi reader', but the bar still shows it on every screen.
interface.suggestion: Show the language's own short name (English, isiZulu, Sepedi...) or the globe plus a 2-letter label users know; keep the code only in the menu.

interface.issue: Coming-soon countries (Germany, Botswana, Mozambique) are listed exactly like open ones.
interface.suggestion: Mark them 'coming soon' and show the qComingSoon screen on tap instead of starting a flow that cannot be saved.

interface.issue: After 'List something else' with the email she typed a minute ago, the server treats her as an existing account and the arrival says 'You already have a TrustSquare account. We emailed you a link', which reads as an error about someone else's account.
interface.suggestion: When QUICK.quickMail is set and r.verify comes back, say 'Saved. To keep your listings together, open the link we just emailed you.'

interface.issue: The door's 'Share' link does not say what is shared (it passes Quick on, not her listing); the meaning is only in the aria-label.
interface.suggestion: Label it 'Pass Quick on' (already translated) next to the icon.

interface.issue: The unfinished-work chip shows only a pencil and 'Carry on ›'; what it carries on (listing or search, which category) is only in a title tooltip phones never show. The × beside it (button.qs-x: 16px font, 0 2px padding, about 12x20px) deletes the saved answers at once with no undo, so a slightly-off tap on 'Carry on' can wipe her advert.
interface.suggestion: Write it out: 'Carry on with your Cars listing ›' / 'Carry on with your search ›'; give the × a 40px target with space from the link, and offer 'Undo' for a few seconds after it.

interface.area: Phone Back with the How guide open
interface.issue: The phone's Back gesture calls $('back').onclick() directly, which does not fire the click listener that closes the How guide, so the form steps back underneath while the guide stays on screen.
interface.suggestion: In the popstate handler, close the guide first when #qhov is visible (call qHelpClose and stop), or dispatch a real click: $('back').click().

interface.issue: Basis chips, 'Plus parts and materials', the role finish chips and the 'Languages I work in' chips toggle visually but have no aria-pressed, so a screen reader cannot tell which is chosen.
interface.suggestion: Set aria-pressed on every toggle chip in paint()/onclick (drawRate, svcFinish, svcFinish speaks, svcFinishSpeaksOnly).

interface.issue: The amount box has no currency shown, so a seller outside South Africa (or a first-time user) is not sure whether to type 'R', '$' or just digits.
interface.suggestion: Show the currency symbol as a fixed prefix in the box (MINW[cc].s / QP.cur) and use the placeholder 'e.g. 300'.

interface.issue: Phone-code and invite errors print the server's English detail (with '--' dashes) inside a translated screen; a 422 validation error would print '[object Object]'.
interface.suggestion: Map status codes to Quick's own translated sentences, as qSaveFail does for saves.

interface.issue: The arrival screen stacks up to seven actions (See my listing, WhatsApp, key box, Add to home screen, email line, List something else, Pass Quick on) on a small phone; the one that matters most is hard to see.
interface.suggestion: Keep the main button plus WhatsApp; fold 'Add to home screen' and 'Pass Quick on' under one 'More' row.

interface.issue: Changing language while on the reference preview (atSub='vouch') throws her back to the draft, because qNextSetLang only checks atBuzz.
interface.suggestion: Guard with !atSub too, or redraw the current sub-screen (drawVouch(stage)).
